launches.title: Tire Swing - AI Compliance for Affordable Housing
launches.tagline: The AI platform for Affordable Housing operators to review and qualify applicants and residents
launches.body:
Hi! We are Lucas and Paul, cofounders of Tire Swing: the AI compliance platform for Affordable Housing.

<https://youtu.be/x4qyhXXz38I>

## **The Problem**

Every Affordable Housing move-in and recertification requires applicant income verification and a strict eligibility review. In addition to the high labor costs and regulatory burden, delays in reviewing applications and thoroughly screening applicants can cause weeks of lost rental revenue.

Lost revenue on a single move-in can accumulate to thousands of dollars, and penalties for non-compliance can cost millions in credit recaptures and fines.

## **The Solution**

Tire Swing uses AI to bring compliance expertise to the point of leasing. It turns weeks of reviews and approvals into a minutes-long process. The platform:

* **Reviews evidence as it is collected.** Tire Swing processes documentation in minutes, allowing problems to be addressed before the applicant leaves the office.
* **Performs the eligibility analysis.** It calculates household income, applies all applicable property, state, and program eligibility rules, and links every finding to its supporting evidence.
* **Automates certification compliance.** Tire Swing flags missing, inconsistent, or incorrect information with steps to resolve the problem from a library of thousands of deterministic and AI driven compliance checks.

**Tire Swing means faster move-ins and recertifications, reduced consulting budget, and more consistent, audit-ready files.** 

## **Looking ahead**

We believe Affordable Housing is the first application of a much larger needs-based eligibility opportunity. Federal, state, and local governments distribute more than $1.5 trillion annually through needs-based programs including Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, utility assistance, and tax credits.

These programs share a common underlying workflow: collect documents, convert them into structured facts, apply eligibility rules, and resolve missing or contradictory information.  The administration costs for these services are approximately $20B annually.

## **The Team**

Tire Swing is founded by Paul and Lucas, college friends and Princeton computer science graduates. Prior to founding Tire Swing, Lucas worked as a software engineer at Instacart and Capital One, and Paul worked as a cybersecurity consultant at Stroz Friedberg.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108324&key=user_uploads/990814/102ac484-df2c-4314-a766-c778a91c6b50)


## **The Ask**

We would appreciate introductions to Affordable Housing property managers, developers, public housing authorities, and state housing agencies.

Please feel free to reach out at [**paul@gettireswing.com**](mailto:paul@gettireswing.com).

# **TL;DR**

Wingman Law is an AI-native personal injury law firm. Instead of handing your case to a pyramid of case managers, **our attorneys lead a team of AI agents** that keep it moving. We only get paid when our clients win.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125445&key=user_uploads/1045396/2a542a65-24be-444d-8bc6-7ae9834321e1)

### **The Problem**

Personal injury is bottlenecked by humans. Every case depends on case managers chasing clients, providers, and insurers, so firms can only grow by hiring more of them. For clients, that means long stretches without updates and slow progress toward a payout.

### **Our solution**

Wingman Law is an AI-native personal injury law firm: attorneys direct AI agents instead of case managers. Cases move faster and clients gets more attorney attention.\
\
We built our own operating platform for the firm, where attorneys can direct AI agents in plain English. Our platform coordinates AI agents to gather the evidence, work across cases in parallel, and prepare the documents and communications needed for the next step. Because calls, texts, emails, and case files are connected, the agents can carry that work from the underlying evidence through to an action ready for attorney approval.

### **Why we built this**

**Sunwoo** has a JD from Harvard Law as well as an MS and BA from Stanford. She worked in world class litigation teams at Orrick and Fish & Richardson, where the smallest cases were worth $50M, but found herself wanting to help injured individuals where the impact felt more tangible.

During law school, she built and sold $350K worth of legal tech. So much of her energy went into integrating with legacy systems. Now she puts that energy into building agents that help clients win. 

**Nick** is a licensed attorney who has worked on more than 700 Bay Area personal injury cases, both at a plaintiff’s firm and on the insurance defense side (Habbas Law and Kern, Segal & Murray).

He was also employee #2 at Strongsuit building litigation platform for law firms. That experience made him realize how much faster and better he could build as a technical lawyer if he were building for his own firm. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125445&key=user_uploads/1045396/77c8aa6f-3f33-4c25-931d-bc290d7ba0e2)

### **Our Ask**

Attorney solicitation rules limit how we can approach potential clients (which is why we got this Tesla wrapped!), so word-of-mouth introductions are especially valuable.

If you, a friend, a family member, or a coworker is looking for legal help after an injury in California, we’d love to help. We work on contingency so there is no out of pocket cost to our clients. We handle cases involving car accidents, bike and scooter crashes, and premises liability like slip and fall. Please shoot me an email at [sunwoo@wingmanlaw.com](mailto:sunwoo@wingmanlaw.com).

Hey YC! I'm [Issa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/issanassar), founder of [Databuddy](https://www.databuddy.cc).

**TL;DR:** Databuddy is product analytics for founders without a data team. One script gives you visitors, signups, funnels, revenue, errors and Web Vitals in one dashboard. Databunny, the built-in AI analyst, answers questions about your numbers and shows you the query behind every answer.

Launch video: <https://x.com/izadoesdev/status/2108216140610543810>

## The problem

Collecting data is easy. Understanding it isn't.

A typical early-stage stack looks like this: Google Analytics for traffic, PostHog or Mixpanel for product events, Sentry for errors, Stripe for revenue. Every tool answers part of the question, none of them talk to each other, and turning it into an actual answer ("did that launch bring paying users?") needs someone who can write SQL. Most startups don't have that person, so they collect everything and decide on gut feel.

## What Databuddy does

* **One cookieless script.** Real-time visitors, sessions, custom events, funnels, goals, error tracking, Web Vitals and feature flags, all from the same install.
* **Revenue next to traffic.** See which referrers, pages and campaigns brought paying customers, not just visits.
* **Databunny, the AI analyst.** Ask in plain words and open the query it ran before you trust the number. On Business and Scale it checks your metrics every day or week and posts real changes to Slack with the next step.
* **Works from your editor.** Sign in from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP client, and your agent can pull traffic, read investigations, and set up funnels, goals and flags for you.

## Traction

* #5 Product of the Day on Product Hunt
* Our YC announcement on X passed 800K views

_"Actually game changing going from Framer analytics to @trydatabuddy. We're such happy customers."_ John Yeo, Co-Founder, Autumn

_"I've tried a BUNCH of analytics providers. Databuddy does things I didn't even know are possible. So far 10x better than anything I personally have ever tried."_ Michael Chomsky, Context.dev

## Pricing

Free up to 10,000 events a month, then from $9.99 a month. No credit card, no sales call.

## About me

I'm a solo founder. I started building Databuddy in Palestine and I'm now building it full time in YC F26.

## Our ask

* **Try it:** [databuddy.cc](http://databuddy.cc) is free to start.

We're[ Sai Vamshi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sai-vamshi-batchu-129256194/) and[ Aditya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aditya-bommakanti-6b035321a/), IIT engineers from high-frequency trading, building[ GodHands](https://godhands.ai).

At our previous company, a key person left. Nobody knew how they did their work. The team kept calling them long after they'd gone, and it took months to get back on track.

Every company has people like that. None of what they know is written down.

They know how to handle the refund that doesn't fit the policy, which customer gets a call instead of an email, and which spreadsheet is actually right.

launches.tagline: Data and models of the distribution grid
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Ryhla gets projects connected to the power grid. Our proprietary models replicate the distribution grid, and we use them to take projects through interconnection end to end. Developers typically get 20 to 40% of applications approved. Our models got 91%.** 

<https://youtu.be/e-qtjw-T0M0>

**The problem**\
Today, a developer files an interconnection request (the application to plug a project into the grid) and waits months for the utility’s answer. Too often it’s a rejection or a massive upgrade bill, after the time and money are already spent. Unlike transmission, where queues and capacity maps are often public, the distribution grid is a black box.

**What we do**\
We built proprietary models that replicate how the distribution grid behaves and how utilities decide what gets connected. Today, developers use them to drop dead projects early and shape the ones that can work into applications that get approved. For each project, we know how much capacity is available (for load and injection), how to size it, how long it will take and what the upgrade would cost. Then we handle the interconnection end to end.

**Results**

* We’re live with one of the biggest solar developers in the Midwest.
* 91% of the sites our models said yes to were approved by the utility (2025 distribution-level applications).
* We saved a battery developer about $160k in fees by ruling out 8 of their 10 planned projects in a few days.

**Why now**

* **Grid demand is exploding.** Data centers, EV chargers, batteries, new factories: everything is plugging into the grid at once, and utilities can’t keep up with the requests.
* **Projects are moving to the distribution grid.** Transmission queues take years, so more and more projects connect at the distribution level instead, where public data is often missing.
* **The opportunity is massive.** More power capacity is waiting in line to connect than all the power plants in the US combined, and every one of those projects has to go through interconnection.

**Who we are**\
We're Sara (CEO) and Yassine (CTO). We've been best friends since middle school and both grew up in Morocco, a country betting big on solar, which is how we got hooked on energy. We studied electrical and computational engineering at École Polytechnique, then did research on grid intelligence models at Stanford, which became Ryhla. We first deployed our models with utilities, so we know how interconnection works on their side. 

**Asks**

* Intros to developers building on the distribution grid: solar, storage, community solar, C&I, EV charging, small data centers. 
* **Have a project that needs a grid connection? Send it to founders@ryhla.ai**

name: Nxtcure Labs
long_description:
NxtCure Labs is an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster. We are reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.

About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century.

NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope.

Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them.

In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We’re building that future.
one_liner: Engineering the future of Cancer Drug Discovery

name: Rodeo Robotics
long_description:
Rodeo builds a robotic technician that automates maintenance so fleets can get vehicles back on the road sooner. Initial deployments focus on oil changes at centralized depots, where routine maintenance competes for scarce technician time.

Cofounders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they worked with OEMs like Toyota and General Motors to bring software and autonomy to vehicles. They saw firsthand how much manual work it takes to keep vehicle fleets running, and learned how to make autonomy reliable through structured testing, real-world data, and human intervention.

They’re now applying their experience to the roughly $600B annual US vehicle maintenance market. The average US vehicle is older than ever, driving up maintenance demand at a time when shops already struggle to hire and retain technicians. That gap leaves fleets facing costly downtime and preventable breakdowns.

Despite this need, vehicle maintenance has resisted traditional automation. Service information is fragmented and unreliable, and vehicle hardware varies significantly between makes and models. Rodeo builds on advances in robotic foundation models to learn maintenance skills that transfer across vehicles.

Rodeo pairs robots with human technicians who ensure each job is completed correctly, handling work the robots can’t yet perform autonomously. These deployments generate training data for Rodeo’s models through both teleoperation and hand tools augmented to record how technicians work. This lets Rodeo earn revenue while collecting the data needed to automate more of each job and improve margins.
one_liner: Robots for vehicle maintenance.

launches.body:
## **Surgery is complex. Finding answers shouldn't be.**

Modern surgery relies on complex implants and instruments. But manufacturer instructions, surgical techniques and hospital protocols are scattered across PDFs, portals and disconnected systems.

For a single procedure, surgeons may need to navigate multiple sources just to find the relevant information.

The knowledge exists. It just has no common home.

## How CONUS works

CONUS brings medical device knowledge into one place.

Surgeons can select a procedure, see which implant systems are available at their hospital and access manufacturer instructions, surgical techniques and hospital protocols.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=121625&key=user_uploads/3347806/fc56290e-fa4c-43ed-9c68-91b22dda1023)

**For medical device manufacturers,** CONUS provides a shared platform to make their product knowledge accessible to surgeons and equip field teams with structured information across their portfolios.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=121625&key=user_uploads/3347806/cfed0a0f-70fa-4f07-9402-4f8c90c298c8)

**CONUS Intelligence** makes this structured knowledge accessible through AI, providing answers backed by citations to the original sources.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=121625&key=user_uploads/3347806/67343f3b-d56a-4d11-9684-76ed1186352f)

## Built with surgeons. Growing with the industry.

**Developed with five chief surgeons**, CONUS is already live in more than 20 European hospitals just six months after launch and works with manufacturers including Stryker, B. Braun and many more.

We're building a growing, structured knowledge base across medical device portfolios, combining manufacturer information with hospital-specific systems and protocols.

And we're just getting started. Over time, we want this foundation to support how hospitals discover, evaluate and access medical devices across manufacturers.

## Our ask

We're now expanding into the US and would love to connect with medical device companies, particularly people in Sales, Marketing, Product and Field Service, as well as orthopedic surgeons and hospital leaders.

launches.title: Roma: The to-do list that does itself
launches.tagline: We're reinventing the to-do list so it does the work for you.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Roma is the to-do list that does itself. It's the original productivity tool reinvented. The task list you already keep, remade so the tasks actually get done.

<https://youtu.be/6bEw1OBRTkU>

### The original

From pen and paper to apps on a phone, the to-do list has stood the test of time. It's the original productivity tool, and the one tool everyone has used at least once.

You can't say that about many things, especially as technology advances. But whether you have one task or seventeen, there's a to-do list in your head, in your pocket, or on your desk right now.

Since the beginning, all to-do lists have made the same promise: write the task down so you can stop worrying about it. The catch is that you always have to come back and do it yourself. So the tasks pile up.

### The problem

When AI became smart enough to actually help you get things done, we did what a lot of people did and built our own agents. It was hard. It took forever. Even when it worked, it didn't work the way we wanted. 

Then the AI Assistants arrived, promising to handle things for you. People love them. That's the clearest sign the demand is there.

But the work never stay put. It lives in one chat, then another, then an inbox, then a doc somewhere. Instead of doing the work, you're tracking the work down.

### Reinventing the to-do list

That's why we're playing the long game and not building another assistant. We're reinventing the original productivity tool: the to-do list.

**Roma is the to-do list that does itself.** 

That sounds possible with AI, but it's really hard to get right. You have to be able to add a task for anything and the system has to figure out what you meant, get to work on multiple things in the background, sort it into the right project, and surface it at exactly the right time. 

So that's where we spent most of our time building Roma. Underneath Roma is a harness built to take a task from idea to execution. And on top, it feels as simple and light as the to-do list that you're used to. 

### What it feels like

Roma gets real tasks done. But what you notice first is what it does to your mind. You realize you haven't thought about that one task in hours, because it's being handled. You walk into a meeting prepared. You close your laptop with a clear head.

### Why us

We're Jan, Tobi, and Cody. Jan previously built Loom (YC W12, acquired by Dropbox), and Tobi built Senic (YC S13, acquired by Gira). 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117892&key=user_uploads/24212/d1545e35-9497-4e2f-a4f9-34f6420684e6)

### Where this goes

We're only scratching the surface of what Roma can do. As Roma takes on more of your work, the to-do list becomes the place you hand off everything. 

We're going to connect with the apps and assistants you're already using. So whatever you're working on, Roma becomes the center of how it gets done. 

We're only scratching the surface of what Roma can do, and we can't wait to hear what you think.\
\
**Try Roma:**

* Website: <https://roma.app>
* Mac & iOS: <https://roma.app/download>

We're very excited to hear what you all think!

launches.title: Confetti: Build hardware projects using plain-English prompts
launches.tagline: Start designing hardware with one conversation
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re Tianyi and Lucas, the founders of[ Confetti](https://confetti.build). 

We’re building a platform that helps you turn your ideas into physical things using plain English.

With Confetti, you can describe what you want, work through the details, and keep refining it as your idea takes shape, with AI agents handling the CAD, parts sourcing, and firmware.

<https://youtu.be/UhtAs4mg5O8>

**The problem**

You have ideas for things that would make your life better. Something for your desk, your kitchen, your garden, a friend. Something you wish existed, built just the way you want it.

But today, it takes layers of experience just to get started. You need to learn modeling software, find compatible components, design enclosures, figure out wiring and firmware, and understand how to get everything made and sent to you.

We experienced this firsthand while prototyping a home AI device we wanted to build. Every step opened up more questions. Which connector did we need? Would the components fit inside the case? Where could we buy the parts, and when would they arrive? Were they compatible?

We spent so much time figuring out the process before we could make progress on the thing itself.

We don’t think that should be the price of admission. Making things should be for everybody.

**Introducing Confetti**

With Confetti, you can:

* **Design:** Generate and edit 3D designs from text or image prompts.
* **Find parts:** Source off-the-shelf components and get help with wiring and firmware for electronics projects.
* **Get things made:** Get manufacturing quotes and send supported 3D printing jobs directly to print farms, with parts delivered to your doorstep.
* **Share and remix:** Explore what other makers are creating and personalize their designs for yourself.

![Confetti CAD design workspace](https://www.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=125304&key=user_uploads/2606179/1972af9c-a7ae-47f7-a430-5298623d3f93)

People are already using Confetti to work on things like a portable dynamic mechanical analyzer for their physics lab, a custom keyboard to type faster, desk companions for the office, and personalized gifts for friends.

**Why we’re building this**

We’re two UPenn CS dropouts who love building. Between us, we’ve won nine hackathons, conducted research at Stanford and Wolfram Research, and published at ICML. Confetti is the tool we wished we had when we started building hardware ourselves.

![Tianyi and Lucas by the Y Combinator sign](https://www.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=125304&key=user_uploads/2606179/ef850b2b-611b-4fdb-a027-7401ff2f87eb)

AI has changed who can build software. We believe hardware is next. We envision an age of personal hardware, where the things around us can be shaped by our habits, our surroundings, and the people we care about. 

With Confetti, more people can experiment, solve their own problems, and make personalized things that otherwise wouldn’t exist.

**Our ask**

**What’s something you wish existed?** Try making it at[ ](https://confetti.build)[confetti.build](http://confetti.build)[ (https://confetti.build)](https://confetti.build), or share your idea in the comments. We’d love to help you bring it to life.

If you know someone who’s always making things or talking about something they wish they could make, send Confetti their way.

Happy making!

launches.title: Alkera - The data agent that you can trust
launches.tagline: Alkera is an agent that replaces your coding agent to reliably and safely perform real data engineering/analysis/science work.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Data teams adopting AI agents want speed, but one wrong step can quietly ripple through your dbt models, dashboards, and business decisions before anyone notices. [Alkera](https://alkera.ai) **is an AI data agent for data engineers/analysts/scientists or anyone who wants to gather data insights that actually understands your data stack** (column-level lineage, graph-based planning, and a living knowledge base), so it ships data work you can trust. It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's [DataAgentBench](https://ucbepic.github.io/DataAgentBench/),** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fQEVpQPYNxg>

Coding agents can write data code that runs. **For data engineering, knowing it's correct is the hard part.** This is knowing that a transformation didn't quietly redefine a column three models downstream and corrupt the revenue dashboard that the exec team checks every Monday. **For data analysis and data science, beyond data access and lineage problems, coding agents struggle with highly parallel work spread across multiple machines.** When interacting with remote computing nodes, they do so only via fragile chains of SSH commands. Long processing and training runs have you more as a babysitter than a scientist.

**Alkera is a data agent that works natively across your entire data stack, with the context and guardrails coding agents lack.** Every change it makes to a query, transformation, model, or notebook is backed by a real understanding of your pipeline.

It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's DataAgentBench,** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks. You reach it through an IDE extension (VSCode, Cursor), a CLI, or the browser — wherever you already work.

What makes it different:

* **Column-level lineage across your data stack.** Trace a single row from Snowflake, through your dbt models, to your Hex dashboard. Before the agent changes anything, it maps the _blast radius_ — every downstream table and dashboard the change would touch.
* **Graph-based planning with flexible computation.** Plan complex data tasks with parallel agents from a quick analysis to days-long modeling experiments to run across your machine and remote CPU/GPU nodes.
* **A living knowledge base.** Alkera learns your schema docs, trusted queries, and the tribal conventions that never make it into documentation — written by both agents and humans, with humans verifying what the agent adds.
* **Production protection.** Fine-grained permissions over every tool, including bash and SQL. Block a seemingly innocent SQL query with a dangerous UPDATE hidden away in a subexpression. Enforce OAuth to connect your warehouses to maintain existing data permissions.

# **Try it**

Download Alkera at <https://alkera.ai> or read the docs at <https://docs.alkera.ai>. For data engineering, point it at your stack and **watch it trace a change through your pipeline**, lighting up everything downstream. name: Definite
long_description:
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build, or operate things can see how the way they run shows up in their numbers.

These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads.

So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter?

Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. We never write back to your systems.

We met studying at the University of Waterloo. Gurshabd worked at BitGo, where proofs that customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand. Farhan built machine learning systems at Meta. Mazin worked at Optiver, then built LLM agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where he saw that finance teams won't act on a number they can't trace to its source.

launches.tagline: The most accurate AI agents for financial reporting
launches.body:
_AI agents that run the entire regulatory reporting pipeline for banks, from raw ledger data to the filed report._

**_TL;DR_**_: Definite automates regulatory reporting for banks end to end, from raw ledger data to filed report, turning weeks of manual work into hours._ [usedefinite.com](http://usedefinite.com)

Hey! We're Gurshabd, Mazin and Farhan from Definite.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji1ae8y_V4E>

**The Problem**

Proving to regulators that their books follow the rules is a constant, non-negotiable obligation for banks. Each report is thousands of numbers, personally signed off by an executive. Getting it wrong can mean a **fine up to a million dollars** over a single undetected error. Producing that proof is slow, and doesn't even guarantee it's correct. 

Here's where the current system breaks down:

1. **Wasted Hours:** A controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it line by line by hand. By regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks of employee time, time pulled from higher-value finance work every quarter.
2. **False Confidence:** The software banks use to file checks formatting, not truth. A loan mapped to the wrong schedule line sails through every check. Nothing catches it until an examiner does, and by then it's not a mistake, it's a violation.

**The Solution**

**Report agents:** We connect to your books and our agents build the reports you owe.

**Verification engine:** Every number is recomputed from source records and checked against a versioned rulebook, so each line carries its rule and source data.

**Self-correcting agents:** When a check fails, the agent gets the reason and fixes it in seconds. Real exceptions come to your team with a drafted explanation, not a blank error. This loop is why our agents are the most accurate in finance.

**Receipts:** Every check produces a tamper-evident receipt you can hand an examiner or auditor.

Your team reviews and signs instead of building.

**How we got here**

Gurshabd worked at BitGo, a regulated crypto custodian, where attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand every period. Farhan worked at Meta where he delved extensively into machine learning and building AI agents. Mazin saw Optiver recheck daily regulatory numbers by hand, then built LLM agents at [Boosted.ai](http://Boosted.ai) and learned finance people won't act on AI output unless every number comes with its source.

The lesson from all three: in finance, producing a number is cheap, proving it is the job. On two public reporting benchmarks, DeepSeek V3 with our verification engine outperformed GPT-5 on reconciliation accuracy (FinBalance) at roughly 50× lower cost, and beat the entire published field on XBRL calculation validation (FinAuditing).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105798&key=user_uploads/2947446/1b80714c-9a38-4d02-a037-ab05ad2c9205)

Follow us: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/usedefinite/?viewAsMember=true), and [X](https://x.com/UseDefinite).

We'll be in the comments. [gurshabd@usedefinite.com](mailto:gurshabd@usedefinite.com)

**TL;DR: Veltha is an AI-native TPA for workers' compensation. TPAs process claims for insurance providers, and our AI owns this service end to end. An adjuster only reviews the decision, work that used to take 6 hours now takes 10 minutes - with better outcomes.**

<https://www.loom.com/share/9e9701f61bf4400890b4799fdda3d3ff>

**The problem**

TPAs deliver terrible service across the board. We have yet to find a carrier or employer that is happy with theirs. The misalignment is structural: TPAs make most of their profit on fees layered on top of claims handling, so quality of the core service barely affects their bottom line. So we decided to deliver the service ourselves.

**What we built**

Veltha runs the whole claim file end to end:

* **Triage.** Reads incoming claim emails and documents, classifies them, and routes each claim to the right workflow.
* **Gap detection.** Checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.
* **Compliance review.** Applies the governing laws and produces a determination where every output is tied to a source and a specific regulatory rule.

Our licensed adjusters review and sign every decision. One adjuster on Veltha handles 4x the caseload of a traditional adjuster with better and quicker outcomes.

* **Carriers and MGAs writing workers' comp** who need a claims administration partner.

Work that took an adjuster \~6 hours now takes \~10 minutes.** Starting with workers' comp and crop insurance.

<https://www.loom.com/share/9e9701f61bf4400890b4799fdda3d3ff>

**The problem**

1 in 4 claims adjusters expect to retire within five years. Experienced adjusters are retiring faster than carriers can replace them, and processing capacity is now the binding constraint on growth.

**What we built**

Veltha is an AI claims adjuster that runs the whole file end to end:

* **Triage** - reads incoming claim emails and documents, classifies them, and routes each claim to the right workflow.
* **Gap detection** - checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.
* **Compliance review** - applies the relevant federal rulebook, and produces a determination where **every output element is tied to a source span and a specific regulatory provision.**

The adjuster's job shifts from _doing_ the claim to _reviewing_ Veltha's output. Less chasing. Faster decisions. Output that survives an audit.

**What we understand that others don't: regulation is the moat, not the obstacle.** Horizontal platforms (Guidewire, Duck Creek) and generic AI-claims startups can summarize a claim file. They can't tell you _which_ provision triggered _which_ adjustment, with citations. We treat the federal rulebook as an anchor for the workflow we embed within the organisation. That's the difference between a summary a human re-does from scratch and an output an adjuster will actually sign.

The love interest sounds like someone worth waiting for. It stops feeling like you’re being read to, and starts feeling like you’re in the room. Any story, ready to play, more gripping than ever.

launches.body:
**TLDR:** Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for companies building with AI in the physical space, from robot fleets on customer sites to agents running in production. This year many insurance companies stopped covering risks that involve AI. We find the insurers that will still cover it, translate what you're building into terms they can price, and read every clause before anything is signed.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jHTzpKbmZa4>

**The problem**

Starting this year, many insurance companies began excluding coverage for injury and property damage arising out of AI.

For a hardtech company that language reaches everything you do. If AI touched the work anywhere, including the tools your engineers designed it with or the product itself, the insurer can deny the claim.

The problem with these exclusions is that they get added account by account, so the same hardware can be covered at one insurer and excluded at the next, and nothing in the process makes that obvious. It shows up as a form number on the endorsement list attached to your renewal, which is why most founders don't learn they have one until they file a claim.

**Why now**

Physical AI is scaling faster than the insurance market underneath it. Insurance moves slower, and its first instinct with an unfamiliar risk is to exclude it and wait for loss data. Cyber went the same way: exclusions first, then specialists who understood it, then a real market. AI is at the exclusion stage now, and these companies pushing the frontier can't wait for the cycle to finish on its own. 

**What we do**

We handle the whole coverage process end to end.

You send us an application. We take what you're building and put it in terms an insurance company can understand and price.

Then we go to market. We have access to hundreds of insurance companies, the ones that actually write this kind of risk, and we take your file to them. Most will pass. The few that want it compete on price and terms, and we keep shopping until every requirement you have is met, including the limits your customer contracts demand.

When offers come back we read the policies line by line. If an AI exclusion is attached, we push to get it removed, or we find a company that writes the AI coverage in on purpose. Then we tell you in plain terms what you've got.

We cover the lines your company actually needs: general liability, umbrella, property, equipment in transit and on customer sites, workers' comp, professional liability, management liability, and cyber.

You never pay us. The insurance company pays us a commission out of the premium when a policy is placed, so applying costs you nothing and there's no additional fee from us at any point.

**Where this goes**

Physical AI is expanding faster than any industry, and every company in it buys insurance every year for as long as it exists. The programs grow as the fleets grow.

We want to be the brokerage that grows with them: the people who know this risk best, hold the relationships with the markets that write it, and build the loss data of the future.

**Why us**

We're Sam and Alex, on leave from Harvard. We were already in insurance building models when we noticed that batch mates building some of the most innovative technology in the world couldn't get covered at all. Since then we’ve landed partnerships to offer these frontier companies easier access to better policies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110197&key=user_uploads/2666435/74c5c462-a2ff-44b8-ac6c-f8ebc7807dbd)


**The ask**

If you're building anything on the frontier, apply at[ risklytics.ai](http://risklytics.ai). It takes a few minutes, it costs nothing, and we'll come back with what the market says.

It doesn't matter what you have in place today. If you're building, we want to get you covered.

And if you're an insurer, MGA or wholesaler with appetite here, we want to talk:[ risklytics.ai/markets](https://www.risklytics.ai/markets/)

launches.title: Limnion: Telemetry storage built for the agentic era
launches.tagline: The open foundation for building agent-first observability.
launches.body:
**Modern observability is dying.**

<https://youtu.be/eE0DmtIGSsw>

Limnion is building telemetry storage for the agentic era. Our open-source foundation, Siglake, stores your logs and traces in open formats in your own cloud storage, so your AI agents can query them directly with SQL. No vendor lock-in, no proprietary API in the way. Here’s why I think this is what observability needs.

Gone are the days of humans building dashboards by hand, scrubbing through log lines, and manually tuning alert thresholds. Agents are becoming the primary consumers of telemetry — and when you actually need to look at a dashboard, an agent can create one on the fly. My prediction: 90% of human-centric observability work disappears within two years.

Observability isn’t becoming less valuable — it’s more valuable than ever. What’s changing is who it’s for. The tooling we have today was built for one job: making vast amounts of data understandable to humans. Once humans are no longer the primary consumers, the entire paradigm changes.

Traditional observability won’t disappear, but will instead shrink into something much narrower: a thin governance layer. Humans will still watch the handful of genuinely critical systems and keep an eye on the agentic layer itself to make sure it’s doing its job. Someone has to watch the watchers. Everything else migrates to agent-native platforms.

The stakes are big. Gartner expects observability platforms to be a \~$14B market by 2028 — Datadog alone is guiding to \~$4.5B in revenue this year — and 44% of Gartner clients already spend more than $1M a year on observability. My bet is that most of that value migrates to the agentic layer, leaving legacy observability as a governance market that’s a fraction of its current size.

That migration is the opportunity — and today’s vendors are on the wrong side of it. Observability vendors, by and large, extract enormous sums for walled gardens that were never built for agentic consumption. They are not — and never will be — incentivized to give your agents wide-open access to the underlying data. Their business model depends on keeping it locked in.

The agentic era needs the opposite: telemetry storage that’s open by design and built for agents first. That’s Siglake.

Siglake stores telemetry in purely open formats — Parquet, Iceberg, Arrow — and makes it queryable with SQL by default. Your data lives in your own object storage, readable by Siglake, any Iceberg engine, or your agents directly. Pull it into DuckDB, feed it into a Spark pipeline, or consume a live Arrow stream to drive custom anomaly detection that feeds your agents for proactive monitoring.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125687&key=user_uploads/57320/9965b1ba-0608-4672-b5de-8ee004bdf5cb)

Companies are already weighing their observability spend against competing AI budgets and realizing that an open, agent-native backend compounds their AI investment instead of competing with it. Siglake is Apache 2.0, and it will stay that way — the open core of the platform we’re building at Limnion.

I’ve spent \~15 years in this space. I co-founded InfluxData (YC W13) and Era Software (acquired by ServiceNow), built observability products for Cloud Foundry at Pivotal, and served as CTO of Hydrolix. I’ve watched this same pattern repeat at company after company — it’s why I’m building Limnion and making Siglake open-source.

If you’re rethinking your observability stack for the agentic era — or you just want to argue with the thesis — I’d love to talk. Siglake is on [GitHub](https://github.com/siglake/siglake), and you can reach me anytime at [todd@limnion.ai](mailto:todd@limnion.ai).

launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋

We're [Aniket](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anideshp/) & [Mugdhaa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mugdhaa-patankar/), co-founders of [Agent FM](https://www.agentfm.ai/).

**TL;DR:** Agent FM is a desktop app that gives engineers one group chat to hear and steer their coding agents. Instead of manually bouncing between different claude code and codex sessions, and combing through walls of text to monitor agents, engineers just tune in to Agent FM. Agents share important progress updates, blockers, assumptions, and decisions in the group chat. Engineers get live text and audio updates and respond right from the chat.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVGLQwclkYI> 

#### The Problem:

**Babysitting agents is exhausting.** Engineers running claude code and codex agents spend all day bouncing between multiple sessions, combing through walls of text to keep track of the work. In long horizon tasks, agents often go down the wrong paths, add unnecessary complexity or make bad assumptions that waste time and tokens. Agents can also sometimes misinterpret instructions, make poor decisions, or perform destructive actions due to lack of context and context compaction. To avoid this, engineers continuously keep tabs on their agents, read agent trajectories realtime for anything substantial worth intercepting. This gets really exhausting with more agents and time. We lack the tooling that automatically does this for engineers.

#### Our Solution:

* **One interface to rule them all:** Computer use + live audio updates + group chat with your agents. One command center to interact with your coding agents without babysitting and manually polling different Claude Code and Codex sessions.
* **Actionable metrics and insights into agent activity across model providers:** Deep insights and metrics about token spend across providers, cost distribution, skills and mcp token performance, and recurring patterns.
* **Works with the tools engineers already use:** No setup needed. Agent FM automatically works across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other coding tools. Local and remote workspaces supported.
* **Voice-to-text AI**: Context aware and low-latency voice-to-text AI to prompt 4x faster anywhere on your computer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109244&key=user_uploads/355672/6ac94f50-a6ac-4b2d-9290-819f9711037e)

#### Traction

* **410 engineers** are using Agent FM (**60+ paying**), 
* **120k+ audio updates** heard by engineers. 
* **1.2 hours/day** average time spent on Agent FM

#### Our asks

* Give Agent FM a try and let us know what you think: [agentfm.ai](http://agentfm.ai)
* If there’s a team or company you think would benefit with Agent FM, write to us at [founders@agentfm.ai](mailto:founders@agentfm.ai) 

#### The Team:

Aniket and Mugdhaa have known each other for almost 10 years and co-founded Agent FM in 2026.

Aniket (CEO) worked at Meta Superintelligence Labs, where he built agent-orchestration, RL, and search infra, fine-tuned models, grew Meta AI monthly active users by 250K and built critical parts of the Llama training data flywheel.

Mugdhaa (CTO) led AI for developer productivity at Snowflake, where she built model harnesses, evals, developer tooling, and orchestration systems that help engineers adopt AI and move faster. Before Snowflake, she worked at Twitch on live video playback and distribution, building systems that keep Twitch reliable at scale for the biggest live events on the internet (Ibai La Velada, MrBeast), serving 10M+ concurrent requests.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We met at Brex in 2020, where we worked on the platform team and saw how manual operational work could become a bottleneck to growth. Even straightforward onboarding tasks required people to research information, handle exceptions, and make decisions.

We started Parcha in 2023 to build AI agents for compliance workflows. That gave us firsthand experience with repetitive, high-stakes work where accuracy and control matter. We built Grep AI to make those capabilities available to teams automating repetitive knowledge work across their business.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer:
We started in 2023 as Parcha, building AI agents for compliance teams. Working on those workflows taught us how to handle complex research, exceptions, and judgment while keeping people in control.

We also saw the same need beyond compliance. In 2026, we expanded into Grep AI, a managed agent platform for repetitive, high-stakes knowledge work across operations, research, and other business functions. We are now building self-improving agents that learn from repeated work, with the goal of improving accuracy and reducing cost as they scale.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Businesses are full of repetitive work that still requires research, judgment, and context. Reviewing documents, investigating a business, or researching a prospect can look similar from one case to the next, but exceptions make rigid automation difficult.

The people who understand these jobs often have to do them manually or wait for engineering help. Grep AI lets them describe the work and create managed agents to repeat it, with tools, shared context, and controls. Our focus is work that needs to be accurate and economical when it runs thousands of times.

At IG Group, our agents review screening alerts during customer onboarding, clearing false positives and escalating cases that need manual review. The IG case study reports that activation time for flagged customers fell from 2–3 days to under 10 minutes.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
We want to rid businesses of tedious, repetitive work so their employees can focus on the highest-leverage tasks. The people who know a workflow best should be able to turn it into a managed agent without having to build and maintain the infrastructure themselves.

As those agents repeat the work, they should become more useful and less expensive to run. Success means teams can grow without manual operational work becoming the bottleneck.

launches.body:
Hey everyone!

We’re AJ and Miguel from Grep AI. We’re building self-improving agents for tedious, repetitive work that’s slowing down your business. [IG.com](http://IG.com), a UK-based online brokerage, used our agents to automate 80% of onboarding, unlocking a record year of growth that led to their graduation to the FTSE 100.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/s9NEm6rRcCA>

**The problem: repetitive work that requires judgment and expertise is still too hard to automate and scale.**

At Brex, we had 2,000 businesses waiting to onboard because we needed to manually review each one to verify they had a physical address. Fast-growing companies are full of tedious, repetitive tasks like this that become a bottleneck to growth, but require research, judgment, and some expertise.

But getting an agent to accurately and efficiently complete a task that requires automation, investigation, and some judgment thousands of times is still a challenge.

Hard-coded LLM workflows like LangGraph and n8n are cheaper to scale, but can’t adapt to edge cases. E.g., the business has a physical address on Google Maps, but it’s actually a mailbox in a co-working facility.

General-purpose agents like Codex, Cowork, and Copilot are much better at handling exceptions, but when performing repetitive tasks, they waste expensive tokens reasoning through the workflow as if they were a new employee. Enterprises often offshore these types of tasks at $6-$12/hr, so if the agent costs $4/tasks they are not going to use it.

**Grep AI: Self-improving agents that get smarter and cost less with every run.**

Grep AI is a managed agent platform that lets you create, optimize, and deploy self-improving agents to automate repetitive work in minutes without writing any code. Our agents learn from every run, getting smarter and costing less as you scale them.

How Grep AI works:

* **Create an agent in minutes** with just a prompt and any useful docs. Grep uses deep research, a library of more than 300 built-in skills, and over 100 data integrations to make each agent an expert out of the box.

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117558&key=user_uploads/21987/30597b7c-03c9-4bc6-aa9d-542b42f8b550)

* **Frontier or open-source models:** Unlike OpenAI’s Agent API or Claude Managed Agents, you aren’t locked into one model provider.
* **Self-improving harness:** Our harness learns as it repeats a task, moving repeatable steps from frontier LLM calls into workflows and code, so it gets smarter and cheaper with every run.
* **Secure sandbox:** Agents run in a secure sandbox with a file system, audit logs, access controls, and cost caps included.
* **Run from anywhere:** Use agents manually in our app, or via schedules and monitors, batches, API, MCP, and TypeScript and Python SDKs.
* **Stay in control:** Manage your agent workforce with a central dashboard to monitor cost, accuracy, and auditability.

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117558&key=user_uploads/21987/e63bf34e-dfd1-42cf-94cc-68ee90612083)


**How companies use Grep AI**

Companies like Airwallex, Citizens Bank, Worldpay, Global Payments, and Shopmonkey use Grep for business due diligence, underwriting, document verification, HR operations, GTM ops, competitive intelligence, and social and market research. 

In six months we’ve saved these companies over 150,000 hours of work

**Why us?**

**AJ** led AI/ML products at Coinbase and Brex. His first startup was acquired by Google, where he worked on Google Photos and Android.

**Miguel** led Platform Engineering at Brex across ML, data, financial infrastructure, and compliance operations tooling. Before that, he led data science at Twitter.

We met at Brex in 2020, where we scaled the customer base 10x in a year with automation across risk, compliance, customer support, and operations, before AI agents existed. That experience inspired us to start working on AI agents for compliance teams in 2023. Then we took everything we learned from building agents and turned it into a managed agent platform to scale any repetitive work.

**Do you have any repetitive operations/back-office work that’s slowing down your company?**

* Go to <https://grep.ai> or point your coding agent there to get started.
* Book an onboarding call with us here: <https://calendly.com/grepai/grep-onboarding>
* Or reach out to [founders@grep.ai](mailto:founders@grep.ai), and we’ll help you tune an agent for your workflow.

launches.tagline: Every request shows up with the work already done.
launches.body:
## **TLDR**

Neomatter is the operating system for in-house legal teams. It plugs into the places your company already works (email, Slack, Salesforce, etc) and picks up legal requests as they come in. When someone sends legal a contract or a question, the work is already done before a lawyer opens it, ready to review and approve.\
\
<https://youtu.be/delvI16C41E>

## **The problem**

Every part of your company runs through legal.

Sales needs contracts signed. HR needs employment agreements. Finance needs board approvals. And every department has legal questions.

But legal teams spend a lot of their time on repetitive work: reviewing the same terms, searching for old agreements, answering familiar questions, and chasing information.

The software tools haven't solved this. One tool manages contracts, another handles requests, and another tracks approvals. Lawyers still have to piece the work together themselves.

And when teams reach capacity, companies hire more lawyers or send work to expensive outside firms.

## **What we’re building**

Neomatter takes a request from start to finish. It gathers context, reviews documents, checks the company’s policies and precedents, and prepares the work for approval.

## **How it works**

Neomatter monitors the places legal requests already come through (email, Slack, teams, Salesforce, and more) and automatically triages requests to the right lawyer. Nobody has to tag anything or learn a new tool.

Then it does the work. It reads everything, does the redlines, checks it against your team’s playbooks, drafts the reply, and waits for your decision. By the time you know the matter exists, 90% of the work has already been done. The lawyer opens finished work, checks the sources, writes any edits, and makes the decision.

And it can handle anything. Commercial work, employment work, corporate work, a “can I do this?” question, or anything else a legal team receives. Neomatter does it all.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122248&key=user_uploads/1633544/eecfd55b-a702-4725-b7b3-3baed9d62b2f)

## **The team**

We’re Luke & Luke. We dropped out of university to move to San Francisco.

We believe AI has fundamentally changed how much work one person can do. After speaking with over 200 in-house legal teams, we realized AI can completely change the way lawyers work.

We’re building Neomatter to make that happen.

## **The ask**

If you're a GC, Head of Legal, or in-house lawyer, book a call and we'll show you: <https://cal.com/luke-wagner-mpxe1o/30-minute-meeting>

If you know someone who works in legal at a company, we'd love an intro.

Or reach us directly at [founders@neomatter.com](mailto:founders@neomatter.com).

launches.title: Simantic: Firmware Simulation for AI Agents
launches.tagline: Firmware validation at the speed of software
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re Seungmin and Ahnaf, the founders of Simantic.

Simantic is building the simulation layer for AI to test and validate firmware at the speed of software.

<https://youtu.be/tIrz-o43ig0>

**The Problem**\
Frontier AI models have made code generation for firmware cheap and effortless, but firmware testing still relies on manual hardware debugging using expensive equipment running software from over a decade ago. Simantic is modernizing the firmware test workflows with simulation made for the era of coding agents.

We’re developing the runtime context that AI models need to verify mission-critical firmware behavior, without being bounded by the limitations of hardware.

**Our Solution**

We built the world’s first agent-first firmware simulator. We provide multiple interfaces to the simulator, so you can use it from anywhere. Here are the interfaces you can use Simantic with:

* **Cloud Sim** is the first virtual devboard you can program and run entirely from your terminal with zero setup, using simple curl commands. All you need is the MCU model and compiled ELF binary.\
  \
  In addition to the curl API, we developed these interfaces:
  * TypeScript SDK (<https://www.npmjs.com/package/@simantic/cloud-sim>)
  * MCP (<https://www.npmjs.com/package/@simantic/cloud-sim-mcp>)

    ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125708&key=user_uploads/3082935/ee71038c-cdef-4a4d-add6-ba7668a02648)

    You can try out Cloud Sim here: <https://simantic.com/cloud-sim>
* **Simantic Bot** is the first AI code reviewer made for firmware. The reviewer agent identifies the hardware platform, build system, and the changes are made in the code based on the diffs and comments. What makes it different from other code reviewer bots is that it actually runs your code on a simulated version of the microcontroller, and inputs to peripherals like CAN, UART, Ethernet, and BLE can be simulated according to different scenarios.\
  \
  Here is a short demo of Simantic Bot:\
  <https://youtu.be/kBK1ZjGWWbQ?si=aJxnbBQjZBPxvt4i>
* **Pyrite** is our frontier firmware simulation model, currently available to select partners and users. You gain full access to the binary so users can run simulations locally, and develop applications like CI/CD pipelines, or agent harnesses with. Please contact us directly for access.

**The Team**

**Seungmin (CEO)** studied Computer Engineering at the University of Waterloo. Previously working at Tesla as a Firmware Engineer on the Keys & Authentication team, and the Prototype Engineering team building early prototypes of the Cybertruck and Cybercab. Seungmin also worked across multiple robotic startups in the Bay Area and Tokyo as an Embedded Firmware Engineer.

**Ahnaf (CTO)** studied Computer Engineering at the University of Waterloo. Previously working at Neuralink as an Embedded Software Engineer, building wireless chargers for the brain implant chips. Ahnaf built AI chips as an AI Hardware Engineer on the Autopilot team at Tesla, designed chips at NXP Semiconductors, and developed wireless firmware for Onsemi.

While working at these companies, we came across the same problem: the hardware testing loop is too slow, and engineering teams are being bottlenecked by hardware in firmware testing and validation. As firmware development workflows are moving towards AI generated code, firmware testing is still manually done on physical hardware, like Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) setups or on development boards.

We came to the same conclusion, that hardware teams needed a better way to test firmware in an AI driven workflow. We founded Simantic to build the simulation environment that enables AI agents to run and test firmware, without being limited by physical hardware.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125708&key=user_uploads/3082935/a537c777-0d8a-46ba-903d-ee66f59a3220)

**Our Ask**

Are you building embedded systems in automotive, robotics, or aerospace? Contact us at [founders@simantic.dev](mailto:founders@simantic.dev), or go to <https://simantic.com/>.

Runtime is building a simulation-based robot policy that needs no fine-tuning or teleoperation.\
\
<https://youtu.be/FgQBFk13k6M>

More companies than ever are deploying robots. For them, deployment should be plug-and-play: show the robot the task, and it works out the rest.

Runtime turns what the robot sees into a simulation, searches through options, acts on what works, and keeps the simulation in sync with reality. In our experiments, Runtime matches or beats leading robot foundation models on real-world tasks like rope threading and egg grasping. Next, we’re speeding up the loop so it can run live.

We’re Liam, Yim, and Chen from Penn GRASP. We’ve published/reviewed at CVPR, ECCV, and NeurIPS, with experiences in CV, control, RL, and robot foundation models. We’ve seen simulation become fast and accurate enough for more than training and evaluation, and we’re bringing sim directly into how robots act.

If you’re building or deploying robots, we’d love to hear what yours struggle with. Early access opens in January at [runtime.si](http://runtime.si).

launches.tagline: Test your agent in stateful clones of the apps it works in
launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're [Aneesh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aneeshkethini/) and [Josh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joshua-d-le/).

**TL;DR:** Hue creates stateful clones of the apps your agent connects to, so you can test changes against realistic tools, data, and state before they reach users.

**The problem**

Agents take on real work now: they send emails on our behalf, update CRMs, and issue refunds. But there’s usually no safe place to test them. You can’t experiment on a user’s live inbox, mock APIs aren’t representative, and sandbox tenants start empty, so your agent never meets the messy data and business nuance it will see in production. When an agent fails in production, it’s difficult to reproduce the issue and verify a fix.

**How Hue solves this**

Hue simulates all the apps your agent might use, like Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, Notion, and Quickbooks. The apps are populated in two ways

* Generate worlds: let your coding agent describe the environment to test against, like the apps of a 40-person software company that just raised their Series B, and Hue populates the apps with months of realistic history within a couple minutes.
* Start from real runs: Hue uses your agent traces to recreate the state of the world during a real run, so you can reproduce agent failures and verify the fix.

Your agent uses these apps just like it uses the real ones, without touching any live accounts. You can run your agent from the same starting point as many times as you need, test it against various situations in minutes, set up evals to measure performance quantitatively, and compare versions before you ship.

<https://youtu.be/tvGNnKpd8oE>

**The team**

We’ve spent the past few years shipping frontier agents.

* **Aneesh Kethini:** Prev PM for Datadog’s AI SRE Agent, and Quantitative Trader at SIG
* **Josh Le:** Prev built frontier legal agents at August, SWE at Apple, Gusto, SendBlue, Wayfair

At our previous roles, we were responsible for building high-quality testing environments, infrastructure to turn production usage into replayable scenarios, and systems to simulate representative data. We know first-hand how important realistic environments are to agent testing. Now, we’re building Hue so every team can hand its agent real work and trust it to do that work well.

**Our Ask**

* Building an agent that works across third-party tools and still using unrepresentative sandbox tenants or mocked APIs? [Book a demo](https://cal.com/aneesh-hue/20min).
* Know a team shipping frontier agents? We’d love an intro: [founders@hue.run](mailto:founders@hue.run)

name: herdr
long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

name: Sentient OS
long_description:
Truly personal AI requires running inference on your life, every day. In the cloud, that’s expensive and a privacy nightmare. On your own chip, it’s free and private.

Our custom inference stack, built on a LiteRT-LM fork, runs on Macs with just 8 GB of RAM. Every night, Sentient’s on-device models process your emails, messages, Granola transcripts, files, and more, building a rich personal knowledge base on your Mac.

Your projects, conversations, commitments, and preferences. Context you’d never have the time to type into a chatbot.

That understanding powers three ways to get work done:

Sidekick: click your Mac’s notch and say “finish this for me.” It already has your context and gets to work across your apps and browser with its own cursor, while you keep working.

Proactive intelligence: wake up to work already prepared. The reply you forgot, drafted. The subscription renewing tomorrow, caught. The report you promised, ready for review. Sentient waits for your approval before acting.

Double Tap: two taps, two seconds, and the reply you would have written appears, drafted from your personal context and writing style. Just review and send.

Open source and built with privacy at its core. Over 30 enterprises use Sentient already.

Our alpha reached 4,000+ users in its first week with $0 marketing. Our launch was the top post of the month on r/macapps.

We’ve raised over $1 million with participation from Y Combinator (F26), Afore, Pioneer Fund, and a16z speedrun’s scout fund.

launches.body:
We’re Aditya and Jesai, 18 and 20, and we’re building **Sentient OS: on-device AI that understands your life overnight, so you can hand off work in an instant.**

<https://youtu.be/if5vwTbmvVw>

Your life is scattered across emails, messages, notes, and files. While you sleep, Sentient’s on-device LLM connects the dots, building the personal context you’d never have time to type into a chatbot.

That understanding powers two magical experiences:

**1. Your replies, in two taps.**

Click into an email or message reply box and double tap your right Command key. Sentient drafts the reply you would have written, drawing on your personal context and writing style, right where you’re typing.

No more spending your morning writing 15 email replies from scratch. Just review and send.

**2. Hand off the work you’re already doing.**

Click your Mac’s notch and say **“finish this for me.”** Sidekick picks up where you left off, working across your apps and browser with its own cursor, while you keep working.

Follow up after a meeting, prepare an investor update, or finish an application. It brings your personal context into the task, so you can hand off the work without explaining your life first.

**Why we’re building on-device**

We’re obsessed with pushing the limits of on-device LLMs and the experiences they unlock. Running inference on the chip you already own lets an AI spend hours understanding your life every night without a cloud inference bill.

Our custom inference stack builds that understanding on Apple silicon Macs with just **8 GB of RAM**. Your knowledge lives in an editable Markdown folder on your Mac. You can read it, correct it, and use it with other AI tools.

Sentient is **open source**. Your connected local sources are analyzed on-device. Sidekick can use your existing ChatGPT or Claude subscription, and cloud-powered features receive context for the task. You can also choose compatible local models.

**10,000+ people already use Sentient**, including users at 130+ companies such as Adobe.

[**Download Sentient for Mac**](https://sentient-os.ai/). Try Double Tap on a reply you’ve been putting off, or hand Sidekick something that’s taking time away from building. We’d love to hear what you hand off first :)

\-- Jesai & Aditya

Hey everyone! We're [Ryan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryan-ning) and [Satyam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/satyamsingh2003).

**TL;DR:** Simulithic sends AI agents through your app the way real users do, on every device, browser, and account type. No test scripts to write, nothing to maintain, and you hear about broken flows before your users do.

**The problem: Verification is the new bottleneck**

Every engineering team is limited by how fast it can verify what it built works. 

For decades, writing code was the slow part, so nobody noticed.

AI changed that. Agents now write code in minutes, but checking it still means hand-written Playwright tests, or worse, manual clicking before every deploy.

This means teams can generate 10x more code but can't ship 10x more, because every change still has to be verified. And the faster code gets written, the bigger this gap becomes.

We believe the teams that win will be the ones that can verify as fast as they can build.

That's what Simulithic does.\
<https://youtu.be/u7nAthxNX0c>

**How Simulithic works**

* **Maps every user flow with one command.** Point Simulithic at your app and AI agents explore it like real users, discovering flows on their own. No more manually write test scripts or describing every flow.
* **Tests where your users actually are.** Every device (iOS, Android, macOS, Windows), browser, account type, and network speed your customers use.
* **No maintenance.** When the UI changes, the agents adapt. Nothing to rewrite.
* **Runs everywhere you ship.** While you code, as the end-to-end step in CI/CD, and continuously in production, checking your live flows every day.
* **Alerts you in Slack** before your users notice something broke.

**The team**

**Ryan (CEO)** was an engineering intern at Uber and Shopify and researched AI agent design, implementation, and evaluation at the University of Toronto as an undergrad.

**Satyam (CTO)** was an engineering intern at Ramp and Bree (YC S21). He's won 41 of 51 hackathons, including NASA Space Apps (first ever Canadian team to win out of 15,444 teams globally), and was an MLH Top 50 Hacker.

The West’s defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains. Demand for new capability is surging, and materials still take decades to develop. We’re building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the materials the West needs, securely, fast and at cost.

launches.tagline: Building a new chemical company for the critical materials the West needs
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re Sam, Ofir and Maor, founders of ChemPilot (YC F26).

We are building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can autonomously discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the critical chemicals and materials the West needs. 

ChemPilot grew out of two and a half years of academic research by Sam and Ofir in the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana. During that research, we collaborated with a top defense prime and government R&D agencies to discover critical chemicals and materials using AI. We saw how urgently better materials were needed, and how slowly they were being developed.

Our models needed experimental data to predict what would work. That data was locked inside companies or had never been collected. Generating new data and testing candidates through defense primes and outsourced labs was too slow to support the pace of development we needed. We needed our own ability to generate high-quality experimental data at scale. That’s why we’re building an autonomous lab!

Maor joined the research effort a year ago, bringing his background in computer science and electrical engineering. Together, we began building the models, software and automation that would become ChemPilot.

<https://youtu.be/q5YMnXcxaIY?si=FkYf1ep25-kvI6vB>

Our AI agents research the chemistry, design new molecules and optimize formulations using predictive models and physics-based simulation, then build experimental protocols. Our lab makes and tests the candidates. Every result, failures included, feeds back into our models and informs the next experiment.

Our first lab is already running experiments, with robots working alongside our scientists. We’re automating it step by step toward full autonomy: AI deciding what to make next, and robots running experiments around the clock to produce consistent, traceable data at a scale we couldn’t imagine achieving manually.

We’re starting with polymers, coatings, resins and composites. Each program builds data and capabilities that help us develop the next product, growing a portfolio of high-performance materials on one platform. Our work on energetic materials and propellants is currently partnership-led, with plans to bring those capabilities into our own lab next.

Our future should be determined by how quickly we can invent and build, not what others are willing to supply.

Our asks:

* R&D and materials leaders at defense, aerospace or chemical companies: tell us the material you wish existed or optimized.
* Robotics and lab-automation builders: if you’ve built autonomous labs or robotic systems for chemistry and materials, we’d love to talk.

Reach us at [sam@chempilot.ai](mailto:sam@chempilot.ai).

launches.body:
**TL;DR** [Veeza AI](https://veeza.ai) helps people with weak passports get tourist visas. Upload your passport, and our computer-use agents verify your documents, fill in all the forms and book your visa appointment.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pGgKG-L-VBU>

**The problem**

Hey, I'm Aly. I'm Canadian-Egyptian, and I've traveled on a strong passport and a weak one. With a strong one, you book a flight. With a weak one, you spend hours filling out forms (the UK's is 68 steps long), collect a stack of documents, then fight for an appointment like Taylor Swift tickets. And just like with Taylor Swift tickets, scalpers get there first. Their bots grab the slots and resell them for as much as $1,000.

My friends and I have missed weddings, engagements and conferences because of this. I get that countries need to vet who comes in. It just shouldn't be this hard.

**How Veeza AI works**

1. Pick your destination from 33 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada and Schengen countries.
2. Upload your passport and documents. Our AI verifies them, flags anything missing, fills in all the forms and books your visa appointment.
3. A human reviews everything to make sure it's done right.

Behind the scenes, our computer-use agents work through the government portals for you.

![](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=122484&key=user_uploads/578651/140a58f6-93a5-4631-aaff-51ce99d2417f)

Since joining YC, we've grown from 1,000 to 7,000+ users. People are recommending us to their families and coming back for their next visa. A woman applied through Veeza AI, then her mom did, then her grandmother. One traveler has had four visas approved through us since June.

About 5 billion people have weak passports. We estimate the Global South files 200 million tourist visa applications a year. We're starting with MENA, then the entire Global South. And as personal AI agents start planning and booking people's trips, Veeza AI will be where they turn for visas.

**How you can help**

Know a travel agency or company whose customers need tourist visas? I'd love an intro for B2B2C partnerships.

You can reach us at [**founders@veeza.ai**](mailto:founders@veeza.ai).

Aly

name: Kailash Labs
long_description:
The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines.  Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives.

We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.

name: Reific
long_description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. Each comes from real, de-identified records (health data, industrial sensors, compute-cluster logs), in three families: personal agents, industry, and science and compute. The world keeps moving while the agent works, so the agent must keep learning: data arrive on a clock, and every answer is checked against what actually happened. In each family, the best frontier model averages below half, and models that train on our environments improve.

We specialise in time series because almost everything that matters is recorded that way: a heartbeat, a power grid, a factory line, a GPU cluster, an experiment. No person can turn thousands of moving signals at once into the state of a system and what happens next. AI can pass the bar exam, but it still can’t watch a system for weeks and act at the right moment. It learned from what people wrote down, in environments that freeze the world and abstract it to our understanding.

Time series let us ride the exponential. The world records new data every second and time keeps grading, so each generation of models gets harder, fresher tasks. We believe humans always strive to explore. Our mission is to build the infrastructure for that exploration: the layer of the AI stack where models keep improving, out into what no one understands yet.
