name: Saccade
long_description:
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention.

Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear.

We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics:
• Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path
• Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns.
• Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis.

Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline.

Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.

launches.body:
**TL;DR**

* Start with an idea; AnyAlpha works it out with you and builds the agent
* Backtest it on historical data before it trades
* Trade live 24/7, on multiple exchanges

We're starting with prediction markets, then every asset class.

👉 Try it on iOS: <https://apps.apple.com/us/app/anyalpha/id6762422950>

### **❌ The problem**

Everyone has ideas about what happens next: a rate cut, a playoff game, an election, a product launch, a storm. Turning an idea into a trade is the hard part. You have to find the markets that move with it, decide when to buy and sell, check whether it would have worked before, and then watch the market until the moment comes.

So people do the research by hand from data sites, news, X and Discord, and they trade when they happen to be on their phone. Most ideas never become a trade, and the ones that do are rarely tested first. This is hardest in prediction markets, where information is far more scattered than in stocks, so that's where we're starting.

**🎬 Launch Video**: <https://youtu.be/r21TNgB58lM>

### **✅ How it works**

1. **Start with an idea.** Talk it through with AnyAlpha, and refine it as you go.
2. **AnyAlpha builds the agent.** It finds the markets that move with your idea and decides when to trade them, running on institutional-grade data and the trading infra we built.
3. **Backtest.** See how your agent would have done on historical data before it goes live.
4. **Go live.** Your agent watches the market 24/7 and trades every time its conditions are met.

### **🎯 One example**

One of our users came up with this idea: **“The most hyped NFL team on social media is overpriced.”**

Their agent:

1. **Tracks the hype** — follows social attention around NFL teams on X, Reddit and TikTok.
2. **Checks the price** — compares Kalshi/Polymarket prices with its estimated win probabilities.
3. **Sets the rules** — defines when social attention and market prices should trigger a trade.
4. **Tests the thesis** — backtests the strategy across past NFL seasons.
5. **Takes the other side** — trades against teams it identifies as overpriced, and keeps checking as sentiment and prices change.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124520&key=user_uploads/1353596/3ea911d9-3899-4bbd-bf9e-b799b408e74a)

### 🔭 **Our Vision:**

**Autonomous agents will be the fundamental units of trading. AnyAlpha is the platform to create, test, run, and combine them.**

### **👋 Who we are**

We met at a poker tournament at Microsoft five years ago and have built together for three years, bootstrapping multiple apps to $500K ARR.

**Shirley (CEO, UWaterloo CS):** crypto trading infra at Coinbase, trading terminal at LSEG.

**Jerry (CTO, UC Berkeley CS):** solo quant for 5+ years. Grew $50K of his own money to seven figures, about 85% a year.

### **🙏 Our ask**

* **Trade?** Download [AnyAlpha on iOS ](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/anyalpha/id6762422950)and build your first agent.
* **Power trader?** We'd love to talk with you one-on-one. Email Shirley directly at shirley@anyalpha.ai.

launches.title: Letterpress-1: The world's first coding agent, harness, and IDE for growth engineering
launches.tagline: Letterpress-1 re-imagines every aspect of developer tooling for engineering growth.
launches.body:
Today, the Letter Company is releasing the beta of [Letterpress-1](https://letter.dev/), the world’s first coding agent, harness, and IDE purpose-built for growth engineering. We believe that growth is quickly becoming an engineering problem, but modern engineering tools aren’t designed for this type of challenge.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XD1kMTWNE9c>

Letterpress-1 is built for both the present and the future. It can set-up classic strategies like A/B testing via a _native_ interface, but also build complex tooling to sell to agents. These challenges look radically different but speak the same language: **pull requests**. 

### What makes Letterpress-1 different?

Unlike your main application, your website is reactive to the outside world. To grow quickly, you need to build on signals from various things: agents, Google ranking, customer behavior, and your competitors. Today’s leading coding agents were designed for complex codebases, but not reactiveness to external signals. 

The Letter platform and Letterpress-1 is a different type of coding agent and IDE. It can tackle challenges both tiny and massive. To illustrate this, let’s consider two examples: 

**A tiny challenge?** After installing Letterpress-1, you can directly edit content on your website itself via ⌘+L, with those edits translated into a pull-request. Stop switching between a terminal window and your website. 

**A big challenge?** You can prompt evidence chains to build conviction in external agents that your product creates real outcomes, has recurring users, and proper usage. 

### Letterpress-1 is built for today.

There are so many things that you can build with Letterpress-1 without requiring external tools. All of these are equally proactive: Letter will encourage you to build these things. For example: 

* Set-up A/B testing, and automatically prioritize winning branches based on conversion.
* Install de-anonymization via middleware, warm email addresses, and set-up outbound. 
* Find missing landing page opportunities and build them with brand consistency. 
* Detect agent behavior on LLMs.txt, [Agents.md](http://Agents.md), and all webpages. 
* Auto-triage your sitemap, flag any SEO or brand inconsistencies, and fix.

This is made possible because of Letterpress-1’s architecture. We use a mixture of state-of-the-art models, our own fine-tuned models for specific tasks (e.g. headline writing), brand evals, and built-in infrastructure for growth problems. 

When compared to Claude Code or Codex, Letterpress-1 produces better, tasteful outputs. This is made possible by orchestrating SOTA models like Claude and Codex, using fine-tuned small models for common growth tasks, and running evals to ensure brand consistency. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125321&key=user_uploads/190672/b29a32a4-95e6-4a60-93a7-6ab4bc5471bd)

However, this is just the tip of the iceberg. Letterpress-1 will also plan futuristic growth strategies to win agentic traffic and create workspaces to build them. This is made possible by Letter’s pre-built primitives, a new class of infrastructure for growth. These include: 

* Proofs, evidence chains that verify customer usage, renewals, and outcomes to build agent conviction. 
* Simulations, automatic mirror applications to enable agents to safely try solutions before committing to buying them. 
* Benches, self-hosted, reproducible benchmarks with open source, independent governance. 
* Kernels, writing pipelines to produce credible copy to appeal to agents. 
* Phantoms, automatic publications to test agentic growth strategies in a sandbox. 
* And more!

Letter makes prompting changes incredibly easy. After being installed in your build, authenticated users can prompt Letterpress-1 directly from their public web application, sharing visual brand context without manually taking a screenshot.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

launches.body:
Hey everyone ! We're [Mathilde](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mathilde-bouilloux/) and [Joseph](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joseph-risson/), co-founders of [Viraj Aero](https://www.viraj-aero.com/).

**TL;DR**

Viraj Aero (YC F26) builds a gas turbine that gives data centers both their power and their cooling water, with no water connection and no wait for the grid. We already have over 1.3 GW of demand under letters of intent, and one of the world's largest engine manufacturers is a paying customer. 

Burning natural gas produces water, and Viraj captures it. Our proprietary system recovers water directly from the turbine exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest goes back into the turbine as steam, delivering 40% more power with the same amount of fuel, with emissions low enough to get permits approved in weeks instead of months.

We first built this turbine for aviation and after a series of ground tests, it is now being integrated into an aircraft. Designed to fly, it can run anywhere : on the ground, it becomes a compact, standalone unit that installs even in the desert.

▶️ <https://youtu.be/XZghETY1lV4>

**The Problem**

AI data centers need two things: power and water. Today they can't get either fast enough.

* The grid can't keep up. New data centers are told to wait years for a connection.
* Water is running out. Two-thirds of new data centers are going up in water-stressed regions. Communities push back, permits stall, projects die.

 

**Our Solution**

We build a compact, standalone gas turbine genset with one twist: it makes its own water.

Burning gas produces water. Our patented water recovery system captures it from the turbine exhaust, and that water does two jobs:

1. It cools the data center. No water connection needed.
2. It goes back into the turbine as steam. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel and up to 99% lower NOx emissions, so permits take weeks instead of years.

Our first product is a 10 MW genset built from stacked turbine modules: redundant by design, and expandable as your data center grows. 

**Why Us**

We're aerospace engineers from GE, Rolls-Royce, Safran and Formula 1. Operations are led by the former Managing Director of GE Aerospace France, and our CTO has built a complete engine from scratch. Joseph is a Supaero turbomachinery engineer (Ascendance, Beyond Aero YC W22). Mathilde has developed 120+ MW of power projects (Neoen, VINCI, Banque des Territoires).

**Born to Fly**

As aerospace engineers, we first built this turbine for aviation and after a series of ground tests, it is now being integrated into an aircraft. Designed to fly, it can run anywhere : on the ground, it becomes a compact, standalone unit that installs even in the desert. 

**Our Ask**

If any of these are you, we'd love to talk:

* Data center developers and hyperscalers who need firm on-site power for 2028+
* Neoclouds and energy teams building in water-stressed regions
* Gas turbine packagers and operators who want more power and lower NOx from their existing fleet

👉 [mathilde.bouilloux@viraj-aero.com](mailto:mathilde@viraj-aero.com) and [joseph.risson@viraj-aero.com](mailto:joseph@viraj-aero.com)

**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.
one_liner: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xtZgwxJMQeA>

**The Problem**

AI demand is driving a massive buildout of power and compute capacity, but the supply chain behind it hasn’t kept up. A developer can have financing, land, and customers lined up, then still wait years for the transformers and switchgear that energize the site. Every week of delay can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars in lost revenue.

This equipment comes from a small number of manufacturers, many of them booked out for years. Developers often end up coordinating several suppliers at once, and the whole project waits on whichever one delivers last.

**Our Solution**

Applied Kinetics builds transformers, switchgear, generators, and cooling systems to each project’s specifications, and owns every order from spec to site. Our AI agents run the work in between: reviewing specs, scheduling production, tracking every order, and catching delays before they reach your schedule. 

1. **Share your requirements.** Send us your project’s specs and timeline. Our agents review them and schedule production across our manufacturing network in the United States, Europe, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific, wherever the build can start soonest.
2. **We build to your specs.** We manage design approvals and production. Our agents track every milestone, follow up with the factory floor, and flag slips early.
3. **We deliver and support.** We handle export, customs, independent QA near your site, freight, and post-delivery service.

Because production runs across our whole network, each build starts wherever there’s capacity, not at the back of a multi-year queue.

Hey YC! We're Finn and Brison, the founders of Capveon (YC F26).

**Capveon is AI for finding, understanding, and winning government work for manufacturers and contractors.**

Across America, thousands of public infrastructure projects are planned, designed, and built every year. Water treatment plants, highways, power systems, industrial facilities, and everything in between.

Behind these projects are thousands of businesses competing to make them happen. Manufacturers supplying equipment, distributors connecting buyers and suppliers, and contractors doing the work.

But finding and winning this work is surprisingly difficult.

Project information is scattered across federal, state, and local agencies, engineering firms, procurement portals, capital improvement plans, and technical specifications. By the time a project goes out to bid, months or even years of planning and specification decisions may have already happened.

And finding a project is only half the battle.

Teams still have to sift through hundreds of pages of technical specifications, figure out whether their products or capabilities are relevant, track changes and addendums, and coordinate with engineers, suppliers, and contractors to put together a winning bid.

**We're building Capveon to make that entire process easier.**

Capveon uses AI to help teams:

* **Find:** Discover relevant government projects, including opportunities years before they go out to bid.
* **Understand:** Analyze engineering specifications, bid documents, and project requirements to identify where their products and capabilities fit.
* **Win:** Track opportunities, stay on top of project changes, and coordinate the information needed to pursue work all the way through award.

We're starting with manufacturers and contractors in critical infrastructure, particularly water and wastewater, heavy civil construction, and industrial projects.

Longer term, we see the same problems across energy, defense, and other industries where complex technical requirements, fragmented information, and long procurement cycles make winning work difficult.

Our goal is simple: help the companies building the physical world spend less time searching for information and more time winning work.

**The future won't build itself.**

Check us out at <https://capveon.ai>

If you're a manufacturer, distributor, or contractor pursuing government projects, we'd love to talk!

launches.body:
**Cardinal Square is building AI-native schools**, starting unaccredited with an after-school writing class before building full, accredited schools. We think education is going to look very different in a few years; not a world without teachers, but one where great educators and AI work side by side to deliver personalized education to every student.

**What we’re building:**

<https://youtu.be/ONdF7YJiUxs>

First, we build AI teachers that read every step of a kid’s work, remember how that kid learns, and adapt to them every day. Our goal is an AI that teaches as well as the best human tutor.

Then we take the programs families already pay hundreds a month for (tutoring centers, writing schools, daily practice programs) and rebuild them around our AI teacher, so every family gets personalized education for a fraction of the price. It’s the same ritual families trust from Kumon or a writing school, with the AI teacher doing the teaching.

**The program:**

Today we’re launching our first class, an after-school writing program for grades 3–8. Thirty minutes a day, one polished essay a week, guaranteed.

Here’s a week for Thomas, a 5th grader in the program.

Every day, Thomas reads and writes for thirty minutes with his AI teacher. He picks a topic, gathers ideas, outlines, drafts, revises, and finishes. The AI teacher reads every line, remembers what he keeps getting wrong, and guides him until he fixes it himself. It never writes a word for him.

Every week, he finishes an essay for his portfolio, and his parents get a progress report on what he worked on, what he practiced, and what comes next.

Every month, his parents meet with an academic advisor to review his progress and plan the next one.

It’s exactly what a $300-a-month writing tutor does, for $29 a month.

**About us:**

Bryan is a second-time YC founder who dropped out of Berkeley, and Jai worked on ML at Snowflake and dropped out of UT Austin.

We’ve been best friends since middle school, and through the years we’ve started businesses, published research, run a college consulting service, and worked on advocacy together.

We both grew up in Asian American communities where Kumon and after-school tutoring were the norm, and later tutored students ourselves. Cardinal Square is our take on how after-school learning should work.

**Sign up today:** <https://cardinalsquare.com/>

Bryan & Jai

launches.body:
We’re building unmanned cargo airplanes to fly freight to every one of America’s 5,000 public-use airports, and to resupply the military where a crewed flight is too costly or too dangerous.

Our scaled composite prototype already takes off, flies a route, and lands on its own. We designed, built, and flew it in under two months.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/b8b7c4b6-95ca-4d38-b5c7-038b5095bb3a)
[ ](https://youtu.be/RPzu5FBxUgg)
I ([Kush Agarwal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kushhansagarwal/)) spent four years at UCLA building autonomous drones, then got my pilot’s license flying out of small airports across California. All these airports have a short runway with a few Cessnas.

The US has about 5,000 public-use airports like this, and almost every American lives within 30 miles of one. Almost all of them see nothing but general aviation, and they make a great spot for autonomous cargo airplanes.

[Arvin Singh](https://linkedin.com/in/arvin-singh-b0b1a7240?utm_source=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=member_ios) has designed and built airplanes for 10 years and has won international aircraft design and flight competitions, where you win by carrying the most payload on the lightest airframe. 

Airplanes transport $8.3 trillion of goods a year, a third of world trade by value, but in the US that network stops at a few hundred airports. Only about 520 are certified for airline service. Past that, everything moves by truck.

The military has a similar problem. In Afghanistan, one soldier or contractor was killed or wounded for every 24 fuel convoys. Contested logistics, disaster relief, and remote resupply all need cargo flown where a crewed flight is too expensive, too risky, or impossible to staff.

We are making it possible for packages to move autonomously, and it starts by building an aircraft fit for the job.

**Solution**

We’re designing cargo aircraft from scratch with no one on board. With no cockpit, seats, or life support, the whole fuselage carries cargo.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/72b04b12-3bc3-47a8-accf-68ead30e2c88)

Our first aircraft will be a purpose-built airframe under 1,320 lb, designed from day one for proposed Part 108 rules. That gives us a path to commercial cargo flights in years, not a decade.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/f5b1a505-a74e-48db-9dfa-fb984e68e66f)

We start on the routes regional carriers fly today: feeder flights from integrator hubs to small airports. The same platform serves defense resupply, delivering urgent cargo into constrained environments without putting a crew at risk.

**What we have built**

We have a self-flying aircraft and a full autonomy stack. Our aircraft take off, fly a route, and land with no pilot in the loop. We built the airframe, autopilot, perception, and ground software in-house.

**What’s next**

* **By Q1 2027:** Fly a retrofitted small airplane fully autonomously, with no one on board controlling it. This proves our autonomy stack on a real certified airframe.
* **By Q1 2028:** Build and fly our clean-sheet cargo aircraft, followed by commercial operations.

The same autonomy stack scales up to larger cargo aircraft and defense missions.

The end state is fully autonomous airports, where aircraft load, launch, fly, land, and turn around with no humans in the operation. Connected together, those airports form a network that moves freight around the clock. We believe autonomous aircraft will become the backbone of how the country moves goods.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/8080f195-f492-4318-bf54-6a4021b9ca2c)

**Our asks**

Introductions to

* **Feeder program leads** at FedEx, UPS, and DHL and other carriers
* **Shippers moving urgent, high-value goods by air** such as medical supplies, aircraft parts, semiconductors
* **Defense logistics** stakeholders such as military bases, units, or elsewhere in the Department of War working on logistics

name: Taan.ai
long_description:
Taan builds foundation music models that do what you tell them to, when you tell them to. We're starting with music for video. Give Taan a video and it watches it, then composes an original score that follows the emotion and timing of every cut. If the scene is tense for 10 seconds and then turns happy, the music changes at that exact moment. You get back a fully mixed .mp4. Agents and apps call Taan through our API, so any video tool can add scored, synced music with one call. 

Today's music models can make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask for "violin at exactly the 11th second" and they usually skip it. We trained Taan from the ground up for control. 

We measured Taan on prompt adherence and instruction success. And against every leading model we tested, Taan was at least 4x better.  

We work with teams building video agents, ad and creative tools, micro-dramas and games. We're musicians and ML researchers. Adithya (CEO) comes from eight generations of Indian classical musicians, tours as a metal guitarist, has done music ML research since 2023, and has filed two patents on music generation architectures. Devansh (CTO) did signal-processing research at IIT Kanpur and was previously an ML engineer at American Express.

launches.tagline: Foundation music models that do what you tell them to, when you tell them to.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Taan is a foundation music model built for control and multimodal inputs. Hum a melody, name exact notes, or give it an image, a MIDI file, a video, or a script, and Taan creates music fit perfectly to your context and timing. Apps and agents can use it with one API call.

VIDEO:[ https://youtu.be/-pt7OGoNZ7g](https://youtu.be/-pt7OGoNZ7g)

**The problem**

Today's music models can make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask to "bring in the violin at exactly the 11th second " expecting the music to exactly fit your video and they usually skip it. You end up regenerating over and over and hoping one take fits. That's fine for a background playlist, but not when you have a specific idea in your head or a video that needs music to change at an exact moment.\
\
 **What Taan does**

* Anything is the prompt. Taan can process any multimodal input to make the right music for its context. 
* Ideal for music in video. Taan can watch your video, finds the cuts and the mood, and composes a score that fits in one shot.
* Direct it in plain English, or don't. "Make the first 8 seconds tense, pause for 2 seconds, then turn uplifting." Or send no instructions and let Taan decide from your input.
* Granular control and edits. "Make the violin happier and start it 3 seconds earlier." Taan changes just that part and keeps the rest of the track.
* Yours to use. Every track is original, comes with downloadable stems, and is trained on 100% licensed music.
* Built for agents. Video tools and agents call Taan through our API and MCP and get synced, mixed music back.

**Taan v1-preview is tuned for orchestral and cinematic music today, with more genres on the way.**

**The benchmarks**\
We gave leading music models 250 timing prompts, like "introduce the violin at exactly the 11th second" or "bring in the drums after 5 seconds, then pause for 2 seconds at the 10th second." Every model was scored with the same detectors and the same tolerance:

* Instruction success: Taan 80.1%, ElevenLabs 28.9%, Google Lyria 23.9%, Suno 22.0%
* Timed events landing within ±500ms: Taan 73.2%, ElevenLabs 12.8%, Google Lyria 8.6%, Suno 6.8%
* Instructed events left out entirely: Taan 0%. The other models mostly skip the event instead of placing it.

Full results:[ https://taan.ai/research/control-benchmarks/](https://taan.ai/research/control-benchmarks/)

**The team**\
 We're musicians and ML researchers.

* Adithya (CEO): comes from eight generations of Indian classical musicians and has toured as a metal guitarist. He has done music ML research since 2023 and has filed two patents on music generation architectures.
* Devansh (CTO): Stats/DS major and signal-processing research at IIT Kanpur, previously an ML engineer at American Express.

**Our ask**

* Try it: make your own track at[ ](http://app.taan.ai/)[app.taan.ai](http://app.taan.ai). Input anything and see what comes back or make music for a video you’re currently editing 
* Building a DAW, creator tool, video agent, ad tool, micro-drama app or game? We'd love to talk. Email [founders@taan.ai](mailto:founders@taan.ai).
* Got a video that needs a score? Send it over and we'll make the music for free.

launches.tagline: Real-time steering for AI agents
launches.body:
**TL:DR;** Stacktrace supervises agents used by your employees and customers. It detects risks across security, infrastructure and cost and lets teams block unsafe actions, require approval or steer agents.

<https://youtu.be/2FCDlUCL_KE>

### **Why we built this**

Agents are moving from tools employees use at the terminal to systems they delegate entire business workflows to. As agents take on longer horizon tasks and run unattended, they make decisions without someone reviewing them. 

The same challenge extends to personal agents that customers use to interact with your business. These agents need enough access to get things done without doing anything the customer or business hasn’t approved.

**Just because an agent has permission to do something doesn’t mean it should.**

Today companies manage this risk by restricting what agents can access or which employees can use them. But these restrictions limit the impact agents can have. We think businesses should be able to give agents more autonomy, with visibility and controls into their actions. 

That’s why we built Stacktrace.

### **What Stacktrace does**

Stacktrace supervises agent sessions in real time, detects actions that violate user intent or company policy, and can block them, require approval, or steer the agent back on track.

**See:** Understand what agents are doing, which tools they use, and what they cost. Detect sensitive data exposure, destructive infrastructure changes, and stuck runs

**Control:** Set policies for plugins, MCP servers, and skills. Block unapproved or vulnerable components and apply token budgets across model vendors.

**Steer:** Block unsafe actions before they execute, require approval, or steer the agent toward a safer way to finish the task. 

Stacktrace extends this approach to customers’ agents like Muse and Instinct, interacting with your business. It sits in front of your customer-facing MCP server, enforces customer permissions, and requires explicit confirmation for consequential actions.

### **Who we are**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126235&key=user_uploads/3627108/68b56ce9-7bfc-47af-acc8-5a46b300e64a)

We’ve spent our careers building infrastructure, security, and platforms for systems where failures have real consequences.

[Vinod](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vinodkone) led Apache Mesos, the open-source infrastructure used by companies including Apple, SpaceX, Netflix, Uber, and Airbnb. He previously led engineering teams at Harness, Twilio, Twitter, and Mesosphere.

[Micheal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michealb) led infrastructure, security, and AI platforms at Airtable, and previously led developer platform and cloud infrastructure organizations at Databricks, Pinterest, and Twitter.

[Prasanth](https://www.linkedin.com/in/prasanthganta) spent 15 years at Amazon, building foundational services across AWS and Alexa, and GenAI systems at Amazon Ads.

### **Our ask**

If you run agents with access to sensitive data or production systems, we’d love to show you Stacktrace.

Book a demo at <https://stacktrace.ai>

name: Altair Health
long_description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

launches.body:
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI agents faster and keep them secure in production.

**TL;DR: For regulated companies building their own agents, Armorer finds real security issues in those agents and fixes them without interrupting the business.**

“The problem I have with most security solutions is they come along and give me another problem to go and fix. You’ve actually solved the problem.” Gaetan Licci, Director of Engineering, Just Eat Takeaway

**Security and engineering leaders in companies building their own agents: book a demo** → https://armorer-labs-inc.cal.com/armorer-labs/launch-demo · founders@armorerlabs.com

https://youtu.be/fkqdK47PEeM

## Team

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS.

- Daniel Begimher (CEO) has worked in security since 2012. He led the development and security of AWS’s first customer-facing AI security agent, scaling to 100k+ customers, and created ASH, an open-source security scanner with 200K+ monthly clones.
- Cristian Leo (CTO) led AI security science at AWS, training ML and AI models for cyber applications. He has published novel research in the AI security space and has open-sourced more than 30 machine-learning models from first principles.

Together we published several papers on AI security, including SIR-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating AI security agents, and ThreatForest, our Black Hat USA 2026 talk on AI threat modeling from source code.

## The problem

Earlier this year, researchers found a security flaw in a fintech's spreadsheet AI agent. One line of hidden white text made the agent send a company's confidential financials to an outside server, with no approval step.

Then, in July, OpenAI’s agents broke out of their sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face’s servers. Neither agent was broken. Each did what agents do: read whatever is in front of it, follow instructions and finish the task.

At the same time, AI models are getting more and more capable of finding security issues. Anthropic’s Claude Mythos found thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities and developed exploits for many of them with no human steering. Attackers can point the same kind of models at your agents. This brings challenges to organizations that want to move fast and adopt more agentic capabilities.

But finding issues is only half the job: nearly 2 in 3 high-risk AI vulnerabilities go unresolved (Cobalt, 2026).

## How it works

1. **Detect.** Armorer scans your agent's code and maps what it can reach: its tools, permissions, identities and data.
2. **Assess.** Armorer simulates attacks to find the issues that are real.
3. **Fix.** Armorer generates the smallest fix as a PR or runtime protection policy. Armorer then shows the attack fails and the agent still does its job.
4. **Protect.** In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Onboarding takes under 30 minutes, and Armorer runs in your cloud or on-premises, including air-gapped environments. Your team approves each verified fix with one click. Every finding and fix is mapped to ISO/IEC 42001 and AIUC-1 controls, so the same work helps you prepare for certification.

## Why this is different

Armorer is the continuous security layer for rapidly evolving agent applications. It doesn’t just identify gaps; it fixes and verifies them. Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer flags it and fixes it, then verifies every fix against your real workflows, because a fix that breaks the business isn’t a fix.

“If modern AI were a powerful car, then agentic AI would be a powerful self-driving car whose decisions and outcomes could not be fully predicted in advance,” said Paul Vixie, an internet pioneer inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2014. “We can’t make agentic AI safe using detailed lists of what can and cannot be done, which is why Armorer Labs is working in terms of verifiable generalities. I’m happy to be one of Armorer’s advisors and investors.”

## Proof

Armorer’s detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks (Jayavibhav, deepset, S-Labs, xTRam1, jackhhao and Gretel). Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won’t feel the delay. High-risk AI findings take a median of 36 days to resolve (Cobalt, 2026). Armorer has a verified fix ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

Armorer vs. JEV benchmark:

https://youtu.be/OvSvxQ7LqI4

**Stop collecting findings. Start closing them without interrupting the business.**

**Book a demo:** https://armorer-labs-inc.cal.com/armorer-labs/launch-demo · founders@armorerlabs.com

launches.tagline: Rhem handles everything that doesn’t need a pair of hands, while keeping you in the loop.
launches.body:
## TLDR:

**Aging at home has a visibility problem. Small changes in health and routine can go unnoticed for weeks or months, until the first obvious sign is something serious. Rhem is a tabletop robot that helps families see those changes earlier, while giving parents the everyday support they need to stay independent longer. Rhem was designed with older adults in mind, but it’s for anyone who wants help getting things done and staying on top of their health.**

Preorders are open now at <https://rhem.ai>

<https://youtu.be/LnNPjpNq_uE>

## 

## The Problem

**At some point, you start paying attention to your parents differently.**

Maybe there was a scare. Maybe Mom missed an appointment. Maybe Dad sounds more tired. Or maybe nothing happened at all. You just start wondering whether everything is as fine as they say.

If you don’t live with them, you mostly get snapshots: a call, a text, a FaceTime.

**You don’t see the full day.**

You don’t know if routines are slipping, something is getting harder, or a small change is becoming a pattern.

**We learned this the hard way with my grandmother.**

Before her stroke, she was sleeping badly, talking less, and seemed unlike herself.

The signs were there. But my dad had a newborn and a full-time job. My grandfather was working too. Everyone cared, but no one saw the whole picture.

**We each saw pieces. No one put them together until something much bigger happened.**

## **How it works for your parents**

Rhem lives in the home and becomes the easiest way for your parent to get things done and keep track of their health.

They just need to say:

“Remind me after dinner.”

“When is my appointment?”

“Order our usual groceries.”

“Tell Jacob I need a ride tomorrow.”

Rhem can browse websites, make calls, manage reminders, answer questions, place supported orders, and follow up.

**If it doesn’t require a pair of hands, Rhem can probably handle it.**

They can also take supported wellness readings on Rhem, keep track of routines, and see how things change over time.

When something needs you, **Rhem brings you into the loop through the rhem connect app.** You can answer a question, add context, or help finish the task. **Help Rhem once, and it remembers how to do it next time.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/9adf4655-4900-4fe0-bdec-29e333c8a3dd)

## **How it works for families**

Your parent gets an assistant. **You get a clearer picture of how they’re doing.**

The Rhem app brings together health readings, routines, requests, completed tasks, and alerts. You can see what changed, what Rhem handled, and when you’re needed.

From anywhere, you can send reminders, leave voice messages, ask Rhem to check in, talk to your parent, or ask about information they’ve shared.

Over time, Rhem helps you spot patterns. **One bad night may mean nothing. A month of worse sleep, missed appointments, and changes in routine is something you want to know about.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/c7652236-3ca9-40a0-9ea8-d1e2160852fc)

## **Why we built Rhem**

**We’re a father-and-son team, and our family spent nearly two decades caring for loved ones at home.**

Before my grandmother had a stroke, there were signs that something was changing. She was sleeping badly, talking less, and seemed unlike herself. We all noticed pieces of it, but nobody had the full picture until much later.

My aunt had a different problem. A brain tumor left her with limited mobility, so a lot of everyday things depended on someone else being available. Making a call. Looking something up. Ordering something. Figuring out what needed to happen next.

A lot of the time, she didn’t need someone physically next to her. She needed someone who could help her get things done.

That’s where Rhem came from.

**We wanted something that could notice when things were changing, help with the everyday stuff, and bring family in when they were actually needed.**

The goal is simple: give our parents more independence, while letting us spend more time being their family instead of managing everything around them.

## **Team**

Jacob: Berkeley CS & DS, researcher at Berkeley AI Robotics Lab with a focus on full stack autonomous driving and edge computing, founding engineer at Mattoboard.

Huey: Executive leader with 30+ years of experience building smart hardware with embedded software at scale and leading global operations across North America, Europe, and Asia. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/2ae2c872-97c6-4ff3-9c05-dde53439c9b4)

## Why order now

If you’re ordering a Founding Edition, thank you.

We know we’re asking you to trust a new company and buy something for someone you care deeply about. We don’t take that lightly.

**Every Founding Edition includes:**

* **Founding Price of $1099 before our price increase to $1499 on Jan 20th**
* **1 x Halo Non-wearable Fall Detector ($80 Value)**
* **2 years of Rhem Plus included ($480 Value)**
* **2 x Merch Pack & Goodies**
* **Direct access to our team** for setup, questions, and feedback

**Thank you for being here at the beginning. We can’t wait for Rhem to start making your parents’ lives a little easier.**

Preorder now at: <https://rhem.ai>

**_Here's to more good years with the people who raised us. 💙_**

**— Jacob & Huey**

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Talos is building an early-warning platform that uses retrofittable sensors and machine learning to detect issues on critical power equipment before they cause multi-million dollar failures. 

**Video:** <https://youtu.be/E43rheBR8FI>  

**Problem**

America’s power grid is struggling:

* Power outages cost Americans over $125 billion just last year, and power failures have more than doubled since 2024.
* 75% of today’s power comes from machines operating past their intended lifespan. 
* With the rise of AI and rapid scaling of compute, demand for power has doubled in the past five years.

Despite this, most utilities still run their equipment till failure and rely on outdated monitoring systems, reacting to problems as they happen. 

**Our solution**

Talos deploys non-invasive, retrofittable sensors on power equipment and continuously monitors vibration, magnetic flux, temperature, and humidity. We learn what normal and faulty behavior looks like for your machine, allowing us to detect small issues before they become catastrophic failures.

With sensors deployed across 40+ assets, Talos is partnering with national laboratories, utilities and plant owners to monitor transformers, turbines, pumps, poles, and generators.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123793&key=user_uploads/3099707/8bebc26c-1b9d-43b7-9967-6f858a48ddeb)

Learn more at [talos-us.com](http://talos-us.com).

launches.tagline: Gene-editing made possible for all crops by delivering CRISPR inside a pollen grain, so breeders can actually use it to move distinct traits straight into crosses of their favorite varieties, saving years on their breeding campaigns.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125202&key=user_uploads/2808867/f1373c3e-730f-415e-88e5-bdb4f706ec87)

Creating a new fruit or vegetable variety through **breeding takes 8 - 16 years on average**: hoping for random mutations, then spending ages selecting the good ones. Since each **trait costs $3M**, only essential improvements get made. The industry is only scratching the surface of a **$40B potential royalty market in specialty crops**.

Get that under **8y**, and crops can ship new resistance genes faster than pathogens evolve around them, like patching security bugs faster than hackers can exploit them, so most of the **pesticides stop being needed**. Get that under **4y**, and crop development gets so fast and cheap that **new varieties can follow, or even set, consumer trends**, the way software went from multi-year releases to shipping new features every week.

Accessible genome sequencing and AI can now tell breeders what to aim for, not hope for, and **CRISPR** turns random mutations into chosen ones. From 2026, it's **legal** in 2/3 of the world. The problem is that **gene editing (CRISPR) really only works on corn and a few other crops**, because CRISPR has to go into a single stem cell that's then regrown into a whole plant. That took 14 years to figure out just for corn - the most capitalized crop.

Nitroduck skips the stem cell and **puts CRISPR into a pollen grain**; the grain pollinates a flower, and out comes an edited seed - seamlessly tapping into how breeders already work.

In the last 6 years, as 3M (Matej, Matúš and Miro), **we've engineered 4x more plants than the average plant scientist does in their whole career**. We've enabled gene editing in duckweed, Earth's fastest-growing and smallest plant, which **won us iGEM, the "Olympics of Biotech**," against 330 teams, including Ivy League schools.

**_We are killing Workday, SuccessFactors and Ashby_**

**TL;DR:** Lantern is an agentic recruiting platform. It runs on a world model of a billion professionals and a model of your own company's hiring taste, and its connected agents source, review applications, run interviews, schedule and report. 

**We processed 2M+ candidates for companies like [Crypto.com](http://Crypto.com), Hyatt, Baker McKenzie and Eight Sleep**. Try it at [lantern.md](http://lantern.md).

### <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XdEasqnED-M>

**Your hiring software knows nothing about the outside world and your company**

Workday, SuccessFactors and Ashby are systems of record. They don’t know who’s ready for a new job, where to find great people, or what makes someone right for your team. Recruiters carry that in their heads and browser tabs. When they leave, that knowledge leaves too.

**Lantern runs on two models:** 

**The world people model.** A talent map across a billion professionals, with career signals tracked live: role changes, launches, team moves, who is hiring. It knows talent density by company and who is genuinely exceptional.

**Your hiring model.** Built from your context, your interview notes and your whole hiring history. Every interview and every offer teaches it what your team values.

### **One brain, connected team of agents**

1. **Kickoff.** Lantern sits in on the kickoff call between the hiring manager and the recruiter, learns what the team values, and checks it against who the company has hired and rejected before.
2. **Sourcing.** With that taste, Lantern proactively starts sourcing: it searches a billion professionals, builds the shortlist, and drafts outreach for the recruiter to approve.
3. **Screening.** When candidates apply or reply, the same hiring context drives application review and the AI interviews, and Lantern books the next rounds around everyone’s calendars.
4. **Learning.** After every debrief and interview, the sourcing and screening criteria update, so the next search starts smarter than the last.
5. **Analytics.** Ask Lantern anything about your hiring pipeline without digging through dashboards or exporting data

Sourcing. Application review. AI interviews. Meeting intelligence. Complex scheduling. Analytics. All of it queryable from Slack and MCP. 

Teams can start with Lantern on top of their existing ATS, or replace it entirely.

name: Munito AI
long_description:
Munito is an open-model inference provider for Europe, private by default. Its API lets users choose their models and keep inference and storage in the EU. 
Founded by the former inference lead at Mistral AI, Munito is built on one belief: open and independent intelligence, both models and inference, is key to economic growth and prosperity.
one_liner: Open-model inference provider for Europe, private by default.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
I led inference at Mistral AI, where my team built its API and inference products, and I built Le Chat's Deep Research. Before that, I spent five years at Airbnb, where I built Hosting Services from scratch and grew it to become a global product.

At Mistral, we built everything in-house, because no independent European provider could handle our scale. I kept seeing the same thing: in Europe, inference is a side product. Cloud providers sell it next to their VMs, and model labs sell it for their own models. At the same time, open models became really good.

This is why I started Munito: the best open models, run in Europe, behind an API you already know how to use.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Companies in Europe want to use the best open models at scale, but they also need privacy and control over where their data is processed. Today it's hard to get both. Most large providers are not European, and EU processing is quite often an extra option instead of the default. There are few European providers, and many of them can't handle real scale.

And this problem grows every month. More and more sensitive data goes through AI models in products, agents and internal tools. Users and regulators ask where it's processed and stored, and companies don't want their AI to depend on one cloud or one model lab.

I saw this from inside at Mistral, where we had to build everything in-house. Munito gives companies open models at scale, with inference and storage in the EU and privacy by default: no data retention, no training on their data. Sovereignty, without running your own GPUs.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
I believe that open and independent intelligence, both models and inference, is key to economic growth and prosperity in the world and the region.

If Munito succeeds, anyone building with AI can run the best open models privately, in the region they choose, without depending on one cloud or one model lab. Munito rents GPUs across many vetted data centers and clouds, and we’re building a self-improving inference stack, so running open models gets faster and cheaper over time.

launches.body:
**TL;DR: Today we are introducing OpenLake, an inference platform that automatically post trains your models for you.**

Hi everyone! I’m [Arnav](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arnavbalyan/), excited to share [OpenLake](https://openlakehq.com/)!

**The Problem:**\
Foundation models are trained on the public world. What makes your company different, its data, its people, its customers' problems, is never seen by frontier models. Bringing that knowledge into a model has meant building an AI research lab. Compute, training infrastructure, evaluation, and a team to run all of it.\
\
This work does not end here. New user conversations constantly flow in and require constant data preparation, training, evaluation and deployment. OpenLake removes that cycle.\
\
**How it works:**\
Choose an open model such as DeepSeek V4 or GLM 5.3 and deploy it on OpenLake. Plug in your datasets, RL environments and data sources. OpenLake post trains the model continuously as new data arrives and serves the improved model in place. A/B test every new version against previous versions.\
\
**What you get:**\
Trained model checkpoints belong to you, ready to export and download. Better performance on the tasks you care about, not on public benchmarks. On average, OpenLake models cut serving costs in half.\
\
**Why we built it:**\
I'm Arnav, I built core infrastructure behind Uber’s data and AI systems, powering products used by millions of people. We soon realized models are usually not a problem, keeping them up to date efficiently is. Closing this gap should not require every company to build an AI research lab. So we built the platform that does it for them.\
\
**Bring your inference to OpenLake**

OpenLake is available today at [openlakehq.com](http://openlakehq.com). [Book a call](https://openlakehq.com/new-meeting) to reduce inference bills and improve model quality for your workloads. Teams running models in production can reach us at [arnav@openlakehq.com](mailto:arnav@openlakehq.com).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tQvVAS5eXk8>\
**Own your intelligence.**

launches.tagline: Solar + Battery systems set up with 1/100th of the labor anywhere in the world.
launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_QyDl8MW3IY>
\
The world is facing an unprecedented demand for energy through data centers, electrification across all industries, and broader economic growth. With the newfound demand, the supply of energy continues to lag behind.

For hardware R&D, infrastructure, and manufacturing, these challenges are compounded by the need for more space, pushing development toward remote land with limited infrastructure. Bringing power to these sites remains a bottleneck: large solar projects take years to build, require skilled crews that are already stretched thin, and face lengthy permitting processes. 

**Why Now**

* Electrification is accelerating across all industries (aerospace, logistics, humanoids, etc) and diesel is progressively less viable.
* By 2030, the world will need over 600 GW of new power, but interconnection times are at an all-time high and the industry faces a historic shortage of specialized labor.
* The levelized cost of energy of solar + BESS is now cheaper than grid power across the country.

So we are building rapidly deployed modular power systems in a box for communities and businesses in remote regions that require dependable scaled energy. 

**What it does**

Micora’s end-to-end solution includes site design, installation, and maintenance across the life cycle of the energy system. 

Once a customer orders a Micora system, we deliver a containerized set of robots, solar blocks, and a battery energy storage system on site. Our drone surveys the area, virtually marks the site layout, and kicks off the installation process. The forklift robots kick off a 24/7 schedule of picking and placing solar blocks while continuously hot-swapping batteries till completion. 

Our design enables us to deliver scaled reliable energy at light speed where no one else can.

**Our Ask**

* **We’d like to meet operators of deep tech startups, remote operations, fuel/energy-sensitive operations and underserved regions/communities to better understand your needs.**
* **We’d like to meet other energy generation companies in wind, fuel cells, and even small scale combustion hardware to make our network offering more resilient.**

name: Mirrors
long_description:
Production AI agents keep making the same mistakes. The usual fix is another line in the system prompt. Over time, the agent carries instructions for dozens of situations, even when it's doing something simple, and every correction becomes another thing to maintain.

Mirrors helps developers maintain production agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections. Mirrors surfaces recurring mistakes across your production runs. You write a correction, choose the situations where it applies, and preview which past conversations it would have reached. Once activated, Mirrors adds it to your agent only in those situations. You can then compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helped. Unlike skills, the agent doesn't decide what to load. The scope you set does.

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework, and your application keeps control of its model calls and tools.

We're building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents.
one_liner: Fix recurring AI agent mistakes with real-time guidance

launches.title: Mirrors: Fix recurring AI agent mistakes with real-time guidance
launches.tagline: Stop playing whack-a-mole with your agents
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re [Aryan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aisinghal) and [Aditya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aditya-gupta-6a771a231/), the founders of [Mirrors](https://mirrors.dev?utm_source=launchyc). Mirrors helps developers maintain production AI agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections they can preview, apply, and measure.

<https://youtu.be/pC8PkI86RGE>

### Your system prompt is becoming a history of everything your agent got wrong.

Your support agent repeats troubleshooting steps the customer already tried. You add a line to the prompt. It keeps pushing a retention offer after the customer declines. You add another.

After enough fixes, the agent is carrying instructions for dozens of situations, even when it’s doing something simple.

As those corrections spread across prompts and skills, there’s more to maintain: where each instruction belongs, which accounts it applies to, and whether it actually helps.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124031&key=user_uploads/3174410/cd6215f1-3b79-4ec5-998d-c420a31dbcc8)

_That’s the agent in our launch video: covered in sticky notes, trying to follow them all._

### How Mirrors works

Mirrors surfaces recurring mistakes across your production runs. Say your support agent keeps restarting troubleshooting instead of building on what the customer has already tried. In Mirrors, you write a correction:

> _Before suggesting troubleshooting, check which steps the customer has already completed. Acknowledge the results and continue from there._

Choose the situations where it applies, then preview which past conversations it would have reached. Once activated, Mirrors adds it to your agent only in those situations. Afterward, compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helped.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124031&key=user_uploads/3174410/6ee1d95c-0fa9-4168-aca3-dd3c848b776b)

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. When requirements change, you update one correction instead of juggling versions of your entire prompt.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124031&key=user_uploads/3174410/cfe19c14-61e8-4540-9177-5ca4c710d518)

Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework. Your application keeps control of its model calls and tools.

### Why we're building this

One of our design partner's agent hit 75 errors editing a single travel guide. The rule telling it to stop was already in its prompt four times. More instructions weren't the fix. Getting the right one to the agent at the right moment was.

We're building Mirrors so improving your agent doesn't leave you with an ever-growing collection of prompt patches to maintain.

### The team

* **Aryan (CEO):** Published six AI/ML research papers in high school, including at NeurIPS and EMNLP. Previously did ML research at UT Austin and UCSB.
* **Aditya (CTO):** Built computer vision and agent workflows at multiple startups serving thousands of sessions per week at sub-second latency.

### Our ask

Tired of playing whack-a-mole with your agent? Bring us one failed run.

[**Book a time with us**](https://cal.com/aryan-singhal/mirrors) or email [**devs@runmirrors.com**](mailto:devs@runmirrors.com). We’ll work through what went wrong and how Mirrors can help.

launches.tagline: Asakana translates texts, calls and handwritten notes from restaurants directly into existing ERPs, including orders, credit memos, returns. Restaurants and distributors change nothing.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Food distributors still receive orders from old-school restaurants via text, phone and handwritten notes, and a rep manually retypes every one into a legacy ERP. Asakana reads those messages and does the entry automatically. Restaurants and reps keep working the way they do today. In production at a US food distributor.

<https://youtu.be/XONUcUsuxSY>

**The problem**

A food distributor runs on messages. Restaurants order by text, phone, WhatsApp, a photo of a handwritten note, often not in English. They report an incorrect, short, or damaged delivery the same way. A rep or an admin staff member reads every one of those messages and enters it by hand into an ERP or spreadsheet: the order, the return, the credit memo.

One of our customers receives about 60 orders a day this way, some over 75 lines. A sales rep reads each one, works out which of 10 salmon items "salmon" means, and types it into the ERP line by line. Then the credit requests from yesterday's deliveries, each one a return and a credit note typed in by hand. Reps there spend about 30% of their day on this.

Apps and portals tried to replace this manual work, but old school restaurants and distributor’s sales reps never learned them, so the retyping remained. The US has more than 27,000 food distributors and their 100,000 sales reps and back-office staff suffer from painful manual work like this.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122477&key=user_uploads/2103989/75737558-db33-4f61-b265-2230e25c9ef6)

**What Asakana does**

Asakana does the manual work so reps can focus on selling. Restaurants and reps keep working the way they do today. Three steps, the same for every workflow:

* Read messy information: spreadsheets, PDFs, handwritten notes, and messages, down to the photo of the handwritten invoice a driver brings back from a delivery.
* Understand your business: customer habits, product shorthand, and unwritten rules. "Same as last Friday" is order SO-78211. "AC" means albacore tuna. Salmon is always skin-on.
* Connect to your systems: work directly with your existing ERP and tools.

Anything unclear goes to a person before it goes in. The rep gets one email notification per task: what was entered and anything to keep an eye on.

Workflows we automate this way:

* Order entry
* Credit memos and returns
* Upsell suggestions
* Cutoff reminders
* Past-due collections
* PO creation
* New customer discovery

Chinese, Korean, Spanish, Japanese: read the way they were written, with the shorthand and nuance of each language, and matched to the item in the English catalog.

Anything that moves by hand from a message into a system or a spreadsheet, we automate.

**The team**

We're Yudai and Ben. Yudai was a fisherman and a seafood distributor (Mitsubishi Corporation), where he did this manual work himself, then at McKinsey transformed companies that still ran on it. Ben spent 8 years at Google as a senior AI research engineer on Project Mariner and Gemini.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122477&key=user_uploads/2103989/00516563-7bf8-455c-8256-40d8ce2b5667)

launches.tagline: Bryel helps your company to build an in-house AI lab, then gives you the software to train and continually improve your own models.
launches.body:
Hey YC, **we’re on a mission to build a billion models, trained by you.** We’re [Kevin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/miaok/) and [Frankie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lifrankie/), co-founders of Bryel.

## TL;DR

**We’re your cracked AI training team, on demand.** We partner with your company, build your in-house model training capabilities, and leave behind Bryel Foundry, our software that makes model development and continual improvement 10x simpler. Think of it as your in-house AI lab. We’ve trained models for Apple, Framer, and F500s.

**Ask:** Considering training your AI model? Email [frankie@bryel.ai](mailto:frankie@bryel.ai)\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LsVUbDIG2RY>

## Problem

**When you train a model for everyone, you train it for no one.** 

Frontier models are incredibly capable generalists, but they fall short on the specifics. So teams build harnesses to work around the edges and cover the gaps: more prompting, more harness infra, more retries, and stricter evals.

Eventually, quality plateaus. We’ve met many teams that are buried in harness work, layering on more and more infrastructure and patches to keep things working. That’s where model training is worth a serious look. With recent advancements in the open-source ecosystem and post-training methods, a few thousand good examples can produce a model that beats frontier APIs on your task, and it’s cheaper to run and deployable on-prem.

The challenge has always been that training is slow, expensive, experimental, and requires specialized knowledge. That’s where we help.

## Solution

We forward deploy into your company, to help you set up your AI model training capabilities end-to-end, and hand off software to help you maintain and continually improve your AI models. Our product, the Bryel Foundry, has been built from everything we learned doing this by hand, many times over.

Models we commonly help train:

* **OCR/Classification Models** that run 20x faster.
* **Search & Embedding models** that cost 5x less. 
* **Long horizon agent models** that match frontier performance at 5-8x lower cost

**One more thing,** we have a second ask. If you know companies that have a lot of proprietary data and no ML team (think insurers, logistics, healthcare, legal)? We'd love a 20-minute intro. We're not looking to sell, just to learn. Happy to return the favor.

launches.title: Hopper – Fast, open-source inference for real-time agents
launches.tagline: Hopper trains open-weight models on your production traces, then serves and improves them against your live traffic.
launches.body:
Hey YC, we are an inference company that works exclusively with realtime agent companies.

We do two things for our customers today:

1. **Optimize inference** to make voice agents an order of magnitude faster and cost-efficient.
2. **Post-train open source STT, TTS, and speech LLMs** on your production calls, then serve and improve them against your live traffic.

## **⚙️ Models**

We currently provide the following models:

1. **LLM:** Gemma 4 31B at 80ms TTFT (7x faster and 4x less expensive than GPT 4.1)
2. **TTS:** Qwen 3 TTS at 150ms TTFA (10x less expensive than ElevenLabs)
3. **STT:** Nemotron 3.5 ASR (2x faster, 8x less expensive than Deepgram Nova-3)

Real-time voice is one of the most latency-sensitive applications today. Voice agent companies already use techniques like interim STT transcripts, TTS caching, and filler greetings to shave off hundreds of milliseconds. Reducing LLM latency from 800 ms to under 100 ms would be a step change.

## **🤝 How we work with you**

Here is our typical working pipeline with a voice agent company:

1. **Inference:** Optimize and deploy the model in required regions. We continually monitor the deployment to hit a 98% KV cache hit rate and catch tool and reasoning leakages.
2. **Evals:** Sometimes you’d want something better than the base models. First step here is building evals. You give us your system prompt, then we sit with your engineers and co-design your first eval.
3. **Post-train:** For LLMs this looks like improved instruction following and better tool calling; for TTS this can improve pronunciation of specific words like a company name, slower speed for alphanumerics, or even something broader like "I want my TTS to be more emotive and happier."

## **💪 Our Team**

Pavan ran voice inference at Salient powering millions of calls a day. Jashwanth wrote inference kernels for Quest 3 at Meta Reality Labs.

## **🌲 What we believe**

**1. Voice models are going to be priced out of the compute market.** An STT or TTS model is less than 2B parameters, which is 2GB at FP8 precision. An H100 and a B200 have 80GB and 192GB of HBM respectively. More than 95% of memory is unutilized. You might have seen in the news recently that memory shortages are spiking up prices of electronics, including PS5s; it's the same HBM. Of course, this can't go on forever, and the more lucrative LLM workloads will occupy the frontier compute, leading to two things:

* Voice models will move to cheaper GPUs like L4, RTX 3090s, and Jetsons.
* Cost per hour of STT and TTS will fall 100x by 2028.

**2. Currently, less than 5% of voice workloads are on open source. This'll be north of 90% by 2028.** Why is that?

* Latency is one of the persistent technical challenges in voice, and you'd get 5-10x lower latencies by using smaller open source models.
* Your lead qualification bot doesn't need the capacity to do frontier math; it needs to be good at following instructions in your prompt. This means every company will have its own voice models that are exactly tuned to perform well in their domain.
* We're hearing from many of our customers that long-term they are uncomfortable sending their traffic to ElevenLabs et al. This is due to  the fact that ElevenLabs, Cartesia, and Deepgram have their own voice agent products, which directly compete with their customers. From a customer's POV, they are funding their competitors with millions in revenue and their data.

## **🙏 Asks**

If you know a voice agent company or a use case that benefits from this work, let's talk. [https://withhopper.com/talk-to-us](https://withhopper.com/talk-to-us?from=hero)

We’re starting with human drivers. As autonomous trucks become available on our routes, we intend to put them to work within an established freight network.

Founder Harpreet Dhaliwal started running his family’s trucking business at 19 and has generated more than $7M in trucking revenue. The tools he built for that operation became TrueMile.

For recurring truckload freight and partnerships: harpreet@truemile.ai
one_liner: AI-native trucking company

founders.title: Founder/CEO

launches.title: TrueMile: The AI-native trucking company
launches.tagline: Plan the fleet. Book the freight. Dispatch the driver. All run by AI.
launches.body:
Hi, I’m Harpreet, founder of TrueMile.

**TL;DR:** TrueMile is an AI-native trucking company. Starting with our own fleet, we use AI to plan loads, find freight, negotiate with brokers, and dispatch drivers. Over four months, AI-selected loads earned 17% more revenue per mile than the market average on dry van and 8% on reefer. Our trucks also averaged 10% more miles per month than the industry average.

**The problem: fleets leave money on the road when planning and execution can’t keep up**

Fleet profitability depends on which contracts to take and how to fill the empty legs between them. The highest-paying load can leave a truck empty or unavailable for a better commitment tomorrow.

In practice, planners are forced to react to today’s market one load at a time, rather than optimize margins across the fleet. They do this while handling calls, delays, cancellations, and breakdowns. Every handoff between planning, dispatch, brokers, and drivers adds another chance for delay or miscommunication.

**How TrueMile works**

<https://youtu.be/MRmZpD42ov4>

TrueMile combines mathematical optimization with AI agents that execute the plan:

* **Optimize the whole fleet.** Evaluate contracts, load assignments, and backhauls together, weighing market forecasts, revenue, costs, available hours, and driver commitments.
* **Source and negotiate freight.** Search load boards and contact brokers in parallel to secure loads that fit the plan.
* **Execute and adapt.** Dispatch drivers, keep customers updated, and rework assignments when plans change.A person approves every load and signs every rate confirmation.

A person still approves every load.

**The result**

launches.title: Antropi Robotics | CNC parts in days, from autonomous factories
launches.tagline: Turning your designs into precision metal parts in days
launches.body:
👋 **Hey Everyone!** I’m Naman. My best friend Shubh and I are building **Antropi Robotics**.

**We make inspected CNC parts for hardware teams.** Our first factory is live and already shipping parts to customers with **lead times under 7 days**.

**Our goal:** a network of autonomous factories across the US, making and delivering parts locally in as little as 24 hours.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V4Ll5DZSP0I>

## ⚙️ Problem

Before starting Antropi, I spent six months running my dad’s CNC machining business in India. The biggest lesson was simple: **automating the machine is not the same as automating the factory.**

A CNC machine can cut automatically. But someone still has to plan the job, load the machine, inspect the part, and decide what to do when something goes wrong.

For hardware teams, this becomes a familiar cycle. Prepare drawings. Request quotes. Go back and forth on manufacturing details. Wait for a production slot. Wait for the parts.

**Every week spent waiting is a design iteration you don’t get before your next demo.**

Adding a robot to load the machine fixes one step. It does not tell the factory whether the part is correct, or what should happen next.

## 🤖 Solution

We’re building **dark factories: autonomous factories designed to run 24/7.** Our Factory OS connects job planning, CNC machines, robots, and inspection into one system.

Software turns CAD into machining programs and checks them in simulation, with an engineer approving them before production.

Robots load and unload. Machines cut. **Every part is inspected.**

Inspection feeds back into production, so the system can make supported corrections or stop the machine before a problem repeats.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123265&key=user_uploads/2771579/275935ea-e97d-40e7-b0fa-cc9d04977486)

For you, it’s simple: upload your CAD, confirm your requirements, and receive inspected parts with an inspection report.

**You buy parts. We handle the factory.**

We’re also building agent ordering through our MCP server and a **Rush option** for priority production.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123265&key=user_uploads/2771579/c7d0124b-0e12-4a10-b4ca-322ecac60205)


## 🌎 Vision

**One factory is the start. The network is the point.**

Our long-term plan is hundreds, eventually thousands, of microfactories across the US, close to the teams building hardware. The same Factory OS will coordinate production across the network.

Autonomy removes waiting inside the factory. Local production puts the finished part closer to you.

The target: **American-made precision at China-competitive prices**, with local delivery in as little as 24 hours for supported parts.

Shenzhen-like speed, without needing to build in Shenzhen.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123265&key=user_uploads/2771579/e012541d-ba88-4809-9423-a1935c878aec)


## 🛠️ We’ve spent nine years getting hardware built.

Shubh and I met in college in 2017. We both studied computer science, built Mars rovers together, and competed internationally. We also spent plenty of days in CNC shops waiting for parts.

Before running my dad’s business, I was the first employee and Chief of Staff at Accio Robotics, a warehouse automation company in India, participating in its journey from the first product through scaling and acquisition.

Shubh completed his Master’s in Robotics at the University of Pennsylvania, working with robotic manipulators. After his master’s, we started Antropi.

We have experienced this problem as the people waiting for parts and as the people responsible for making them.

**Now we’re building the factories we wish we’d had.**

## 🙌 Ask

**Need CNC parts?** Send us your most challenging part and we’ll get it done. 

👉 [www.antropi.shop](http://antropi.shop)

**Know a team scaling production?** We’d appreciate introductions to hardware or procurement teams at Series B+ companies in computing infrastructure, robotics, medical devices, and energy.

We’re happy to start with one part and earn the next order.

**Naman & Shubh**

Antropi Robotics
