launches.title: Agent Relay - Let your teams' coding agents message each other
launches.tagline: Real time messaging for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Conductor or any other agent on your team.
launches.body:
**TL;DR - You can stop copy/pasting messages between agents now**

Soon, agents will outnumber people on the internet. We think they should be able to find each other, talk to each other, and work together.

Today, even agents working on the same project depend on humans to connect them. My agent needs something from your agent, so the message takes this route:

My agent → **me → you** → your agent.

Every person on the team can have agents producing work faster, while the team still waits on people to pass questions, context, and updates between them. We’re all the bottleneck!

We built Agent Relay to fix that.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124128&key=user_uploads/50118/7832a56a-13b4-49e3-a610-bf9dfbab0b49)

**How it works**

Agent Relay works inside the tools you already use, like the Codex Mac app, Claude in the terminal or even Conductor. Start your sessions as usual, and then choose which agents they can talk to. Relay runs in the background, delivering messages between them.

Before Relay, handing off work meant having my agent write up a summary, pasting it to Khaliq in Slack, and him pasting it into his agent. Now my agent just asks his. It can read his session to see what he changed and why, ask follow-up questions, and get pinged the moment his work is ready.

We don’t have to carry messages between them, and everyone can keep using their preferred tools.

Shared, searchable session history lets agents catch up on what their teammates did and why, even after those sessions have ended.

Agent Relay is [open source](https://github.com/agentworkforce/relay). You can self-host it or if you prefer to not to spend your days managing difficult infrastructure you can use our hosted cloud.

**What our customers say:**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124128&key=user_uploads/50118/d9f2fcda-2207-4157-9881-2fe29ce428ce)

**Our Team**:\
We’re Will and Khaliq. We met on the basketball court in high school and have been teammates ever since. Khaliq went on to play basketball at Cornell. Will went on to dominate rec leagues.

Since then, we’ve been building software and leading engineering teams. Khaliq was the founding engineer at Nango (W23) and lead engineer at Overview (W19). Will spent 14 years building Tailwind to eight-figure ARR and leading its engineering team.

Now we run 50+ agents in parallel ourselves, and we’re building Agent Relay to solve the coordination problems we hit every day.

Messaging is where we’re starting. We want the agents on your team to work as naturally as the team does.

**Ask:**

If you’re running coding agents on your team and still have a backlog, we’d love to learn more about your company and buy you lunch. You can reach out at [founders@agentrelay.com](mailto:founders@agentrelay.com) 

Don’t be a meat proxy. Get your agents on the relay. 

<https://agentrelay.com>

launches.body:
Hey YC, we’re Joseph and Kaan.

We’re building **Energy Superintelligence: swarms of coordinated AI agents to operate energy infrastructure and data centers, carrying out work across entire organizations.**

Energy is one of the bottlenecks to scaling intelligence. Our vision is agents coordinating humans and other agents to operate, maintain, and build energy infrastructure worldwide, with applications extending to data centers.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uDH6pMn5OE>

**How we got here**

We reached out to roughly 5,000 people in energy and had over 400 conversations. The same problem kept appearing: people were manually connecting fragmented data, investigating faults, and coordinating work across departments.

**What we’re building**

Our engineers work inside energy companies to map their data, workflows, responsibilities, and operating procedures. We combine that knowledge with an energy-specific ontology, giving specialized agents a shared understanding of the business and procedures they can follow. We see the same opportunity in data center operations: connecting equipment, maintenance procedures, suppliers, and on-site teams so agents can coordinate real work.

The system we’re building connects four things:

1. **Onology:** equipment, telemetry, documents, contracts, and people in one connected model.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116072&key=user_uploads/2057026/a14398e1-34a7-4399-a75f-c2ce6eb631c3)

2. **AI Employees:** agents use different tools, correlate evidence across assets, and review each other’s findings. 

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116072&key=user_uploads/2057026/70610c1d-cc3e-4c13-a96e-38a1acc6777f)

3. **Physical execution:** agents coordinate interventions with humans, incorporate field observations, and verify production recovery.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116072&key=user_uploads/2057026/7c425af9-22cb-44ec-9da9-dd79ce445a54)

4. **Sofware builder:** We allow technical and non technical builders to build on top of the platform. creating visualizations, agents, ML models, all using the data of the platform and centered intelligence.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116072&key=user_uploads/2057026/8abcc1a0-1a6d-44cf-8da9-74dbef23944d)


Our ambition is coordinated agents at every critical infrastructure company in the world, helping produce more energy and accelerate intelligence.

We believe **Energy Superintelligence is a necessary step toward ASI.**

launches.title: Dydema: Personal, programmable brain-computer interfaces
launches.tagline: Control your computer with a thought, no surgery required
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Dydema is building personal, programmable brain-computer interfaces- a headset plus the AI models behind it. You pick a thought and bind it to whatever you want, like a key in a game or a command to an agent. No surgery required. Our models already run on research headsets, and we’re designing our own consumer hardware.

<https://youtu.be/zJCDVuodHzk>

Hey y’all! We’re [Julian Weaver](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2801705) and [Christopher Oosthuizen](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1675405), the founders of [Dydema](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/35392).

Brain-computer interfaces have mostly lived in labs. We want one you can order online, take out of the box, set up in a few minutes and use with any app on your computer, like a keyboard or a mouse. You decide which thoughts it listens for (imagined movements, for instance) and what each one does. The agent in the video is one example; it works the same way with games, tools, robots, and whatever else you hook it up to.

**Where we are**

* After a few minutes of setup, our general decoding models work on someone they’ve never seen before, and on our benchmarks they beat models trained only on that person’s own data.
* We’re pushing on how many distinct thoughts the models can be programmed to tell apart, and how fast they decode each one. Every new differentiable thought is another key on the keyboard.
* We’re training the models to hold up on cheaper sensors and designing our headset around them.

We treat BCI as a machine learning problem, which mostly means needing lots of brain data. So we’re building the infrastructure to record more of our own. We’ve accumulated, cleaned and standardized \~14.6 years (128k hours) of EEG data, and we’re starting to record in real world contexts. People have debated for years about whether EEG models scale, and so far ours keep getting better with more labeled data.

Computers keep getting smarter, but the way we tell them what we want hasn’t changed in decades. Long term, we want a brain-computer interface that anyone can buy and use to communicate with computers and each other, faster than talking. We’ll keep posting demos as we go!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125458&key=user_uploads/2801705/ece4b187-376e-4844-b520-1e4439de5354)

**About us**

* [Julian](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2801705) (CEO) graduated from UT Austin at 20 with degrees in CS and neuroscience. While there, he co-founded Longhorn Neurotech, which he grew into one of the largest student neurotech research orgs in the world (200+ members), and he led EEG/fMRI ML interpretability research.
* [Chris](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1675405) (CTO) was an ML researcher at UH SAIL, where he built state-of-the-art GraphRAG systems and worked on reducing LLM hallucinations. He’s been programming his whole life, and wrote his own programming language from scratch in high school.
* We’ve been best friends since freshman year of high school, and we were both founding engineers at [Syntra (YC S24)](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/29987).

**Asks**

* Building something that could take a thought as an input (games, agents, robotics)? We’d love to talk.
* If you have brain datasets, we want them!
* We’ll be hiring more hardware engineers soon. If you know anyone who’s built wearables or low-noise biosignal hardware, please send them our way.
* Want to try our rig? Let us know!

Cheers y’all,\
Julian & Chris

Reach us at [founders@dydema.com](mailto:founders@dydema.com).

**Workers IO: Deterministic simulation environments to verify mission-critical systems**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3wW8qNPPswg>

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but verifying what they build still requires significant engineering effort.

The slowest part of engineering now is verification.

Teams need to understand how different parts of a system work together and what happens as they fail and recover. It’s difficult to think through every scenario that could cause a failure, which is why teams often discover these issues in production.

That’s why we’re building[ ](http://workers.io/)Workers IO. We run your entire system, including its dependencies, under millions of simulated production scenarios to verify that it never fails. This allows teams to do years’ worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

Every simulation runs inside a deterministic hypervisor. It uses checkpoints and branches to efficiently explore your system’s state space, verifying different timelines in parallel. Across these timelines, it inject faults, including network delays, disk errors, process failures, and clock skew to verify your system can handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows you to perfectly reproduce scenarios, giving your agents rich context they need to investigate failures and fix them.

<https://youtu.be/TM3ToSRY8GE>

We’re already helping teams whose systems process millions of requests a day, where failures can be catastrophic and verification is becoming a barrier to modernizing their stacks.

Law firms spend 62% of their time on admin tasks they don’t bill. Client data lives in tools that don’t talk to each other, and legal assistants copy data from one system to another and chase documents by email for weeks. To keep up, law firms hire more assistants.

We’re Feifei, David, and Kai, the founders of Shepherd Robotics.

## The problem

Data centers and advanced manufacturers need to scale, but skilled technicians are hard to hire. Repetitive work—wiring, assembly, and equipment testing—ties up the people needed to troubleshoot problems and keep projects moving.

At a single factory, repetitive assembly alone can consume more than $2 million in annual labor costs. Yet traditional automation struggles to handle the variation across products and sites, leaving this work dependent on manual labor.

## What we’re building

Shepherd’s robots perform physical tasks under human supervision. We’re starting with:

* **Data center commissioning and inspection:** Operate equipment controls, verify responses, and capture photo evidence.
* **Electrical assembly:** Wire routing, terminal insertion, and other repetitive assembly tasks.

Qualified people direct the work and handle exceptions. Their interventions help us improve the system and automate more over time.

The goal: more output, consistent execution, and more time for skilled people to focus on troubleshooting and decisions that need their expertise.

## Our team

Our team brings 30 years of combined experience in autonomous systems and robotic manipulation, with backgrounds at Waymo, Cruise, and Dyna Robotics.

We’d love introductions to leaders in data center operations, construction, and manufacturing whose teams are struggling with repetitive manual work or production bottlenecks.

**Problem:** \
The world was full of physical tasks no technology could automate till now. Generalist robot models can finally handle the messy, variable work that traditional automation never could: mixed orders, returns, tasks that change every day.

But a capable model isn't the same as a robot reliably doing the job on your floor. Most robotics projects stall in the gap between a good demo and a shift that runs 24/7. 

**Solution:** \
Deploy closes that gap. We’re the generalist robot deployment company. We turn generalist robots into reliable workers, and our customers pay for completed work, not the robot.

**How it works:** \
→ We break each new task into a sequence of steps and track progress in real time\
→ The system knows what's done, what's next, and when a robot needs help\
→ Every human intervention becomes training data, so the robots get better the longer they run

**The backstory**\
[Irene](https://www.linkedin.com/in/irene-grace-karot-polson/) and [Sahith](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sahith-reddy-chada/) have been building robots for over a decade, from opposite ends of the stack. Sahith built robot models at Honda Research Institute. Irene deployed autonomous vehicles in safety-critical airport environments. We kept hitting the same wall: deployment. Deploying across different robots and different models is fundamentally the same problem. If it’s one problem, one platform can solve it. So we’re building Deploy.

launches.title: Caladh: Anti-drone maritime defense
launches.tagline: Caladh protects critical maritime infrastructure from drone attacks above and below the waterline so they can't get near the assets they want to disrupt.
launches.body:
**TL;DR Underwater drones can navigate under the surface to reach ports, ships and seafloor cables, and no reliable solution exists to stop them. Caladh systems detect, track and defeat hostile drones by bringing the principles of electronic warfare underwater.** \
\
I’m [**Kristen Kita**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kristen-railey-kita-18388722/), founder of Caladh ("Call-luh"). I've spent the past decade working on this problem, starting with my PhD at MIT and most recently as a Principal Investigator for DARPA Sync. I started Caladh to close the gaps I've seen in how we protect critical infrastructure.\
\
<https://youtu.be/oQJC_hS07DQ>

\
**What we do**

* **Eclipse: deny the drone.** Eclipse is a moored buoy that persistently protects ports, terminals, offshore energy sites and cable landings. It listens passively, and when a threat appears it triggers automatically or on an operator’s command. It then denies the vehicle its navigation, comms and sensing both above and below the waterline, so the drone can’t find its target or report back. A towed version deploys from a small boat for expeditionary missions. It’s non-kinetic, unattended, and it plugs into existing C2 and layered defenses.
* **Cloak: hide the target.** Cloak sits low on the seabed next to cables, pipelines and other subsea assets. It defeats the imaging sonar and cameras that drones use to find and map those assets, so the asset blends back into the seafloor.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126106&key=user_uploads/3880244/585d7584-ead6-4de2-a3f6-5a19fdf33e8f)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126106&key=user_uploads/3880244/162d1022-921b-44c5-bda8-f1ca80cedba9)

**Why now**

A cheap drone can now threaten an asset worth hundreds of millions. In December 2025, Ukraine claimed it struck a Kilo-class submarine with an underwater drone. Above the surface, missile and drone attacks at Bab-el-Mandeb cut Suez Canal trade by about 50% in early 2024, and in October 2026 naval drones hit at least six merchant ships in the Black Sea.

The seafloor is just as exposed. The Nord Stream pipelines sabotage shows what one strike on seabed infrastructure can cost: the largest methane release on record. Underwater drones now give attackers a cheaper, harder-to-attribute way to reach the same kinds of targets: ports, offshore energy and subsea cables, none of which has a perimeter below the waterline.

**Why me**

I’ve worked on this problem for 10 years. My PhD at MIT was on detecting and tracking underwater drones with passive sonar. Across five DARPA underwater drone programs spanning navigation, sensing and autonomy, I learned exactly how these vehicles fail. I conceived the counter-UUV concept for DARPA Sync, led the DARPA study that shaped the new program, and served as the Principal Investigator, demonstrating new approaches to defeat underwater drones.

**Asks**

Introductions to:

* Port and terminal security leads
* Offshore oil, gas and wind security leads
* Subsea cable and pipeline operators
* Navy, Marine Corps expeditionary and Naval Special Warfare operators
* Advisors with Navy acquisition or submarine/NSW operational experience

Contact us at [founders@caladh.com](mailto:founders@caladh.com) or on [caladh.com](http://caladh.com) 

_Caladh is a Gaelic word for harbor, haven or safe landing place._

launches.body:
tl;dr: Evardi builds AI agents that engineer the grid edge: the transformers and local lines where rooftop solar, batteries, EVs and data centers connect.

<https://youtu.be/Xztpv94BkL8>

Hey everyone! We're Diva and Aarya. Blackouts have affected both our families, in Kenya and India, and working inside utilities showed us how hard their teams work with tools that stop at the substation. So we built Evardi.

Outages cost Americans up to $121B in a single year, and most of them start below the substation, where utilities have limited real-time data. After a storm, a feeder comes back on while transformers behind it stay dark. A switching order relies on a switch that's already failed twice. A meter mapped to the wrong transformer sends crews to the wrong street. Evardi catches all of these, and more. 

Evardi turns the data a utility already collects into a live digital twin of its network. On top of it, our physics-based models:

* **See every transformer.** Every meter is matched to the right transformer, and every transformer gets a virtual meter, with no new hardware.
* **Find outages earlier.** Signals already streaming in show which transformers are still dark after a storm and who's affected.
* **Test every plan.** Every outage, maintenance window and new connection is tested on the twin before it happens. Studies that take engineers days run in under two minutes.
* **Check every switching step.** Orders are drafted from the utility's own history, switches that have failed before are flagged, and every step is simulated before it reaches the field crew.

In case studies, Evardi restored power to 63% more customers and pinpointed the source of outages 10x more often. We are working with utilities across the globe serving nearly 10 million customers.

Learn more at [evardi.ai](http://evardi.ai).

**Do you work in operations, outage response or grid planning at a utility, or know someone who does?** Please connect them with us at [**diva@evardi.ai**](mailto:diva@evardi.ai), we'd love to chat!

launches.tagline: We collect egocentric video data + force and contact dynamics derived from workers' muscular signals. Adding Hemlock's force data to human training demos improved pi0.5's success by 10x and Gemini Argon's by 2.7x on force-sensitive manipulation tasks.
launches.body:
## TL;DR:

**For robots to be effective, they need to understand real world force and contact dynamics.**

We equip workers with EMG wearables and egocentric video gear to analyze their muscular signals and generate the force/contact data needed to **train physical AI models to use their hands the same way skilled workers do**. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124952&key=user_uploads/2947535/4f8a50ae-f121-473e-a450-1d2a5726b1cd)

Adding Hemlock's force data to human training demos **improved Pi0.5's success** **on egg pick-and-place by** **10x** and **Gemini 4 Argon's success** **on a lightbulb screwing task by** **2.7x**. If you or anybody you know is working on robotic dexterous manipulation or training physical AI models, [**please get in touch ASAP :)**](mailto:julian@hemlock.inc)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124952&key=user_uploads/2947535/33e3ff55-81e7-402f-80fb-fadf63fa0317)

## **The Problem 🤖**

Today’s robotics companies and frontier physical AI model labs are spending **hundreds of millions** on egocentric video data to train their systems to perform tasks in place of humans. However, whether the deployment site is somebody’s kitchen or an automotive assembly line, successful task execution depends on an understanding of force and contact dynamics. 

**Currently, there’s no good way to get this data into a model.**

1. Tactile gloves occlude the user’s hands. 
2. Instrumenting the environment isn’t scalable. 
3. Video alone drops this information entirely.

And thus, Hemlock was born.

<https://youtu.be/adox0I2cmBE>

## Hemlock - The Missing Piece 🧩

Hemlock equips skilled workers with egocentric video capture gear and our proprietary EMG wearable - the Bracelet. We read their muscular activity while they do their day-to-day work to understand how they apply force with their fingers, move their hands, and manipulate objects and tools. 

We turn a day of work into rich tactile information used to improve robotic AI models’ dexterous manipulation capabilities. Any industry. Any task.

We recently collected a few minutes of human demonstration data on a basic egg pick-and-place task, using it to finetune **Pi0.5** twice: **once only with video and once with video + Bracelet data**. 

Success rates shot up **10x**.

We then decided to up the ante: same idea, except screwing in a lightbulb using **a humanoid hand** and **Google’s Gemini 4 Argon model**.

Up **2.7x**.

Check out the full videos [here](https://hemlock.inc/#case-study) ;)

## The Ask ⁉️

**If you are:**

1. **working on physical AI foundation models,**
2. **involved in data ops at robotics/physical AI companies,**
3. **working on robotic manipulation,**
4. **automating a force-sensitive task for a deployment,**
5. **friends with anybody fitting the criteria above,**

   **please [shoot me an email](mailto:julian@hemlock.inc). I’d love to discuss your data needs and any intros would be greatly appreciated 🙏**

## BTS 🎬

Hey everybody, 

I’m Julian Olschwang:

* Prev. @ CMU ECE+Robotics & UCLA Biomechatronics
* 4 patents in wearable tech
* Elbow deep in circuits from 11 years old

Very blessed to be building among such talented folks. Much love to you all!

launches.tagline: Building Autonomous Factories in America, Starting with On-Demand CNC Machining
launches.body:
We’re Hemant and Sam, founders of twentyfour26. We are building fully autonomous factories in America, starting with on-demand CNC machining.\
\
<https://youtu.be/5zW00NYwJno>\
\
**The Problem**

Factories have spent decades automating mass production. But most hardware companies aren't manufacturing millions of identical products. They need hundreds of different components, in changing quantities, with new designs coming every week.

Every new design requires its own machining strategy, tooling, workholding, programming, setup, and inspection. Much of this process is still manual, making low volume manufacturing slow, expensive, and difficult to scale.\
\
**What We're Building**

We're developing standardized manufacturing cells that bring machines, tooling, workholding, and inspection under a single system. Our models are being developed to interpret CAD designs, plan machining strategies, select tooling and setups, and operate the machines.

We're already manufacturing components for hardware companies in and around the Bay Area, with turnaround times as fast as \~48 hours. Operating our own machines allows us to develop and deploy automation against real production workloads.

Our goal is to make manufacturing 100 different designs as easy as manufacturing 100 units of the same design.

From individual components to complete assemblies, we want to abstract the entire manufacturing infrastructure into an API.\
\
**Team**

I've spent my career in hardware, from building ATVs and running supersonic simulations to designing products for high volume manufacturing. Across all of it, getting parts made was consistently one of the biggest bottlenecks.

Sam has spent the past decade building hardware and software for hardware. He sold his first company at 18 and moved into software after experiencing how slow hardware development was. For the past two years, he's worked with startups building vertical AI agents.\
\
**Our Ask**

**Teams building in space, defense, robotics, or anything else physical:** Have a part you're about to send out for a quote? Send it our way. We'd love to make it.

**Teams going from prototyping to production:** What's the biggest manufacturing bottleneck you'd pay the most to solve?

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Ben and Ariyaman met as students in Montreal. Ben ran a roofing company, then founded Timrep, a contractor permitting startup that reached six-figure revenue and raised from Accomplice. Ariyaman grew an SEO startup to six-figure ARR and automated property management for 3,000+ units.

Before building Fleety, they worked as dispatchers at home service companies. Dispatch decides how much a shop makes, but it runs on gut feel and bad data. Jobs go to whoever is free, not the tech most likely to close.

They moved to San Francisco to fix that, starting with dispatch.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Plenty of startups help plumbing and HVAC shops answer phones and book jobs. But once a job is booked, someone still has to decide who to send, and keep moving things around as the day changes.

We spent months working as dispatchers and found it was one of the hardest parts of running a shop. You're balancing technician skills, drive time, customer needs, and revenue, all under pressure. And the stakes are high: a shop's best technician can bring in $500K more a year than an average one. Sending the right tech to the right job is how shops earn more from the calls they already have.

That's why we started with dispatch. It touches almost every part of the business and gives us the context to improve other workflows too. Customers are already asking us to build more, and that's how we want to grow: stay close to them and let their needs guide what we build next.

launches.tagline: Sends the right tech to the right job, and rebuilds the schedule all day.
launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Ben and Ari, cofounders of Fleety.

**TL;DR: Fleety is an AI dispatcher for plumbing and HVAC companies. It decides which technician goes to which job and rebuilds the schedule all day as things change.**

<https://youtu.be/k1n0ZgVW6SY>

_Hear from Alex Nelson, Operational Manager of Panther Services Group, on working with Fleety._

**The problem**

Dispatch is harder than sending the closest tech. One tech won't drive into SF, another can't fit in crawl spaces, and only a few can fix tankless water heaters. Then jobs cancel and techs run late.

Getting it wrong is expensive. A shop's best tech can bring in $500K more a year than an average one. Sending the right tech to the right job is how shops earn more from the calls they already get.

**How Fleety works**

Fleety plugs into ServiceTitan. It checks and fills in job details before they reach dispatch, so jobs are tagged correctly from the start. Then it assigns each job to the best tech for it, based on skills, location, availability and close rate. When the day changes, Fleety rebuilds the schedule.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125686&key=user_uploads/1701704/50d0ea86-2a6a-443f-8a7c-87f19e4004a7)

_Fleety assigning jobs directly on the ServiceTitan dispatch board_

**Results**

At Albert Nahman Plumbing, Heating & Cooling:

\- Fleety makes \~92% of job assignments

\- One dispatcher runs 30+ techs

\- The GM and operations manager are off dispatch, saving \~$60K/yr in overhead

long_description:
Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve.

Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. Each codebase has conventions, history, and failure modes that a general-purpose model doesn't know. We learn those continuously from the code, how the team works, and the mistakes agents make. Then we fix the codebase and add merge gates that use deterministic verifiers instead of another model's judgment, so the same mistake can't ship twice. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work.

We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.

launches.title: Primordiant: Programmable access to flexible scientific experimentation at scale
launches.tagline: On-demand experimentation in scientific data centers, run by self-evolving robot scientists, for the discoveries of tomorrow.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We're building general-purpose robot scientists that learn new tasks, adapt as experiments change, and improve on their own. We give people and AI agents **programmable access to physical experimentation at scale**, either in our labs or with our robots on-site in theirs. 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yd6z26toh6w>

**The problem**

AI models can now propose hypotheses and design experiments. Testing them still depends on human hands, or rigid lab automation scripted for custom machines that run inflexible scientific protocols. Discovery moves as fast as physical experimentation, and today those are slow, manual, and hard to scale. 

**Our solution**

Science needs experimentalists that **iterate as fast as a machine and adapt as readily as human scientists**. Primordiant's robots plan experiments, run them, observe what happens, and decide what to try next, closing the loop between reasoning and physical action . **Instead of building a new machine for every task, we're building generalist robot scientists that can take on whatever comes next**, and improve with every experiment. We’re firm believers in the Bitter Lesson, and we believe general purpose robots are the pathway to scaling scientific discovery.

**What we've built so far**

\- We designed and built our first robot in less than 3 weeks and took it to an early client's wet lab (They gave it a skull with goggles. We approve.) 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125694&key=user_uploads/2759626/82db9ca3-e7f1-421d-99d6-22b8cc3e57db)

\- We opened our own lab in Mountain View, where we're working with a second client to synthesize and test heat-resistant polymer coatings proposed by AI models.

\- A few weeks earlier, we ran our very first experiments from a makeshift materials lab in our Airbnb, in our pajamas :)\
\
**What comes next**: \*\*Scientific Data Centers!\*\*\
Compute became a utility once data centers let anyone use a server through an API. We think experimentation is next. We imagine **data-center-sized laboratories full of general-purpose robot scientists**, where anyone can call up a physical experiment as easily as a cloud GPU, and run it at a scale no human lab could match.\
\
**Team**

We are three Brown PhDs who have spent years building the core pieces: robots that act reliably in the real world, AI that does real science, and hands-on experimental physics. 

* [**Owen Tower**](https://linkedin.com/in/owen-tower-phd-270630133) **(PhD, Experimental Physics, Brown):** Studied topological phase transitions under Nobel Laureate Mike Kosterlitz, developing new algorithms and nanofluidic experiments for random-field Ising models. Ex **NASA JPL**, **CERN**.
* [**Cooper Niu**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cooper-niu) **(PhD, Theoretical Physics, Brown):** Created **ALBERT**, an AI particle physicist that **recovered the top quark's mass and properties from pre-1990 data in under an hour**. Ex **Fermilab**, **CERN**.
* [**Benedict Quartey**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/benedictquartey) **(PhD, Robotics, Brown):** Pioneer in **generally capable yet verifiable robot autonomy**. Created **LIMP** (ICRA 2025) one of the first systems that enabled robots to follow open-ended instructions with guarantees in the real-world. Ex **Boston Dynamics Robotics & AI Institute**.

\
**Our ask**\
If you lead R&D in **biotech, chemistry, materials, semiconductors** and want to run more experiments, faster, we'd love to put a robot scientist in your lab or run your experiments in ours. If you need high quality experimental data for scientific foundation models we would love to chat.\

launches.tagline: Test your agent in a simulated world before unleashing it on the real one.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Evan Whitehouse](https://www.linkedin.com/in/evwhitehouse/) and [Zachary Kiihne](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zachary-kiihne-56b944129) from Rystic 👋.\
\
**TL;DR**

Rystic gives your agent working copies of the tools it acts on: Slack, Stripe, Google Drive, and 14 more. Your tests can check what the agent actually _did_, not just what it said. Each copy keeps its state, runs locally or in CI, and is checked against the real service every day .\
\
Every test job gets its own isolated copy, so tests run in parallel: **50 Stripe test jobs finished in 19 seconds, compared with 40+ minutes on shared real-API sandboxes.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125187&key=user_uploads/1541344/455d2179-8995-42bb-afcf-20ed45dfef14)

**Asks**: Building an agent that acts on real systems? Try free on [rystic.ai](http://rystic.ai). For custom environments, including internal services, get in touch at [founders@rystic.ai](mailto:founders@rystic.ai).

**The Problem**

At a previous job, the first agent we gave write access to GitHub flooded our CI runners by creating hundreds of PRs within a few minutes. There was no way to iterate on our agent without running it against our production systems.\
\
When giving an agent write access to a system with real consequences, how can you trust that they’ll behave properly?

<https://youtu.be/8dvzTRv_la8>

**How We Solve It**

Rystic can simulate an API or Web app as a lightweight binary. Run it anywhere and get behavior that matches the real thing. These simulators are stateful: delete data, query it, and you’ll get the same error the real service returns.

A simulator also lets you test things you never could with the real API. What happens when latency triples? What if the data feed’s websocket connection drops in the middle of placing an order? With a simulator, you can script the failure cases that matter and prove you handle them correctly.

We use these to create an environment which can be seeded with either real trace data or synthetic data, so you can validate your agents’ actions and their impacts before you release them.

**Why You Can Trust It**

How do you know the simulator behaves like the real thing? We check every simulator against the real service daily and publish the results. Our simulator matches Stripe on [99.1% of 1,813 checks](https://www.rystic.ai/simulators), and every known difference is listed.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125187&key=user_uploads/1541344/8c3c4791-70e6-4a1f-9331-68b7a680742b)

**Catalog**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125187&key=user_uploads/1541344/b5629ce4-59fa-468a-99db-e07e63172d5a)

**The Team**\
We met all the way back in 2016 when we were up and coming professional Magic: the Gathering players. We practiced together and spent over a year on the same pro team. Evan finished 2018 ranked #2 on the SCG tour, the largest independent circuit; Zach made the Top 8 at three Pro Tours, the game's premier event. Then we both pivoted into software engineering.

Since then, Evan graduated with honors from Columbia CS and helped build Roblox’s service mesh from 0→1, supporting hundreds of millions of concurrent requests. Zach has spent 5 years at Google, and shipped AI integrations in Gmail and Google Docs to billions of people.

We learned to win at Magic by finding the edge cases everyone else missed, so we’re building Rystic the same way.

launches.title: Vorelios: AI that can engineer anything
launches.tagline: Solving engineering, then using it to solve everything else
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re Daniel and Krish, the founders of Vorelios.

**TL;DR:** Vorelios is a research lab building AI that can engineer anything. Our model takes a design’s geometry and predicts its fluid, thermal, and structural behavior in seconds instead of hours or days of simulation, and uses those predictions to invent and improve designs autonomously. We’re expanding it to more domains as we go.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7_CMTf_Z-SE>

**The problem**

We already understand the physics behind many of the technologies we want to build. But knowing the equations doesn’t give us a working design. Computing how a single design will behave can take hours or days of simulation, and finding one that works means investigating many possibilities. That process can take years, so we only explore a small fraction of what could work.

AI can explain the physics and propose designs, but evaluating those designs still depends on the same expensive simulations. Most AI for simulation today trains a separate model for each problem and only works on designs close to what it was trained on. We’re building one model that learns how physics actually works, so it can predict how completely new designs will behave and use those predictions to engineer them.

**Where we are**

* **It works from CAD.** Give it clean geometry and operating conditions, and it predicts the full physical fields in a fraction of a second.
* **It’s tested on real, full-scale designs,** not simplified shapes or isolated components.
* **It’s built for designs it hasn’t seen.** Public benchmarks mostly test designs similar to the training data. When we tested on families of designs outside the training set, every model we tried failed, including our own previous architecture, which was state of the art on those benchmarks. Our current model does substantially better, and closing the rest of that gap is the center of our research.
* **It’s one model across physics.** The same model predicts fluid flow, heat transfer, and structural behavior, and we’re expanding it to more domains as we go.
* **It has started designing on its own.** In our first end-to-end runs, the system took a written spec, searched thousands of candidate designs with the model, and refined the best ones with no human in the loop. An independent solver confirmed the designs consistently beat a typical candidate, with the model’s predictions within a few percent.

**How we’re approaching it**

* **Data.** There’s no internet’s worth of physics data to learn from. We have to generate it through simulation, but today’s solvers were built for engineers checking one design at a time. We’re building the entire pipeline from the ground up for AI, from generating geometry to running the simulations, so it runs automatically and produces physics data with a scale and breadth that has never existed.
* **Architecture.** A model can predict familiar designs accurately and still get the physics wrong on something new. But engineering means inventing new things. We’re designing models that have to learn how physics actually works instead of finding shortcuts, so they can make reliable predictions for new designs. Getting there depends as much on the architecture as on the training data.
* **Breadth.** Engineers use separate tools for different kinds of physics, even though those effects interact in the same design. Our model already predicts fluid, thermal, and structural physics together. As we add more domains, each one builds on what the model has learned from the others.

**Where we’re going**

We want to turn humanity’s hardest moonshots into tractable engineering problems. If years of engineering can happen in a fraction of the time, projects that are too complex or expensive to attempt today become practical to pursue. We could explore far more ways to make them work, figure out how to build technologies people have spent decades trying to build, and discover inventions no one has imagined yet.

**The team**

We’re Daniel McNeil (CEO) and Krish Kapadia (CTO), both 19. Daniel studied physics at the University of Florida, where Krish did research in AI and cyber-physical systems.

We started Vorelios because we want to see the future we imagine become real within our lifetimes. We see engineering as the biggest bottleneck to getting there. So we set out to solve it.

**Our ask**

We’re looking for exceptional AI researchers, and for engineers and researchers in numerical solvers and CFD. If you know someone whose work you really respect, we’d appreciate an intro. You can reach us at [founders@vorelios.com](mailto:founders@vorelios.com).

launches.body:
**TL;DR: We're 40-50% faster than existing cloud providers in serving frontier robot AI models, e.g. DreamZero, MolmoAct2.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jVqvJFBRcd0>

\[1x speed, autonomous\]

DSL is building the fastest cloud inference platform for robotics. We let you deploy physical AI without needing expensive local GPUs.

Robot foundation models are growing more and more computationally expensive. The latest frontier of robotics no longer fits feasibly on local GPUs. Compute costs keep soaring amidst a global LPDDR shortage; NVIDIA just doubled the prices of Jetsons in July.

**We're taking a contrarian bet that the future is moving inference _off the robot_ and _into the cloud._**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/4ca20fc9-00a8-4043-bc43-d51b8b5d0cbf)

How do we do this? We work across the full stack of robot inference to push latency down:

* Model-level architectural adjustments for faster inference
* Kernel-level optimizations to maximally leverage server-grade GPUs
* Network-level optimizations for fast and reliable transport over the cloud
* Region-specific compute allocation to ensure the shortest physical distance between the servers and our customers' robots

These optimizations enable us to be **8% faster** than NVIDIA's implementation **at half the GPU count** (320ms vs 350ms, for DreamZero 14B).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/69393040-ca17-41cd-a1fb-cd5d70176921)

Furthermore, something we noticed for robotics companies with fast R&D cycles was that their GPUs had long idle periods with concentrated bursts of inference traffic. We're one of the first companies in the world to offer on-demand pricing for physical AI inference, giving users more flexibility with the cost.

We're already working closely with a range of early partners across deployment, research and evaluation. In full FDE spirit, we collaborate with our customers to custom-fit inference stacks that address their unique deployment challenges. We help you get your robot AI to deployment faster.

Our mission is to democratize access to frontier physical intelligence, and we believe cloud is the way forward. You can read our thesis here:

•⁠ ⁠<http://dreamscalelabs.com/blog/why>

\
**Our ask:** Reach out at [founders@dreamscalelabs.com](mailto:founders@dreamscalelabs.com) !

launches.tagline: Halmos designs experiments for biotech teams
launches.body:
Halmos enables biotech teams to get more out of every experiment. It reads the literature, runs simulations, and selects or trains models to optimize every step — so you extract more information across discovery, process development, scale-up, and manufacturing.\
\
<https://youtu.be/u1ptzxsgzWo>
\
**The problem**\
Experiments are slow, expensive, and most of the information they could yield is wasted. Teams run tedious trial-and-error or exhaustive screens, burning months of lab time and budget to reach conclusions better experimental design would have reached far sooner. The pharmaceutical industry alone performed **$126B of U.S. R&D in 2023**.\
\
**How it works**\
Halmos runs unbounded research by coordinating hundreds of AI agents, checks the logical consistency of their reasoning, and revisits arguments that fail validation before presenting conclusions to your team.\
Zero installations, no data engineering, and no need for your own statistics team.\
\
**Tested in industry:**

* **Bioprocessing:** In a collaboration, Halmos matched the best performance from a company's wet-lab campaign in an average of **30% fewer evaluations** across repeated simulations. Halmos repeatedly recommended testing beyond the permitted range; when the experimentalists eventually explored it, performance improved further.
* **Food-tech fermentation:** For a company two months into fermentation optimization, Halmos simulated the organism's metabolism and identified a nutrient variable missing from the experimental plan. The team confirmed the finding and replanned its next month of experiments.

\
**Towards increasingly large R&D tasks**\
We start by designing experiments. From there we take on increasingly large R&D tasks until we can run full end-to-end programs for biotech teams at a fraction of the cost of a consultant — enabling new discoveries in less well funded industries like food, rare diseases, biomaterials, and agriculture. \
\

launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Koosha and Anmol, the founders of Resin. We’re building an AI-native PCB design tool that helps engineers turn ideas into working electronics faster and more reliably.

**Demo: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JByTuaHHHGg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JByTuaHHHGg)**

Mandatory GIF:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=120163&key=user_uploads/501763/ddae1ba4-75e5-43a7-9a30-fe4fa392848f)

**Problem we’re solving**

* **PCB design is slow and manual:** Engineers can spend weeks reading datasheets, finding components, drawing schematics, and routing connections on traditional design tools. 
* **Design mistakes are expensive:** A design error that only gets surfaced _after_ fabrication can require redesigning and manufacturing the board again, adding weeks/months of delay and cost.
* **Requires expertise:** Good board design takes years of experience to master, so many smaller companies can't do it in-house. Resin makes it accessible to experts and non-experts (including hobbyists) alike.

**How Resin solves this problem**

Resin brings AI into a complete ECAD workspace to increase engineering velocity & design reliability:

* **Draft and review schematics:** Describe your requirements. Resin researches parts, drafts schematics, and documents its design decisions. It also reviews existing designs to help catch mistakes before manufacturing.
* **Find or generate any part:** Tell Resin which component you need. It searches millions of parts, analyzes them deeply and generates accurate symbols and footprints.
* **Route boards:** Connect selected signals or your whole board with our proprietary routing engine. We’re especially excited about this one!
* **In the cloud and collaborative:** Resin runs fully in the cloud, and allows seamless collaboration across multiple users!
* **Prepare for manufacturing:** Check component pricing and availability, manage your bill of materials, and export manufacturing files.
* **Stay in control:** Resin is a complete EDA workspace with full schematic, PCB tooling (**and not a mere chatbot!**). Users can delegate entire workflows to AI or get hands-on with individual components, connections, and traces. Every AI change is editable and auditable.
* **Bring existing work into Resin:** We have full support for project & library imports from Altium & KiCad so you can continue existing projects in Resin! There are more integrations on the way!
* **MCP compatible:** Work from Claude Code, Codex, etc.

**Team**

We’ve been long time friends — we met in college where we studied Engineering Physics together! Koosha has tons of electronics and hardware experience, having designed very complex hardware at Bosch, Kodak, IHS. Anmol mostly recently led the FDE team at [you.com](http://you.com) and was an early member at various successful AI startups.

**Our Asks**

launches.title: Routant — Let AI agents into your apps, on your rules
launches.tagline: Selective, secure access for AI agents to exactly the apps and data you choose
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Routant lets AI agents work inside your apps and private systems, with access rules you control. Choose which tools an agent can use, require approval for sensitive actions, and review what it did.

<https://youtu.be/3cYCNFWQjuc>

**The Problem**

An AI agent is only useful if it can get into the systems where the work happens: your inbox, your database, your payment provider, a customer's internal tools. Today, giving it that access is all or nothing.

An agent connected to your email can read messages it has no reason to see. An IT agent troubleshooting a production issue may need access to infrastructure far beyond the affected system. And a company deploying support agents across customers needs to navigate a different set of private networks, credentials, and security policies for every environment.

Teams stitch together VPNs, custom integrations, credentials, and approval workflows to make this work. They often rely on prompt instructions or scattered configuration files to limit what agents can do, but these aren't reliable security boundaries. The result is that agents either get too much access, creating unnecessary risk, or too little, leaving humans to do the work themselves.

**Our Solution**

Routant sits between your agents and the systems they use, and enforces your rules on every request.

* Connect once: agents reach your apps through a single MCP endpoint. Private and on-prem systems connect through an outbound-only gateway, with no inbound ports to open.
* Selective access: an agent only sees the tools and data you've granted. For example, your assistant can handle work email while messages from friends stay invisible to it.
* Approvals for what matters: sensitive actions are held until someone approves them, and disallowed actions are blocked outright.
* A full record: every request and decision is logged, so you can see exactly what the agent did.

Because the rules live in Routant and are built into the access itself, they hold no matter what the prompt says. For companies building agents, each customer sets its own rules, so you integrate once instead of rebuilding access for every customer.

**Why We’re Building This**

I’m Aditya, the founder of Routant. Before this, I built ML pricing models as a quantitative options trader at IMC and studied computer science at Princeton.

Working with automated trading systems taught me that software needs explicit authority to act, controls around consequential decisions, and a record of what happened.

AI agents need those controls as they start working inside other companies’ systems. We’re building Routant to make that access practical.

**Our Ask**

Know a security leader putting AI agents into production? We’d appreciate an introduction.

If you’re a CTO or CISO deciding what those agents can access in your systems, we’d love to show you Routant.

Book a demo at [routant.ai](http://routant.ai)

Hey YC! It's Nick.

There's a version of every founder who says health benefits are handled. I was that founder for five years at Plated as we scaled to over 1,000 employees. ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115270&key=user_uploads/765651/78da6cb4-1537-435e-859e-650ecdbb5326)

Employers fund the health insurance system but see almost none of it:

* Renewals arrive as a number with no explanation - dinosaur brokers claim “it’s a hard market.”
* Carriers price you based on data you're never shown - if you’re 500 employees, you see data. If you’re 50, you don’t.
* Small groups get worse rates without a benchmark to push back - no data = no leverage
* Switching feels risky, so most companies stay put.

With Ignition, we combine the market access and expertise of a traditional broker with an AI-native platform that gives you more transparency and control. We’re brining the enterprise benefits experience to the SMB.

### See your workforce the way the carrier does

Ignition analyzes the health and risk data carriers use to price your plan, so you can see what's actually driving your costs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115270&key=user_uploads/765651/6f505ce5-4438-461f-9ade-8541298a1086)

### Licensed experts + AI interventions in your corner

Our licensed experts compare plans, take your renewal to market, and guide you through your options. AI surfaces recommended actions and answers questions in context, so nothing sits in a black box.

### AI-native benefits administration

Enrollment, renewals, compliance, and life events run on an AI-native platform, with licensed experts in the loop.

### No cost to you

Ignition is paid by the carrier, not you. We analyze your data, identify opportunities, and let you decide what happens next.

## The Ask

Whether you're hiring your twentieth employee or your two hundredth, there's a version of this decision you're making blind right now.

Don't let the dinosaurs run your benefits. Your benefits. Your data. Your decision.

[@Alan Ma](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/4166436) and I are ex-McKinsey and ex-Scale AI, where we were forward-deployed with Fortune 500 companies in finance, healthcare, and software, including orgs like the Mayo Clinic. **In our experience building enterprise agents, integrations with legacy systems were a major bottleneck**: without them, agents could not pull data or take actions on behalf of users, undermining speed and accuracy. Creating these integrations required extensive planning, time, and money - delaying agent builds and requiring more devs.

<https://youtu.be/z9gO7npwxDQ>

**The solution**

Pomerado lets you or your agent create a hosted API or MCP:

* 🏎️ **Fast, cheap, and reliable:** Our deterministic integrations are significantly faster (2-4x), cheaper (10-1000x), and more reliable (+30%) than browser use

We’re working with GlobalFoundries on 3D chip development, targeting our first tapeout in 2027.

launches.title: Polemos Industries: The next generation of autonomous precision strike
launches.tagline: Mass strike capability, delivered by networked launchers and AI guidance.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Precision strike, rebuilt for the age of autonomy.**

Polemos Industries (YC F26) is building next-generation autonomous precision strike. Watch the launch [video](https://youtu.be/Tid8NZQvhrE) below and learn more at [polemosindustries.com](http://polemosindustries.com)

**About Polemos**\
Modern war is changing faster than the weapons built for it. The conflicts of the next decade will be decided by speed, autonomy and scale, and the precision strike the West relies on today was built for a different era.

Polemos combines AI guidance, networked launch systems, and mass strike capability into one integrated system. We design our full systems in-house, from guidance to final integration, and we’re building out propellant production so we can scale on our own terms. Everything is built from day one to be mass-manufactured and to protect the West in the next generation of modern warfare.

**The Polemos Team**\
Hey, I’m Henrijs, founder of Polemos. I attended Astra Nova (formerly Ad Astra), the school founded by Elon Musk, where I was part of the first international cohort and focused on aerospace and mechanical engineering. I went on to work hands-on with the engineering teams at two defense companies building autonomous systems fielded by NATO forces, across navigation, firmware, electrical and aerospace production.

I’m building Polemos alongside a team with backgrounds across NASA JPL, Caltech’s GALCIT aerospace lab, the US Army’s DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory and Imperial College London. Their work spans frontline and counter-UAS systems, eVTOL flight testing, space programs and hardware taken from design to production with industry partners across the US and UK.

**The Polemos Manifesto**

Precision and scale, never traded: For decades, the West has had to choose between weapons that are precise and weapons that exist in numbers. Polemos refuses that choice. We build precision strike designed to be mass-produced.

Propellant is power: No munition flies without it, and supply is one of the West’s deepest bottlenecks. We are building our own propellant production so our output is never capped by someone else’s.

Built for the surge: We design every system for mass manufacturing from the first day, so production can scale with the industrial base when it matters most.

Strength in the network: No single system wins alone. We build everything to connect, coordinate and act as one, because the advantage belongs to whoever links their capabilities fastest.

Every round guides itself: AI guidance carries each round from launch to target and takes over in the terminal phase, where precision is decided. Intelligence goes into the munition itself, not just the systems around it.

Precision at scale is how the West stays ahead. Polemos is building it.

As we scaled, it was expensive to resolve factory-wide bottlenecks quickly and it became harder to stay competitive on price. 

Other companies are trying to layer AI agents on top of legacy ERPs to do logistics work, but the underlying data architectures limit how much those agents can understand and do. So we’re building a new ERP from the ground up for the era of AI.

Organizely continuously improves over time, suggesting new ways for manufacturers to reduce costs and produce more with their existing facilities and teams. It's the whole factory solved. 

We’ve deployed to factories across six U.S. states and now we’re bringing AI to all factories across America. 🇺🇸

launches.body:
We’re Pankaj and Nitish, co-founders of Hesper AI 👋

**TL;DR:** Hesper’s AI agents do the full workup on every insurance claim: read the documents, run the database checks, call the provider, search the web, and hand the adjuster a decision with proof behind every flag. Minutes instead of days, at a fraction of the $1,500 to $2,500 per claim it costs to outsource. If you know anyone who runs claims at a carrier, TPA or MGA, we’d love an intro: [founders@gethesperai.com](mailto:pankaj@gethesperai.com)

<https://youtu.be/XGc5tiN-7Kg?si=X7u6fTBk7WI94GVP>\
\
**❌ The problem**

Claims teams can process 100 files a day. They can’t work 100 files a day.

Working one file properly means calling the provider, verifying their license, reading every invoice line, checking where the photos were taken, searching the parties online, and chasing the documents that never arrived. That is hours of work per claim, and outsourcing it costs $1,500 to $2,500 per claim. So it only happens on the handful of claims that look bad enough to justify it. The rest get a glance and a payment.

This was not solvable with software before. A model could score a claim, but someone still had to make the calls, read the 200 pages and chase the records. Agents can do that part now.

**✅ What we built**

A team of AI agents, each working one piece of the claim and sharing what it finds with the others:

* Document agents read every page (invoices, estimates, medical records, police reports) and check them against each other
* Verification agents check providers and licenses against databases
* A doc collection agent emails, texts and calls the parties for anything missing
* A GPS agent finds where a photo was taken, even with no metadata
* A social mapping agent finds connections between the parties on a claim
* Medical agents review records and medical necessity

Things the agents have caught recently:

🧾 A repair invoice with its total edited after it was issued, and another generated by AI with no real shop behind it\
📞 A clinic claim where the agent called the clinic and found the patient was never seen there\
📍 Damage photos taken 40 miles from the reported loss location

Every flag links back to the page, record or call it came from, so the adjuster can check it in seconds. The adjuster makes the final call, and every decision trains the agents. Models built on insurance data. SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR.

**📈 Where we are**

Claims worth more than $5M already processed. We are live in production with paying customers, and running pilots with carriers, MGAs and TPAs. Our agents have handled everything from pet claims to homeowners claims after Hurricane Isaias. Works across every P&C line.

**💬 Our ask**

Intros to anyone with these titles at a carrier, TPA, MGA or pet insurer:

* Head of Claims, VP Claims, Chief Claims Officer
* SIU Director
* Claims Operations lead
* COO at a TPA

If that’s you, book a demo at [gethesperai.com](http://gethesperai.com) or email [founders@gethesperai.com](mailto:pankaj@gethesperai.com). And tell them not to worry about hallucinations: every flag comes with the evidence it was built on.

**👥 Team**

Pankaj was an engineering manager at Nanonets (YC W17), where he built the AP automation product from zero and grew engineering from 7 to 25. Nitish drove $4M+ ARR at Nanonets and 5x pipeline growth at [Super.AI](http://Super.AI), and runs GTM at Hesper. We talked to 25 claims teams before writing a line of Hesper. Every one said the same thing: we know which claims look off, we have nobody with time to work them.

**TL;DR:** EveryApp is building open source alternatives to every SaaS. It’s a platform to host these open source apps and personal software. Everything runs behind one secure sign-in in your own Cloudflare account.\
\
<https://youtu.be/krDediTp0MI>

**The problem**

“SaaS is dead.”; “Per-seat pricing sucks.” Blah blah blah.

1. People aren’t taking full advantage of agents capabilities because there is too much friction to put web apps & custom agents on the internet
2. 99% of businesses need the same set of basic tools and the tools need to be rebuilt to work with their agents

**Solution**

1. Standardize how to build and deploy web applications & agents for internal use.
2. Build open source versions of every SaaS.

**\
EveryApp**

EveryApp makes two things easy: hosting open-source apps, and hosting custom apps you build with your agent. Your team accesses and manages them through the EveryApp Gateway. 

Today, we’re launching the self hosted version.  Anyone comfortable with coding agents can self host in a few minutes. More on the Managed Service below. 

_Secure by default_

* Every request passes through the Gateway. Apps have no public address. 
* Connect an API once. Apps ask for access, and the Gateway makes the call, so no app ever holds your keys.
* Secured behind Cloudflare Access.

_Scales from zero to infinity_

* Fully serverless, in your own Cloudflare account.
* Apps cost $0 if they aren’t used. 
* Scale up to Cloudflare’s scale if needed.
* $5/month for Cloudflare Paid Plan which can host hundreds of apps.

_Standardized_

* When you add an app, it’s immediately accessible through the Every App MCP Gateway.
* You don’t need to think about infra. Everything must run Cloudflare’s cloud primitives like KV and R2. 
* When building something new, use our preferred tech stack and component library so you don’t need to define patterns yourself.

**Managed EveryApp**

We'll make money by providing this as a managed service. This will start at $10/month, but scale with their usage. First party apps will be pre-loaded. "Custom Deploys" will be one click or agent managed and all the integrations will be pre-configured.

**OpenSEO & more**

I first launched EveryApp in January. It was just the Gateway with no useful apps, nobody had a reason to trust it, and building an app on it was still hard.

So, I set out to build a standalone product that was compelling. That ended up being OpenSEO which now has over 24,000 GitHub stars and thousands of customers who love it.

Coding agents got a lot better since then too. We’re starting to take on building every SaaS that millions of businesses need. In the meantime, building your own app on EveryApp is now something you can do in a few hours while multitasking.

launches.title: Particularity: AI investigators for government regulators
launches.tagline: AI agents that catch consumer protection violations before anyone complains
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're Kavin and Chris.

**TL;DR:** Particularity gives federal, state, and city consumer protection agencies AI agents that check live websites for violations like junk fees, subscription traps, and deceptive ads and turn what they find into court-ready evidence.

<https://youtu.be/f6qVdEjYR9Y>

**What enforcement looks like today**

Chris and I found ourselves frustrated by the deluge of undisclosed advertising on social media (which violates FTC guidelines) and started thinking,“How does a government agency capture the true scope of illicit activity at scale?”

That question led us to find that most consumer protection regulation today still starts with a complaint. Investigators work through an inbox that never empties, while millions of websites change every day. Most people who are harmed never file at all. 

The result is ad hoc enforcement: few companies get caught and often years later. When breaking the rules rarely costs anything, competition stops being about who builds the better product and starts being about who's willing to cheat.

**What Particularity does**

\- **Uncover.** Agents check live websites the way a consumer would. Does the advertised price match checkout? Can you actually cancel online? Every step is captured, timestamped, and hashed.

\- **Investigate.** Every complaint gets a first-pass investigation within the same minute, matched against evidence already on file.

\- **Act.** Findings map to the elements of the law, so staff can move straight to a warning letter or enforcement action.

**About us**

Kavin worked at a causal inference startup and on consumer protection and capital markets at the Senate Banking Committee. Chris built security and compliance infrastructure at AWS, including services for the EU Sovereign Cloud. \
\
**If you’re a regulator, please reach out!**

We’re interested in talking to consumer protection staff at state AG offices, large city consumer affairs departments, and state agencies. We’d also love to talk to any former FTC or CFPB folks and others generally in the consumer protection space.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Reconero is an AI platform for police departments. Reconero answers policy and law questions in seconds, reviews hours of bodycam footage and pulls out the key moments, and drafts reports from the video. It sits on top of existing records and dispatch systems, so deployment is seamless and pain-free.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/lFBvZeNyzJM>

**Hi! We’re Edward and Riwan. We built Reconero, a platform for law enforcement that automates administrative workflows with AI.**

**The problem**

Officers spend a huge share of every shift on work that isn't policing. Studies have estimated roughly 40% of an officers work is spent behind a desk.

* **Paperwork.** After a DUI arrest, an officer may owe an incident report, a crash report, an implied-consent form and a toxicology request before the end of the shift. Each form repeats the same facts in a different layout.
* **Footage.** A single stop can produce 30 to 40 minutes of bodycam video. Finding the one moment you need means scrubbing through it by hand, and that's before CCTV, dash cam and interview-room footage.
* **Answers.** "Which forms do I need?" and "What does policy say here?" often means a call to a sergeant or digging through general orders mid-shift.
* **Data.** Command staff want a simple answer, like DUI arrests by month or where incidents cluster, but have to wait days for someone to pull a report.

**Reconero**

* **Ask anything, by voice or text.** "I responded to a fatal DUI crash. What forms do I need?" Reconero answers in seconds and cites your department's policy and state law.
* **Reviews every kind of video.** Bodycam, CCTV, dashcam and interview recordings. Reconero scans the whole recording, finds every key moment (sobriety tests, searches, arrests) and timestamps each one, so officers jump straight to it.
* **Writes the paperwork.** Reconero drafts the report narrative from the footage, with each line linked to its timestamp. It also picks the right forms for the case and fills them in. The officer reviews and signs.
* **Any graph from any question.** Ask in plain English and get charts of arrests, case clearance and hotspots in seconds.
* **Sits on top of your RMS and CAD.** Reconero reads the systems you already have. No migration, no rip and replace.

**Team**

Riwan Azeroual and Edward "JiuJiu" Liu started Reconero to give officers back the hours they lose to paperwork. Riwan was in defense at Safran and JiuJiu was studying CS/Eng at Stanford. Reconero is shaped by conversations with over 100 officers about exactly where their time goes.

**Our ask**

* **Intros:** Know a chief or decision-maker at an agency? We’d love to connect!
* **Chiefs and command staff:** Book a demo at [**reconero.com**](http://reconero.com)
* **Officers:** If you've ever lost an evening to paperwork, reply or email [contact@reconero.com](mailto:contact@reconero.com). We want to hear if we can help you.

launches.title: Yam - AI-powered romance simulation games for women
launches.tagline: Be anyone, in any world. Live out your wildest fantasies.
launches.body:
Yam is a gaming platform that turns your wildest romantic fantasies into playable simulation games. Walk into the villa as the new bombshell. Star in your own K-drama. Fall in love with your enemy turned lover. Describe a world and who you want to be, and Yam brings it to life — populated with AI characters who remember you, react to your choices, and have lives of their own. 

Since YC, Yam's beta players have spent **1 million hours on the platform.** Daily active users spend an average of **3+ hours a day** playing.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Dop-PmIi-I>

Hey, we're Shan, Crystal, and Qinyu — three besties and former Meta and TikTok builders who grew up watching anime, bingeing dramas, and reading romance novels, wishing we could jump into our favorite fictional worlds.

We wanted to meet the characters we loved, change the endings that broke our hearts, and be the main character for once. So we built Yam.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126413&key=user_uploads/352249/aceec170-7bc4-4666-80bf-4985482b3053)

**The next generation of entertainment is playable.**

Women have spent decades imagining alternate lives through romance novels, fanfiction, and fandoms — They don’t want to just consume but also shape them and become part of them.

AI is dissolving the boundaries between storytelling, creation, and gameplay. We're building the infrastructure that turns those imagined worlds into playable realities, powered by 3 core systems:

### 🌎 World OS — Worlds That Live and Evolve

World OS turns a simple prompt into an interactive universe, complete with its own setting, characters, relationships, and storylines.

Unlike traditional games with predetermined paths, worlds on Yam evolve dynamically. Relationships shift, conflicts emerge, and events unfold in response to players' actions.

### 🧠 Personality OS — Characters With Minds of Their Own

Personality OS gives every character a distinct personality, memory, values, motivations, and relationships.

Characters don't just respond to messages. They make decisions, form opinions, remember shared experiences, and develop relationships over time. They can fall in love, get jealous, form alliances, or hold grudges.

### 🎮 Game Engine — Turning Infinite Possibilities Into Play

Our AI-native game engine turns open-ended simulations into playable experiences with goals, challenges, and consequences.

It orchestrates character interactions, player actions, and narrative progression in real time — creating everything from dating competitions and love triangles to unexpected betrayals and plot twists.

Together, **World OS creates the universe, Personality OS brings its characters to life, and our Game Engine makes it all playable.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126413&key=user_uploads/352249/c3ae6043-1f88-4965-ae30-0b2893158757)

### What’s Next

We're excited to launch Yam into the public today on web, and iOS and Android app is coming soon!

Fandom is just our starting point. Next, we're creating our own studio-quality original IP and giving creators the tools to turn these worlds, characters, and stories into playable games.

Our vision is to build the next generation of entertainment — where worlds aren't just watched, but lived in, played with, and reimagined by anyone.

### **About Us:**

* **Shan (CEO)** built products at Instagram and MetaMask, and previously founded and scaled a consumer fintech startup to 100K users and $2M ARR in under a year.
* **Qinyu (CTO)** built AI creator tools at TikTok, grew the world's 6th largest Discord server for indie creators, and is a top-ranked gamer in North America.
* **Crystal** led design at Webex and was the first hire at Amesite, helping take the company from zero to IPO in three years.

Come build worlds on Yam 💜

Reach us at [hi@yamstudio.ai](mailto:hi@yamstudio.ai)

name: Ailit
long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype and targeting first deployment in summer 2027.
one_liner: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.

app_answers.question: Describe what your company does in 50 characters or less.
app_answers.answer: Electrifying US rail with swappable batteries

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
American freight rail needs a cheaper, practical alternative to diesel. Electric power must match diesel’s power, range and uptime at a lower cost. The energy system has to operate at all times. Trains can never be allowed to stop because power is unavailable.

What drew us to this problem was how well batteries suit long-distance rail, contrary to popular belief. The potential reduction in total cost of ownership is enormous, trains can handle the weight, and diesel-electric locomotives already use electric motors, meaning we can electrify the existing fleet.

That gives us a practical starting point and a path forward: electrify existing locomotives with Superwagon, build out the battery and swapping network, then use that same infrastructure to support the next generation of fully electric, autonomous locomotives.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Everything that can go electric will go electric. Batteries are getting cheaper, and a new generation of companies is building the energy infrastructure to support them. Freight rail should be part of that future.

Our goal is to make diesel economically obsolete in rail.

If we truly succeed, Ailit becomes the primary way America moves goods at scale: a nationwide electric, autonomous freight network that makes moving heavy loads as cheap and efficient as possible. By connecting  mines, mills, factories and ports, we enable them to produce and move more at lower cost, strengthening American industry.
