launches.title: Native: Artificial intuition for marketing
launches.tagline: Native predicts what you should post, and then runs it across your socials and ads.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! 👋

Ben, Håkon and Trond here, founders of Native (YC F26). 

Today we're introducing Norn, a model that predicts which marketing ideas are outliers, before the content is made. We call it artificial intuition, and have our first model live in Native helping over 2000 companies run their marketing. By dogfooding we've reached $2M ARR within our first 6 months.

<https://youtu.be/YTpaKxp1NOs>

**The problem**

AI has made it much easier to produce text, images and video. But you still have to decide what’s worth saying, which angle fits your brand and what your audience might care about.

Producing more content doesn’t answer those questions. It just produces more noise.

Our bet: knowing what to say becomes more valuable as creating it gets cheaper.

**How Norn works**

Just type in your website. Native gathers your business and brand context, and Norn ranks ideas using four signals:

* Brand personality: your voice, positioning and style
* Social performance: what happened after content was published
* Trends: what people are paying attention to
* Taste: which ideas you approve, rewrite or reject

Norn’s output is an idea: the point to make, the angle and the format. Native uses frontier models to turn it into images, video, ad creatives and social posts. You review the results, and Native handles scheduling and publishing.

The original idea, your feedback and the published result become part of the learning loop.

**Already live**

More than 2,000 businesses use Native, and Norn v1 is already working inside it.

That gives us something useful to build on: feedback from the whole creative process, from the first suggestion to what happens after publishing.

**Why us**

Ben comes from YouTube and agency work, with 15 years in content and marketing. Trond built a marketing agency and founded a music festival. Håkon built machine learning models for visual imagery and brings the AI and engineering background.

Between us, we’ve spent years creating content and building the software behind it. Native brings those experiences together.

**Next: the Norn API**

We’re developing an API so other products can ask for ranked ideas before creating content: a marketing tool, an agency workflow or an AI agent deciding what to make next. Like Jev for marketing.

In the video, we explain the model and where we want to take it.

**Our ask**

If you’re building a product that creates content, join the Norn API waitlist and tell us what you’d build: <https://native.no/norn>

launches.body:
**Shire (YC F26)** turns existing restaurant cameras into a real-time operations layer, giving every restaurant the equivalent of five great general managers. **Shire is live in 13 restaurants and is rapidly growing.**\
\
<https://youtu.be/WyPUArKoZLg>

Restaurants depend on great managers to keep service running smoothly. They watch the floor, notice when guests need attention, keep servers from getting overwhelmed, and make hundreds of small decisions throughout a shift.

But even the best manager can't watch every table at once. Guests wait to order, dirty tables sit empty, and one server gets slammed while another has nothing to do.

Traditional restaurant software doesn't solve this. A POS knows when an order was entered or a check was closed, but almost nothing about what happens in between.

**Shire gives restaurant software eyes.**

Using cameras restaurants already have, Shire understands what's happening across the dining room and helps staff respond in real time. It can:

* Notify servers when guests are ready to order or pay
* Alert staff when tables need clearing
* Seat parties based on each server's live workload
* Help restaurants optimize staffing, reservations, pricing, and table turns using what actually happens during service

This also unlocks a new kind of restaurant software. No more estimating wait times from historical averages: Shire can see how far tables are through their meals. Instead of staffing around last week's sales, restaurants can make decisions based on actual workloads and service patterns.

We believe restaurant software should do more than record transactions. It should understand what's happening in the restaurant and help run it.

**Built by restaurant operators, for restaurant operators**

We're Math, EECS, and MechE dropouts who have spent years working in restaurants. Cameron and Alex have known each other since kindergarten and spent years working together in restaurants. Alex went on to manage two large restaurants, while Cameron worked on the front lines of service. Harshith brings deep technical experience, having published graph research in _Nature_ and built reinforcement learning systems for real-world operations at Bastazo. After a year of building together, the three of us left Duke and Clemson to work on Shire full-time.

**Early results**

Across the restaurants that are live, Shire has reduced table turn time by **12%** on average.

We're now looking to partner with more restaurant owners, operators, restaurant groups, and POS distributors who want to run more efficient restaurants.

launches.title: Silica: Actuators for Physical AI
launches.tagline: Sensitive hardware that helps robots feel the world around them
launches.body:
## **TL;DR**

Silica makes the first actuators that can sense force at an affordable price, so that all robots can feel the world around them. Customers have requested more than 60,000 units within a month of launching pre-orders. 

Our Launch Video: <https://youtu.be/KhL5KK1SEH0>

## **Problem**

The robot arms used to train physical AI can't feel anything lighter than a tennis ball. So the data collected on them doesn't accurately record how hard they push. Torque sensors cost several times more than the actuators, so most arms go without them.

## **Solution**

Our actuators integrate sensors into the gearbox, so the joint can feel objects as light as a paperclip. Our tech only adds a little bit (10–15%) to the price of a standard actuator, so the long tail of the industry can have access to physical intelligence. They’re also integrated right into the actuator, so that you don’t have to add a clunky retro-fit to your designs. 

We've designed three sizes to kick off our platform. They drop into today's low-cost training arms with no redesign required. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125282&key=user_uploads/730778/e5fb7b31-3bf4-4499-885b-404a39c3275b)

Our actuators can go into almost anything that moves: factory robots that assemble parts, lab robots that handle samples, and eventually humanoids. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125282&key=user_uploads/730778/a3b5a2f4-e955-4464-aa4c-5476735c108a)

Long term, we want to make embodied AI in its final form.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125282&key=user_uploads/730778/c6a03639-ecc8-4352-9e4c-52dc23896c20)

## **Team**

Before Silica, I worked in the product design department at Apple, where I developed composite materials for new products. Before Apple, I was the first employee at Artefact, where I helped build the first automated, low-power manufacturing cell for a composite manufacturing process called VARTM.

name: Latent
long_description: Latent catches wrong or unsupported LLM answers before they reach your users. Instead of running a second model to check every output, it reads the model's own internal state as it generates, so every request is verified with no added latency, no extra inference cost, and nothing leaving your deployment. Teams running LLMs in production, in finance, legal, healthcare and customer support, get a review queue of the answers most likely to be wrong, calibrated to their own model and traffic, with a plain explanation of why each one was flagged.

launches.title: Latent - Stop hallucinations before they reach your customers
launches.tagline: Catch your AI's wrong answers before your customers see them.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! I'm [Vedant Gaur](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vedantgaur/) from [Latent](https://runlatent.ai/).

**TL;DR: Latent catches your AI's wrong answers before your users see them. It reads signals inside the model while it answers, scores every response, and stops the ones about to be wrong. It works with any model and costs over 500x less than an LLM judge.**

Website: [runlatent.ai](http://runlatent.ai)\
Start free: [app.runlatent.ai](http://app.runlatent.ai)

[Demo](https://youtu.be/Dd8cez0CIDY)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123748&key=user_uploads/1788540/af18344d-59fb-4a63-9f84-65e38f95a216)

**The Problem:**

AI fails quietly. A model gives a fluent, confident answer that's wrong: the wrong dosage, a refund policy that doesn't exist, a clause that isn't in the contract. Latency is fine, the dashboard is green, and the model passed last week's evals. You find out when a customer does.

The usual fix is a second LLM that re-reads the output. That's slow and expensive, so most teams only check a sample, and everything outside it ships unchecked. In healthcare, finance, insurance, and legal, that gap is what keeps AI out of production.

**What We're Doing:**

**1. Reading the model while it answers**\
Latent scores every answer from signals inside the model. On self-hosted models, a read-only hook reads the hidden state as tokens are generated, with no added latency. On API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, a lightweight reader model scores each answer in milliseconds.

**2. Stopping wrong answers before anyone sees them**\
You decide what happens per model: hold the answer and show a fallback, re-ask a stronger model, or send it to a review queue with the reason attached. About 95% of what Latent flags is a real error.

**3. Checking every answer instead of a sample**\
Our classifier costs over 500x less than an LLM judge, so you can run it on all of your traffic. That catches 4x more hallucinations than checking a sample.

**4. Getting sharper on your data**\
Every answer your team confirms or clears becomes a label, so Latent calibrates to your traffic and improves the more you use it.

**5. Fitting into your stack**\
\`pip install runlatent\` wraps the model calls you already make, or you can point traffic at our OpenAI-compatible gateway. Self-hosted models run it as a vLLM plugin. Use it hosted, or run everything in your own cloud with nothing leaving your environment.

**The team:**

I'm a solo founder. At Penn (M&T), I published interpretability research at ACL, EMNLP, and NeurIPS on what a model's internals reveal that its outputs don't. Latent is the production version of that work. Before this, I worked on post-training at Amazon and Robinhood.

**Asks:**

If this sounds like your stack, I'd love to work with you. Reach out if you're:

* Running long-running agents, where one bad step early can derail everything after it.
* Doing research or continual learning, and want a signal the moment a model starts going wrong.
* Shipping AI in healthcare, finance, insurance, legal, or anywhere else a wrong answer is expensive.
* Paying for LLM judges or human review and want to cut that bill.

Intros help too. If you know someone leading AI at a company in one of those industries, I'd be grateful for a connection.

Email me at [vedant@runlatent.ai](mailto:vedant@runlatent.ai), or book time at [runlatent.ai](http://runlatent.ai).

launches.title: Odin Robotics: Robot arms that do repetitive manual work in existing factories
launches.tagline: AI-powered robotic automation that adapts to your factory, not the other way around
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We put robot arms into existing factories to automate repetitive work: machine tending, packing, and palletizing. They fit into the line you already have and adapt as your work changes.

Hi! We are [Alper](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alper-sametoglu) and [Samriddhi](https://linkedin.com/in/samriddhi-simi-s-1240321b5/), co-founders at [Odin Robotics](https://odin-robotics.com/).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-Mein4nAlA>

**Why the work stays manual** 

Traditional automation means rebuilding the factory around the robot. It's built for one product running the same way millions of times. Most factories don't work like that. They run many products, change over often, and handle parts that never show up exactly the same way twice. Robots that only follow a fixed program break the moment anything changes, so the work stays manual.

**What's in the demos**

* **Machine tending:** fully automated tending of a CNC mill. The robot loads raw parts, runs the cycle and unloads finished parts, with no operator needed.
* **Conveyor packing:** food containers picked off a moving conveyor and packed into totes in real time.

**Our approach** 

The best software combines deterministic code, trained models, and LLMs. Robotics is no different. Programmed controls run the steps that must be exact every time: machine doors, fixtures, safety zones. Learned skills handle everything that varies: new parts, mixed products, cluttered bins, and items that are soft or irregular. Our robots don't need every part perfectly placed. They handle the real variation of a working factory. Every deployment adds reusable skills and machine integrations, so each new factory goes live faster than the last.

**How to work with us**

1. **Show us the job:** the task, a photo or video of the setup, and current volume.
2. **We scope it:** scope, price, timeline, and safety guardrails, agreed up front.
3. **We deliver the full setup:** robot, end effector, sensors, and integration, installed on the existing line.

**Team**

Simi founded GirlsCanCode at 13 and grew it into a government-funded program. She has worked on robots ranging from humanoids to industrial arms, and left Electrical Engineering at ETH Zurich to build Odin.

Alper worked at a manufacturing intelligence startup in high school, built supersonic rockets and satellite propulsion valves, then turned down NASA JPL to deploy robots on Earth.

**Our ask:** Run or know a factory with repetitive loading, packing, or palletizing work? 

Send us the job, and we'll show you how it can be automated 📩 [**founders@odin-robotics.com**](mailto:founders@odin-robotics.com)

name: Graphide
long_description:
Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification pipelines the new bottleneck. Graphide builds that verification, starting with CI.

Graphide CI runs faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and always-on agents tune machines, caches and test splits together, around the clock. Optionally, we also patch the tests themselves with our own libraries so they run faster. We have seen most of our customers cut CI time 80-95% compared to their existing setups.

Our PR review agent then runs the old and new code in our live environments, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests, as well as analyzing synthetic and production data through the PR before it merges.

Finally, our visualizer allows you to see these data flows and graph based diffs to both easily analyze the found bugs, run custom data flows, and see / understand a PR in seconds.

Graphide's focus is on verifying the code agents write.
one_liner: CI 10-20× faster than GitHub runners, with a 24/7 agent optimizing it.

launches.title: Kanopy - spatial intelligence for physical infrastructure
launches.tagline: We monitor critical infrastructure using only video
launches.body:
TL;DR: Utilities plan operations using field data that can be years out of date. Kanopy uses computer vision to turn ordinary video into a 3D model of the grid, helping teams map tree risks, assess asset condition, and plan maintenance. We’ve already deployed across thousands of miles of power lines.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VFx7_ZF07nI>

**The problem**

There are roughly 100 million miles of above-ground linear infrastructure worldwide. The electricity grid alone accounts for \~60 million miles (equivalent to 2,500 times around the equator). Infrastructure is aging, the cost of failure is higher than ever, and the systems we rely on are too vast to monitor manually.

For utilities, vegetation management makes this challenge concrete. Arborists patrol power lines to identify dangerous trees and determine what needs cutting. Contractors estimate the work using manual surveys and historical averages. Once crews finish trimming, utilities send people back to verify the work. \
Planning the work and executing these multiple inspections take millions in spent resources.

**What Kanopy does**

Kanopy turns ordinary video from any camera into a detailed 3D model of the grid. The video can come from a drone, a GoPro on a truck, or simply from an iPhone shot.\
Our models measure vegetation clearances, identifies hazards, and assesses asset condition. Utilities use these insights to prioritize maintenance, plan fieldwork, and verify completed work. Each new drive or flight can refresh that picture using cameras teams already own.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125913&key=user_uploads/4010388/8d098664-36f4-487c-8c3d-ff9160ba2dc0)

**The team**

We’re Yann and Nicolas Pfitzer, brothers and founders of Kanopy

Yann spent more than five years at McKinsey as a Junior Partner working with utilities and energy companies\
Nicolas brings computer vision and robotics experience from work at ShapeScale (YC15), ETH Zürich, and research at University of Cambridge.

Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems like the EHR, REDCap, and wearable platforms, reading notes chart by chart, and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets. Sutrix automates that work by deploying AI systems within each team’s own environment, linking patient records across sources, applying the study's rules, and flagging unclear cases for staff to review.

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

We're brothers who've built together for 4 years. We first solved this problem doing forward-deployed work at HSS, where we built an injury surveillance system now used by 700+ teams. Ritvik's clinical research at HSS and Emory showed us every research team has the same bottleneck. Supratik previously founded Kairo (a16z Speedrun, exited) and built production AI agents at Amazon.

launches.title: Sutrix: AI that turns patient data into study-ready datasets
launches.tagline: Cut data prep time by 80% for healthcare research teams.
launches.body:
Hey YC community! 👋

We’re [Ritvik](https://www.ycombinator.com/founders/ritvik-panuganti) and [Supratik](https://www.ycombinator.com/founders/supratik-panuganti), brothers and co-founders of [Sutrix](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/sutrix). We turn EHR records, surveys, and wearable data into analysis-ready datasets for healthcare research teams.

### **TL;DR**

Patient records documents care as it happened, but the information a study needs is often scattered across notes, visits and systems. Each study has its own criteria, time windows and outcome definitions. When those requirements change or new data arrives, teams have to rework datasets, delaying answers about which treatments work best and for whom. Sutrix deploys AI software to turn the team’s existing data into study-ready datasets. It flags unclear cases for review with supporting evidence and lets teams reuse the preparation workflow across analyses as records or study definitions change. Across 10+ institutions, it has cut data preparation time by 80%, helping teams build evidence faster for more personalized care.

**_Ask:_** Know a healthcare research team spending more time preparing data than analyzing it? We’d love an intro: [founders@sutrix.ai](mailto:founders@sutrix.ai).

Check out our launch video 👇

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j-EwkyX0_0o>

**❌ The problem**

Healthcare research teams have no shortage of patient data. However, it is scattered across EHRs, clinical notes, surveys, and wearables, with different identifiers, codes, units, and time points. Bringing it together requires understanding what each record means. An unusual measurement could be a unit mismatch or an entry error. A blank response could be missing or intentionally skipped. Those cases need different handling, and the wrong choice can change the results.

Each study adds its own definitions of which patients qualify, which observations count, and how outcomes are calculated. Teams need to trace those decisions to source records and study rules, apply them to new data, and revisit them when the study changes. That repeated interpretation and checking keeps studies waiting for months, even when the analysis itself is straightforward.

### **What Sutrix does**

Sutrix carries your study’s definitions through the full workflow: pulling records, preparing the analysis table, reviewing exceptions, and keeping it up to date.

**_1. Connect and reconcile the source data_**

Sutrix brings together patient data from EHRs, clinical notes, surveys, wearables, and other study sources. It links each patient’s records and standardizes codes, units, and formats.

![uploaded image](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/d/1td_wwCkgXfQg7x8dollFcpB9WB58ye08)

Inspect the source, rule, and conversion behind a prepared value. Unclear cases go to your team for review, with the evidence attached.

**_2. Build the dataset your study needs_**

Apply a saved definition set or specify the study’s rules. Sutrix builds the cohort, derives the required variables, and produces the analysis table with one row per patient, visit, or time period.

![uploaded image](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/d/1vHPjU2XMtMYabn8Rim-dmS2soUaP39wc)

When new records arrive, run them through the same preparation rules. When definitions change, update the rules and regenerate the affected cohort, variables, or time windows. Then run the analysis on the revised dataset.

### **Results**

Across **10+ institutions**, we’ve cut data cleaning and preparation time by **80%**, giving healthcare research teams a faster path to the evidence they need to tailor care for patients.

### **Why us**

We’ve built together for four years. Before [Sutrix](https://www.sutrix.ai/), we built an injury surveillance system at Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS), now used by 700+ teams. We saw this preparation work firsthand and fixed it.

[**Ritvik**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ritvik-panuganti-739822273/) **(CEO):** Published clinical researcher at HSS, Emory, and Georgia Tech. Led a 300-participant, IRB-approved concussion study.

[**Supratik**](http://www.linkedin.com/in/supratik-panuganti-4732532a4) **(CTO):** Founded and exited a company backed by a16z Speedrun, built production AI agents at Amazon, and left Georgia Tech at 18.

### **🙏 Our ask**

If you run or support a healthcare research team, we’d love to talk. If you know someone who does, we’d appreciate an intro.

Email us at [founders@sutrix.ai](mailto:founders@sutrix.ai)

launches.tagline: OpEra: The AI decision engine for factories, warehouses and fleets
launches.body:
**TL;DR: OpEra helps operations teams make the best decision at every step of the supply chain: what to produce, what to stock, which orders go on which truck, who works which shift. We build custom AI decision engines that re-plan when reality changes: a sick employee, a broken machine, a new regulation.**

**🎬 Launch Video**: <https://youtu.be/3wfSc84J8b4>

Hi, we're Hindy and Bernardo. We met at MIT's Operations Research Center, where we worked on delivery routing for a major retailer. On their data, **our model cut transportation costs by 38%**. More projects followed, and **we turned down offers from Palantir, Mercor and Stack AI to build OpEra.**

**🏭 The problem**

Every day, companies decide what to produce, how much stock to hold, which orders go on which trucks and who works which shift. Most still **plan in spreadsheets, or in software built for the average factory or warehouse. But no two operations are the same.** Generic rules produce workable plans, not the best ones, and **the gap is real money and real waste**. And when a machine breaks, a truck runs late or an order changes, someone rebuilds the plan by hand, and more is lost.

**🧠 What OpEra does**

**OpEra connects to your existing systems (WMS, ERPs, Excel) and builds an optimization model of your operation: equipment, people, capacity and rules.** From that model it produces your **production schedules**, **warehouse plans** and **delivery routes**. When something changes, your planner describes it in plain language, in the interface or to the OpEra agent, and the plan is recomputed around the new constraints.

• **38% lower delivery cost and 10% more on-time deliveries** for a major retailer

• **10.4% higher premium over market on the same volume** for a global sugar producer

• **54% fewer unfulfilled orders** for a services marketplace

**🏅 Why us**

We're **operations researchers from MIT**. Bernardo built **optimization models at Sanofi and did AI research at BMW**. Hindy did **machine learning research on nuclear fusion at MIT**, on a Los Alamos-sponsored project, and built the **hallucination-detection system used by thousands of consultants at McKinsey.**

If your team plans production, a warehouse or deliveries in spreadsheets or in pre-AI software (WMS, ERPs, etc.), we'd love to **deploy OpEra at one of your sites**. And if you know a **COO, VP of Supply Chain, plant manager or head of logistics** with this problem, we'd appreciate an intro.

launches.title: Papaya - Continuous Optimization for your AI agents
launches.tagline: Papaya finds what's hurting your agent's quality, cost, and latency, and fixes it for you.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! 👋 \
\
We're Macy, Faiz and Niyaz - co-founders of[ Papaya](https://papaya.fyi) 

**TL;DR**

Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Connect your production agent and Papaya watches every action, finds what's hurting quality, cost, and latency, and gives you the fix. Once a fix is in place, Papaya makes sure your agent doesn't regress. Teams running Papaya are seeing 20%+ improvements to quality, latency, and cost.

**Ask:** If you run an agent in production, connect it to Papaya. [Grab a time to get started here](https://cal.com/macy-mody/macy-papaya).

<https://youtu.be/cG9iIVB5Psk>

**The Problem**

We’ve been building agentic systems for years (6 years to be exact…before it was cool), including really large ones that helped run major workflows inside Amazon. We know firsthand that the hard part isn’t getting an agent to work, it’s keeping it working at a high quality bar. We consistently saw that every model update and every prompt change shifted behavior in ways nobody caught until something downstream looked wrong. The only way to find out what changed was to pull traces and read them by hand.

Most companies shipping agents today are focused on the next feature for customers and they don't have time to fully maintain what's already been released. When we built our own agent as a three-person team, we hit the same wall. We needed to make sure our agent had high quality answers, was fast for our customers, and as low cost as possible, but we had to look at everything by hand. Every hour we spent examining traces was an hour we couldn’t spend on new product development. That's why we built Papaya.

**How Papaya works 🔧** 

At Papaya, our goal is to do the hard AI engineering work for you, staying up to date on the latest and greatest research so you can take advantage of this knowledge through optimizations. Simply stream your production traces through a lightweight SDK. From there, Papaya:

* **Finds your use cases**: groups every run by the job the agent is doing, so you're looking at "refund requests," not "run 4812."
* **Runs 200+ analyses**: checks every use case against 200+ research-backed failure patterns across quality, cost, and latency.
* **Ranks the fixes by impact**: every recommendation comes with an estimated effect on quality, latency, and cost. Approve the ones you want directly in Papaya and Papaya opens the PR.
* **Watches for regression**: once a fix ships, Papaya keeps checking that the improvement holds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115486&key=user_uploads/2135001/0a49f356-ac11-44d5-bcc1-69caf4ba64d9)

**Our Ask 🙏**

* Run an agent in production? Connect it to Papaya. [Grab a time with us here](https://cal.com/macy-mody/macy-papaya).
* Know any companies spending tons of time maintaining and fixing their agents? Intro us at [macy@papaya.fyi](mailto:macy@papaya.fyi).
* Building agents and want a second set of eyes? Ping us. We are happy to help however we can!

**The Team**

We've spent over 10 years building large scale agentic systems at Amazon, and we've scaled other YC startups from $0 to $10M ARR through acquisition. We started out building an analytics agent. The harness we built to optimize our own agent became the center of every prospect conversation, so we pivoted to it. Meet our team below :)

launches.title: Sinter: Accelerated Plastics Manufacturing
launches.tagline: The Fastest End-Use Plastic Parts in the World
launches.body:
Sinter accelerates plastics manufacturing with 48 hour injection molding production. Our additive tooling delivers end use plastics 10x faster and 10x cheaper than traditional methods, allowing teams to scale and iterate at previously unattainable rates for hardware development.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125314&key=user_uploads/3253127/79de7420-d976-4019-8cff-9f180f8c3c86)

We unlock these unit economics by building tooling with additive processes. Rather than using a traditional machined approach, our tooling is printed additively with photopolymer resin. They remain fully compatible with existing infrastructure while significantly lowering time and cost to manufacture, allowing even single digit part runs, something unheard of in the injection molding space.

In our first month, we’ve helped companies produce over 500 kg of parts, seeing companies through first prototype to mass production tooling without forfeiting their ability to iterate.

Justin and Oliver met online at 13 building custom formulated mechanical keyswitches to the tune of 5 figure months, and have been immersed in plastics manufacturing ever since. We both dropped out of college (before we got into YC!), and spent 4 months this summer living on the floor of an illegal, ant infested El Segundo warehouse to make Sinter come to life.

launches.title: ObsessionDB: a real-time data warehouse built for agents
launches.tagline: Give your agents the data stack they need
launches.body:
Hi YC, we are Marc, Rafael, and Marc - co-founders of ObsessionDB.

**TL;DR:** ObsessionDB is a real-time data warehouse that makes your data stack agent-ready. Your agents can ingest and query vast amounts of data in seconds, without the scary infra bill.

<https://youtu.be/1AFlb772hl4>

**Why now**

Agents are the new heaviest users of your data warehouse. They generate data nonstop, scan it millions of times a day, and provision their own infra. Existing data warehouses and data platforms weren't built for these workloads. We see this as a generational opportunity, and we're building it.

Warehouses and data platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks are built for batch jobs and get expensive fast at this volume. Operational, transactional databases fall short. Without a scalable, cost-effective solution, teams end up rationing their data instead of building on it.

Companies shouldn't fear their fast-growing data.

**What ObsessionDB does**

ObsessionDB allows data teams to ingest, process, and query all their growing data:

* **Agent data to insights:** messy transcripts, logs, and traces become structured, queryable data as they arrive, fast, in real time
* **Real-time analytics** on huge, fast-moving datasets
* **Real-time customer-facing APIs** served directly on that data, fast enough to power products, not just dashboards
* **Scale without the bill scaling with it:** Built on top of our own compute-storage implementation for ClickHouse t

**In production today**

* **We are processing millions of real-time API requests for our customers,** turning their AI agents' session transcripts into live, queryable data and building real-time APIs on top.
* Our biggest customer moved off Elasticsearch and now serves real-time APIs on **50TB of data**, ingesting **hundreds of thousands of events per minute**.

**Why us: we've already run this at petabyte scale**

At our last company, we built real-time blockchain APIs on **petabytes of data** and hit a wall with every warehouse on the market, both on cost and on speed. So we took the open-source ClickHouse® engine, forked it, and rebuilt it with compute and storage separated: one copy of the data on cheap object storage, with stateless compute on top. ObsessionDB is that system, productized and built for the agent era.

**Our ask**

* **Building with AI agents and sitting on a growing pile of transcripts, traces or logs?** Let us help you extract more value.
* Is Postgres getting too slow for your analytical workloads? Talk to us.
* **Paying too much for Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, or ClickHouse Cloud?** We can help you cut it in half; reach out.

launches.title: Asim: Find your robot’s safety limits before deployment
launches.tagline: We test real robots under changing physical conditions to uncover failures before deployment around people.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re Douglas, Raphaël, Maëlic and Tristan, the founders of[ Asim](https://www.asim-group.com) (YC F26).

**TL;DR**

We’re building standardized benchmarks for physical intelligence: how well robots handle objects, coordinate movements and adapt when conditions change. We test real robots to help engineering teams measure their capabilities, understand their limitations and identify safety risks before deployment.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwA0V_8gfnU>

**The problem**

A robot picks up a glass perfectly in the lab. Then the glass is heavier, the surface is slippery, or someone reaches into its workspace. Does it still behave safely?

Completing a task in one setting doesn’t tell us how reliably a robot will perform when conditions change. A success-or-failure score alone doesn’t explain what caused a failure or how to prevent it.

As robots increasingly operate around people, understanding those limits is critical to safety.

**Our solution**

At Asim, we systematically vary objects, tasks and environments in the real world to find the conditions where robot behavior breaks down.

Our testing examines three things:

* Adaptability: how performance changes when we vary physical properties such as shape, weight, friction and material.
* Robustness: how reliably robots grasp objects, coordinate movements and respond to unexpected changes.
* Failure conditions: which changes a robot can handle, which cause failures and when those failures become safety risks.

Robotics teams get actionable feedback on their robots’ limits for safer deployment around people.

**Why us**

We’re four founders, including three PhD researchers, two specializing in robotics. Our backgrounds include Sony and NASA JPL, world-class research in machine learning and human–robot interaction, and two RoboCup@Home championship wins.

**Our shared mission: enable robots to operate safely in the real world.**

**Our asks**

* **Building or deploying robots? We’d love to hear which tasks and failure modes are hardest for your team to test.**
* **Intros to robotics engineering teams: CTOs, Heads of Robotics and VPs of Engineering preparing robots for deployment around people.**
* **Reach us: email [contact@asim-group.com](mailto:contact@asim-group.com) with the task or failure mode you’re struggling to test.**

**Asim. Benchmarking physical intelligence.**

Sona8 uses AI voice agents to interview employees about how work gets done. Consulting, transformation and corporate development teams use it to hear from more people and follow up after changes.

Employees open a link and speak in their own language. The agent asks follow-up questions, and teams compare problems across sites and departments. We’ve completed 10,000+ employee interviews and signed one of the world’s top three consulting firms.

Thilo and I worked together at BCG, interviewing employees and repeatedly going back to them during implementation. On our evening runs, we started asking whether AI could make those conversations possible across an entire company.

We started building after BCG, while I was at MIT and Thilo was researching conversational AI at TUM. As pilots gained traction, we both left our programs. Madeleine brought her experience as a self-taught engineer, repeat founder and former principal engineer at McKinsey QuantumBlack.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every major decision depends on context. Much of it sits with employees who know how work happens and why things fail, but that knowledge rarely reaches the people deciding what to change.

We’re building Sona8 into the operating system for strategy and transformation teams. We will combine what our voice agents learn from employees with company data to build a live model of the organization. Teams will use it to compare alternatives and understand what a decision would require across sites and departments.

The same model will be the context layer for AI automation. Sona8 will use it to deploy agents and coordinate execution, then learn from the results. Small teams will be able to steer company-wide change, with the organization keeping what it learns as people and agents move on.

launches.title: Sona8: Understand, improve, and automate workflows
launches.tagline: We turn what employees explain in interviews and show on screen or through a phone camera into workflow maps that AI agents can use as a context layer
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Sona8 maps company’s workflows with the employees who know them best. Employees explain and show their day to day work to Sona8’s agent: in a conversation, on a screen share, through the phone camera, or by letting Sona8 record the steps in the background while they work. This produces a concrete records of processes used to fix inefficiencies and guide AI agents to automate them.

<https://youtu.be/yZFELAnWr0A>

**🧩 The problem**

The bottleneck for automation is domain knowledge. LLMs have the reasoning capabilities, but they lack the operational context. E.g., how a quote gets approved, which exceptions matter, who gets called when the system is wrong; this knowledge lives in people’s heads, in email threads or old excel files. People remember it, but agents can’t read it. So automating one step creates new problems next to it, because the automation doesn’t match how the work is done.

**🛠️ What we’re building**

Employees explain and show their day-to-day work to our agent, in a conversation, on a screen share or through the phone camera. It asks follow-up questions where something is unclear and produces a map of the workflow as it runs today, exceptions included. Teams pull these maps into Claude, ChatGPT or their own agents via MCP to improve processes and give AI agents instructions.

**🆕 What’s new**

Employees can now share their screen, point a phone camera at physical tasks, or let our agent record the steps in the background while they work.

**📈 Where this goes**

1. **Consulting projects.** That’s where this knowledge gets collected today. We’ve signed one of the world’s top three consulting firms (MBB). They use Sona8 to map their clients’ processes.
2. **Then enterprises directly.** Strategy and transformation teams run the mapping themselves. Right now, process knowledge dies in a slide deck when a project ends. With Sona8, the map stays alive inside the company.
3. **Finally the agents.** The live map becomes their infrastructure. Before an agent takes over a task, it reads the current execution logic for that step. When the human workflow changes, the map updates with it. Every project adds to the same company brain.

**👋 Team**

At BCG & McKinsey, we helped companies map their processes and identify what to improve. The answers were always with the people doing the work, rarely in the documentation.

We’ve completed more than 10,000 employee interviews and signed one of the top three consulting firms.\

Companies will try a lot of AI agents and automation tools in the next few years. Each one needs to know how the work is done before it changes anything, and most of that isn't written down. Sona8 creates infrastructure for AI automation tools. Over time we are building a live context graph of workflows by reading the systems a company already uses and connecting them to what employees say. \

launches.tagline: Track finger movement and estimate fingertip force while people work.
launches.body:
**We’re building training data for dexterous robots by recording the muscle signals behind skilled human hand movements.**

We’re Max and Arsh, founders of Axonnic (YC F26). Our wearable forearm sleeve reads electrical activity from muscles to track finger movements and estimate fingertip force, while leaving the hands completely free.

<https://youtu.be/iyKoL_kfyKU>

Video shows where a hand moves. EMG adds information about muscle activation and effort, including when the hand is hidden from view.

![](https://ph-files.imgix.net/8d8d84de-dce6-4fde-9d52-8dede1c7c5ae.png?auto=compress,format&codec=mozjpeg&cs=strip)

When the hand goes inside the box, camera-based tracking loses sight of it. Axonnic keeps decoding finger movement from forearm EMG. We’ve also demonstrated live control of a robotic hand from those signals.

We synchronize EMG with video and hand pose to build training datasets from skilled people doing real work. The tasks we’re targeting include guiding fabric through a sewing machine, handling an electrician’s tools, and positioning small parts during delicate assembly.

**Why we’re building this**

Max studied Biology (MBiol) at Oxford, where his research on high-density surface EMG alignment earned the highest research mark in his cohort. He is now publishing that work as a first-author paper. He saw Skyscanner grow from its early days into a unicorn through to its sale, and also built internal tools there. As an early employee at Voxblock, he worked across PCB development and supply chain.

Arsh studied medicine at Oxford, has published clinical research, and has worked on machine learning for cancer and stroke imaging. He also wrote control software for OxRAM’s undergraduate quadruped robot and previously helped build Medical Advice GPT, which passed 10,000 user interactions. His background brings together machine learning, robotics and biological systems.

Sleeves are shipping and paid pilots are underway with our first design partners. We’re opening a few more spots.

Building robot hands, training robotics models, or running a factory with a dexterous task you can’t automate? We want to hear from you.

launches.title: Composal: A swarm of agents that tests your product like real users
launches.tagline: Catch bugs before your users do
launches.body:
Composal sends a swarm of agents through your product to check that users can still do what they came to do. When something breaks, it captures a recording, logs and steps to reproduce, so your coding agent can make the fix and Composal can verify it.

We're Pandelis, Jonathan and Jan, the founders of Composal (YC F26). We're building the verification scaffolding for autonomous software factories: the part of the loop that is still reliant on humans today, checking whether what the agents built actually works.

<https://youtu.be/MmnVcWLlnAQ>

### The Problem

Coding agents have made building cheap. Checking has not kept up. Teams tell us about features that pass CI and get approved by a review bot, then fail the first time a real person tries them. So someone still clicks through every flow by hand before a release, or skips it and hears about the bug from a customer.

End-to-end test suites were supposed to solve this. In practice they are tedious to write, they break every time the UI changes, and they are the first thing to rot. As agents raise the pace of shipping, that gap widens every week.

### How Composal works

Give Composal an environment to test and the credentials it needs. Our agents learn your product by using it, mapping features and exploring user journeys in parallel with different roles and goals.

For example, testing an invitation flow means following what happens to the person receiving the invite: can they join the right workspace and reach the features they need? A successful API response only answers part of that question.

When an agent finds a problem, Composal captures the evidence. Your coding agent uses it to investigate and make a fix, then runs the scenario again to confirm the result. What Composal learns becomes product knowledge and repeatable scenarios that keep running as your product changes.

We call this **Continual Agent Verification**: checking that users can still accomplish their goals as the product evolves.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125454&key=user_uploads/239422/b7775a00-5c12-4e9b-811d-63d111ca960d)


CI checks code, CD ships it, Continual Agent Verification checks that user goals still work as the product changes.

### Why we're working on this

Pandelis spent the last few years building coding agents as CTO at Cosine (YC W23). That team was no different from the teams we talk to now: ship a feature, test what changed, move on, then onboard a customer and find that a flow nobody had touched in weeks was broken. The agents kept getting faster. The checking stayed manual. Composal is the tool we wished we had.

### Who we are

* **Pandelis Zembashis**: previously CTO at Cosine, where he built one of the first CLI agent harnesses, sandboxed execution from scratch, and large-scale repository mirroring for model training.
* **Jonathan Davies**: built mission-critical software for Telefónica, Vodafone and Mitie.
* **Jan Moehlmann**: built commercial functions at 11x, Encord (YC W21) and Tractable.

We worked closely together at previous startups in London, and we keep hearing the same question from customers: how do you know an agent's work is ready for your users?

### Where this goes

Our ambition is a self-healing software factory: you set the direction and agents carry the work from idea through building, testing and shipping, then keep improving the product. Verification is the first step, because nothing else in that loop can be trusted without it. 

Build, Verify, Ship, Improve: a fault is caught and healed without stopping the loop.

### Try it on a feature you're about to ship

If your team uses coding agents and still checks their work by hand, we'd like to test an upcoming feature with you.

[**Start at**](https://composal.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=launch_yc) [**composal.com**](http://composal.com) to run your first discovery, or book a call with us directly and we would be happy to setup your first batch of tests for you.

— Pandelis, Jonathan and Jan

launches.body:
Hi everyone, we’re Sonny and Tung, the founders of Verdun.

**TL;DR:** Verdun is a remote video monitoring service. AI agents review every camera alarm then escalate real threats to trained operators who coordinate police or guard response. 

**Video:** <https://youtu.be/UmI3OZjt4Ac>

**The problem:** Most commercial properties have cameras, and almost nobody is watching them. Even the cameras that are monitored aren’t being watched effectively, because monitoring centers are poorly equipped to handle peak activity. 

Monitoring centers can’t instantly add headcount when alarms spike, so they mute noisy sites and bulk dismiss alarms hoping that they didn’t just wave off a true threat. 

Verdun’s AI agents monitor security cameras for businesses and analyze behavior and context before escalating high probability threats to our trained operators. Unlike traditional video analytics, which flag every person or vehicle that crosses the frame, our agents judge whether the activity is normal for that site and time of day.

**How it works:**

* **AI triage:** false alarms are dismissed with the reason written down, and real threats are flagged in seconds.
* **Trained human operators:** An operator trained on your site’s protocol confirms the threat, pulls up the live view, and decides the response: a voice-down, a call to your contacts, or police or guard dispatch.
* **Voice-down:** AI voice agents and operators warn intruders off through on-site horn speakers.
* **Reporting:** camera health, incident breakdowns, response times and a full log of every single agent and operator decision.

**About us:** Sonny is a former U.S. Marine officer and repeat founder who previously scaled a computer vision object detection company to over 100,000 cameras. 

Tung holds a PhD in applied math, is a National Math Olympiad Gold Medalist, and was a senior AI engineer at LinkedIn, VergeSense (YC S17) and WeWork.

**Our ask:** intros to multi-site businesses with cameras (especially car dealership groups) and to security dealers and integrators who sell monitoring. Email [sonny@verdun.ai](mailto:sonny@verdun.ai).

name: Acyclic Labs
long_description:
Acyclic builds the infrastructure for agent swarms: open-source primitives for running agents in parallel, and a managed agents platform that runs swarms for you. Complex, long-running tasks are split across many agents, each working in its own instant fork of the workspace, and finish in a fraction of the time.

We built Acyclic because we believe there are huge gains to be had in how agents are run, beyond the models themselves. Agents can already do real work, but they still do it one step at a time, so complex tasks take hours or days. Running them as swarms is an infrastructure problem: isolating each agent, dividing the work, and merging the results without conflicts. Today, teams use Acyclic to run heavy document-processing pipelines in minutes instead of hours.

At Cambridge, we researched ML and auto-parallelising compilers, and then we built multi-agent systems in production: Ram as a Palantir FDE for pharma clients, shipping systems for clinical trial design, and Varun leading agent architecture at Tracelight for Big 4 accounting firms. We kept asking the same question: the agents were good enough, so why couldn't we run thousands of them at once to make everything faster and cheaper? Acyclic is our answer.
one_liner: Agent swarms that make long-running tasks exponentially faster

launches.title: Clean: Real-time company data for sales teams and their agents
launches.tagline: Know what just changed at every account you sell to, and what to do about it.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Clean watches 1,000+ live sources and keeps a running picture of every company you sell to: what changed, when, why it matters and who to talk to. Our customers have made over $1M in revenue with it. Try it at \[[tryclean.ai](http://tryclean.ai)\](<https://tryclean.ai>).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qZO3QrW57os>

**Sales data is old the day you pull it**

Every sales team works off a snapshot. An Apollo export, a ZoomInfo list, a Clay table, all frozen at one moment. Meanwhile the companies on that list change every week. They open a plant, switch a supplier, hire a new VP. And now everyone's building sales agents that read the same databases and send the same emails, so the gap only gets bigger.

The teams that win will be the ones who know what just changed at an account, and what it means for them. That's what Clean does.

**A real example**

One of our customers makes custom battery packs. A company they wanted to sell to was a hybrid-electric aircraft maker. Over two months, Clean picked up:

\- **Week 0:** they announce a new plant

\- **Week 1:** they sign their engine supplier

\- **Week 8:** they fly their first demo flight

Alone, none of that means much. Together, it means the plane is real, the engine is decided and the battery is the next thing they buy. Clean flagged the account and the person who picks suppliers. He replied to our customer in 15 minutes. They'd signed a battery supplier that same week, and he still wanted to hear more.

That's how small the window is.

**How it works**

1\. **Learns your business** from your docs and website.

2\. **Watches 1,000+ sources:** filings, press releases, spec sheets, hiring posts and more, lined up per company as events happen.

3\. **Tells you what matters:** which accounts are in market, what changed, who decides and how to open. Every signal is sourced.

4\. **Lives where you work:**

   - Your own agents

   - Claude, Codex and your other AI tools

   - Your CRM and sequences

   - Our app

   - Our API and MCP

**More than leads**

Timing is one signal. The same live picture tells you which prospects to prioritize, which customers are ready to expand and which accounts are showing risk. We're building Clean to be the company data layer behind every step of the customer relationship, for humans and agents alike.

**Results**

\- One customer closed **$60K in their first week**

\- Reply rates went from **4% to 19%**

\- Weekly booked meetings are **up 32%**

**Team**

We're four technical, sales-heavy founders. Pavan is a 2x founder who was closing enterprise deals at Cisco straight out of high school, then led growth at a seed-stage startup to $300K+ in revenue and 28M views in six months. Clarissa won the International Physics Olympiad, then turned down a quant offer from Citadel to build Clean. Pratham is a top open-source builder whose app has 10K+ users, and did AI research backed by India's richest person, alongside IIT researchers. Tejas is an operator who previously scaled a startup to $40M, and 2x time as well.

**Our ask**

If you sell B2B, especially into manufacturing, insurance, fintech, legal or infrastructure, book a demo at [tryclean.ai](http://tryclean.ai) or email [yc@tryclean.ai](mailto:yc@tryclean.ai). If you're building sales agents and want live company data behind them, we'd love to talk.

We run **benefits, people ops, and compliance for startups for free**.

Instead of giving founders another piece of software to manage, we give every company dedicated senior HR and benefits specialists who actually do the work, on top of the HRIS they already use — Rippling, Deel, Gusto, ADP, and others.

### **TL;DR**

* Dedicated senior HR + benefits specialists working directly with your team in Slack
* Works on top of the HRIS you already use 
* We implement better-fit, more cost-effective health plans and have reduced healthcare costs by around **15% on average**
* We run open enrollment, benefits administration, payroll, compliance, onboarding/offboarding, and employee support 
* It’s free for startups: we become your benefits broker and are paid by insurance carriers

watch here: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T6paMQfwwHU>

### **The problem**

Rippling, Deel, Gusto, and other HR platforms are great software. But someone still has to operate them, deal with issues, coordinate with carriers, answer employee questions, manage compliance, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.

At an early-stage company, it usually falls on the founder, COO, finance lead, or whoever happens to know the most about it. That work quickly becomes a second job.

Software helps. But someone still has to do the work.

### **What we built**

**Spine does the work for you. For free.**

Every company gets a dedicated senior HR lead and benefits specialist who works directly with the team, primarily through Slack, on top of the systems they already use.

We:

* Review your existing health plans and run the market for better options

* Handle compliance, onboarding/offboarding, and ongoing people ops

You don’t need to migrate away from Rippling, Deel, Gusto, ADP, or whatever HRIS you already use. **We operate on top of it.**

For benefits, we become your broker of record. Insurance carriers already pay broker commissions, so we use those commissions to provide the rest of the service for free.

### **Why we started Spine**

We spent years building and operating startups ourselves and kept running into the same problem: as our companies grew, we accumulated more software for payroll, benefits, compliance, and HR, but **the work itself never disappeared**.

We thought startups shouldn’t need to build an internal HR team just to make all of this work.

launches.title: Durable Actors: The perfect primitive for Multiplayer AI and Agent Coordination
launches.tagline: OSS alternative to Durable Objects
launches.body:
Hey everyone, Thomas & Olivier here, founders of Terse (<https://www.useterse.ai/>).\
\
We are building the next Agent Infra company and we are announcing our first product: Durable Actors. An open source alternative to Durable Objects.\
\
Star us on Github! <https://github.com/TerseAI/durable-actors>\
\
Durable Actors help you build real-time applications like chat systems (e.g. ChatGPT, Codex), collaboration tools (e.g. Notion), and agent swarms (e.g. Devin).

They provide _stateful serverless functions_, a foundational building block that abstracts away persistence, coordination, and infrastructure challenges in distributed systems.\
\
Why is this useful? It reduces complexity tremendously and It saves you a lot of money!\
\
Our actors go dormant and back up in S3 when not in use. So agents only incur cost when your users are getting value from them. Because each actor has its own database and websocket server, we remove a ton of pressure from your main DB as well as your websocket server and you can scale those down.\
\
In addition to being cost efficient, they are the perfect tool for building agentic applications. You no longer need to store JSONB in your Postgres DB, no more complicated websocket logic, it handles race conditions elegantly and helps keeps your REST API fully stateless.\
\
Here is me with a whiteboard explaining why this is the future of multiplayer infra:\
<https://youtu.be/UNaG-PLw17s>\
\
And here is a demo using Durable Actors to make a mini-lovable.\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wpF3VTmljqM>\
\
Who Are We?\
\
I was previously at Apple for 7 years as a Staff Engineer working on the platform for Siri and Apple Intelligence. \
\
Olivier was a Tech Lead at SquareSpace and the New York Times building highly scalable data pipelines for marketing teams. 

\
We met in at @McGill University and have stayed close friends since. We won several hackathons together, and even worked on a project that had 15K MAU.\
\
Why are we building this?\
\
In 2021, Swift released actors. It was game changing for my team where threads competing for resources/data races were our #1 source of bugs.\
\
Agents are becoming like threads now. We have many of them doing work at the same time, and they sometimes need to share a CRM record, a code base etc… It’s a very similar problem!\
\
The actor model is a perfect fit for this. It only allows one agent in the actor at a time, preventing race conditions at the core of it.\
\
I came across this problem when looking to have 10 agents do work on a large CSV. I was using Postgres to store a shared state variable, and the snapshotting system was serving stale data to half of the agents causing duplicate work to happen. I quickly realized, there was no existing tool to solve this problem outside of locks in front of Postgres, which is essentially System-R.\
\
I then came across Durable Objects, and found the magic line “Designed to give serverless functions state”. It then hit me this was the correct architecture for this. Cloudflare forces you to go through there workers platform to access this functionality and has insane lock in. I then realized we needed another alternative. That alternative is now Durable Actors.

launches.tagline: Glasses that let you talk to your computer without talking out loud
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re Aarush & Arnav - co-founders of The Subvocal Company

TL;DR: We’re building glasses that let you talk to your computer without talking out loud. You mouth the words silently, and almost invisibly, and Subvocal decodes it to text in real time.

<https://youtu.be/9nW3RA7MOBU>

A more crude version of this won the YC G1 product showcase a few weeks ago!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125559&key=user_uploads/2632951/b9aaa515-80e0-43e6-87f3-c2fdae6b14cf)

**Why we’re building this**

Voice is the fastest, most natural way to use a computer and as agents handle more work, our job moves upstream, to structured and detailed prompting. Expressing your thoughts is best done through unconstrained, open voice. Wispr Flow’s popularity has shown how much people love fast input.

But voice also fails in exactly the moments it needs to work. In an open office or a cafe or in public transit, it’s incredibly awkward for you and distracting for those around you to talk into your computer.

People have found incredibly creative and weird workarounds to this, including gooseneck whisper mics and even sound proof masks you can talk into.

We wanted the speed of speech without having to make a sound.

**How it works**

Subvocal uses RF sensing from a pair of glasses to pick up the tiny facial movements you make while silently articulating words.

We send low-power radio waves through the face and measure how they change as your muscles move. Our models then decode those signals directly into text.

You can articulate clearly, or do it subtly enough that someone sitting across from you barely notices.

**Where we are today**

We started working on this about four months ago after building the first version at a hackathon.

Since then, we’ve gone from a table full of electronics and antennas taped to our face to a semi-portable board and sleek glasses that can decode open-ended speech at 200+ WPM and a reasonably low error rate even at a small dataset scale.

The hardware currently looks a lot worse than the product we intend to ship. Our website shows what the final product looks like, and we’re getting there fast. In the next week, we’ll miniaturize our hardware enough to fit completely on the glasses.

The core thing we wanted to prove first was that the signal exists and that we can decode it. Over the next few months, we intend to collect 000s of hours of population-scale RF data to pretrain a model that works with a very short calibration on anyone.

**What we want this to become**

We think silent speech can become the next interface for interacting with computers, replacing voice and the keyboard.

Instead of choosing between typing and talking out loud, you should be able to just silently articulate what you are thinking, and have it appear on screen.

Emails, prompts, messages, code, notes, commands, all at the speed of speech without bothering anyone around you.

Our goal is to get this into normal-looking glasses you can wear all day.

**We’re opening reservations**

We’re starting with people who already use voice heavily and wish they could use it in places where speaking out loud doesn’t work. Reserving early gets you a founders price and earliest batch shipping.

You can reserve one of our first units for $199 here: <https://subvocal.co/preorder> for shipping in the first limited batch and get a special $200 early bird discount on the final price.

We’re initially opening up a limited number of reservations while we work toward the first production run.

If you use tools like Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, ChatGPT voice, or dictation constantly, we would especially love to hear from you.

**Our asks**

1\. Reserve one if you want this. The most useful signal for us right now is whether people are willing to put real money down for it.

2\. Tell us where you would use it. Office? Meetings? Coding? Walking around? Somewhere else entirely?

3\. Send this to the most voice-addicted person you know. We want to find the people for whom this immediately feels indispensable.

We started building Subvocal four months ago, and we’re moving as fast as we can to get this into your hands.

We’re Maya and Carl, founders of Frontrunner. Previously, we built GTM systems at Console and Encord that supported hundreds of millions of dollars in pipeline. At Console, Maya built and led a 10 person team across GTM engineering, demand gen, content, events, product marketing, and outbound. At Encord, Carl led GTM engineering and built out robust internal systems to bridge the gap between sales and marketing. 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RA1-78Gpkgo>

\
Frontrunner is the agent platform for GTM. **How it works:** 

* We plug into where your data already lives: CRM, email, calendar, product, call recordings
* We turn it into a graph of your business: accounts, people, conversations, signals, and how they connect.
* A fleet of agents run on the graph to continuously research accounts, find and enrich prospects, monitor buying signals, prioritize who to go after, and hand the right action off to your team.

**The result:** instead of rebuilding context in Claude or stitching together point solutions for every workflow, your GTM team has a system that remembers what it learns and gets better as it runs.

**What customers run on Frontrunner:**

* Signal-based outbound: Monitor buying signals → identify and enrich the right people → score and route them to reps
* Account research: Continuously research target accounts and keep CRM context current
* Pipeline revival: Monitor closed-lost and dormant opportunities for reasons to re-engage
* Inbound qualification: Research and score inbound accounts → route them to the right rep
* Attribution: understand which signals, campaigns + touchpoints actually turn into revenue

**Results from customers**

1. 15% higher win rate on new business
2. 40-50% conversion to meeting booked on signal based outbound 
3. 10,000+ contacts in their TAM sourced and enriched
4. 100+ of signal based opportunities actioned daily

_“We are already booking more meetings with you than we did with our first GTM hire”_ 

Unlike Claude or other general purpose AI tools, Frontrunner is an opinionated harness for GTM. Your nth project in Claude will not incorporate the meeting outcomes, closed won business to scale and improve revenue for you based on bespoke playbooks for your company. But it will gladly take up your team members afternoons vibe coding on siloed ideas and projects.

**🏇**

We’re building Frontrunner so GTM teams can spend less time stitching together tools and rebuilding context, and more time figuring out what _actually_ moves the business. If your team wants to or is already experimenting with agents across sales or marketing, we would love to chat!

Hi everyone. I'm [Nick Soman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicksoman/), cofounder of [Decent](https://www.decent.com/) (F26) with [Andrew Budker](https://www.linkedin.com/in/abudker/).\

<https://youtu.be/ICNV6Scchqw>

\
**The problem**\
You choose your company health plan once a year at renewal, and then nobody touches it for twelve months. All year long you overpay without seeing it. A one-time surgery gets built into next year's rates as if it’s recurring. You get billed for employees who left months ago. Your team uses the ER for things that primary care could have handled for a fraction of the cost.\
\
I learned this the hard way. A carrier raised my old company's rates 27% in January because an employee had started an expensive treatment the February before. They told me it was my data and my fault for not looking. Almost all of that cost was waste. She could have been treated at home for 30% less. An equally effective treatment that cost 25% less could have been free to her. Optimized dosing could have saved 20% more, with fewer side effects and no negative impact on her health.\
\
**How Decent is different**\
Your health plan should get better all year, not once a year. You don't buy a year of ads or a rack of servers up front anymore, but health insurance is stuck on a single annual renewal. Decent is an AI-native health insurance broker for US companies with 2 to 200 employees. We compare every way to cover your team, show what each one costs, and then keep improving your plan all year, for your company and for your employees. The insurance company you choose pays us, so we’re free to you.\
\
**Why trust us**\
Andrew and I met 16 years ago building the Kindle at Amazon. He spent the last several years leading engineering for Metamate, Meta's internal AI platform. I've started and sold two companies and raised $42M. Before this I built and ran level-funded plans, PEOs, and association health plans, with a Net Promoter Score of 79 vs. the industry average of 14, so I know what good looks like and where the system breaks. \
\
The full story of why I came back to this, and why it's called Decent, is here: <https://www.decent.com/blog/run-it-back>\
\
**Traction**\
AI is doing 89% of our brokerage work and climbing, and we just caught a one-time surgery driving 46% of a client's claims spend and kept it out of next year's rates. 67 companies are working with us so far, and many more are close behind.\
\
**What you can do now**

* If you or someone you know runs or helps run a US company with roughly 2 to 200 people renewing by January 1, 2027, book 15 minutes with me to find the best plan for you: <https://meetings-na2.hubspot.com/nick-soman/15-yc>

Our mission: affordable healthcare for all. It's never too late to save the world.\

Nick & Andrew

name: GrayPass
long_description:
Login tells you who signed in. GrayPass helps apps check who’s behind sensitive actions and whether they’re authorized before those actions go through.

It combines identity, device and session context with behavioral signals like typing rhythm, cursor movement and scrolling. Before a sensitive action goes through, GrayPass evaluates that evidence against your team’s policy and returns a decision: allow, challenge, hold or deny. Your app enforces the decision.

This applies to actions like exporting sensitive data, changing admin permissions or allowing an AI agent to act on someone’s behalf. Allowed actions receive short-lived, signed proof tied to the exact action and your app.

Your existing login and authentication stack stays in place.

launches.tagline: We help your company stop unauthorized people, bots, and AI agents before they move money, export data, or change permissions.
launches.body:
Your app knows who logged in. But does it know who's **actually** in control when someone moves money or exports customer data?

That's the problem GrayPass (YC F26) is solving.

GrayPass has already processed over **900,000 sessions** across its customers' apps and generated **$50K in revenue** so far this month.

Before sensitive actions like moving money, exporting customer data, or changing admin permissions, GrayPass helps apps verify who's in control and whether they're authorized to take that action.

GrayPass works _alongside_ existing login systems, combining signals like typing rhythm, cursor movement, and scrolling with device and session information. Based on the rules each company sets, it tells the app whether to allow the action, request additional verification, put it on hold, or deny it. The app enforces that decision.

As the internet becomes increasingly agentic, apps need to know when an agent is acting and whether it has permission to do so. GrayPass helps them do both.

Because knowing who logged in isn't the same as knowing who's taking action.\
\

launches.title: Cyclon : the AI phone to replace your iPhone

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re Adam and Thomas, the founders of Cyclon.

**We’re building an AI phone to replace your iPhone.** Tell it what you want, and it uses your apps for you, or builds the ones you need.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=no4BYVy3RmY>

**Why we're building this**

We spend hours on our phones doing things we could explain in one sentence.

“Find the latest contract, send it to Thomas, then call him.”

Today, that means opening Drive, finding the document, checking permissions, copying a link, switching to WhatsApp, and making the call yourself.

AI is becoming capable of doing this work. We’re building a phone that gives it the access and context to follow the task through.

**How it works**

Cyclon puts AI in the operating system, so it can work across the phone’s apps and notifications.

**It uses the same apps you do.** In the demo, I receive a notification asking me to send yesterday’s pictures. My phone has already done the work in the background: identifying Alex in my photos and gathering the right pictures. All I have to do is approve.

**It builds real apps.** Describe what you need—for example, an app to practice Spanish. Cyclon writes the code in a sandbox, tests it, and fixes issues before installing it on the phone. These are real apps you can open and use, and they can connect to APIs.

**It handles notifications.** Cyclon summarizes what matters and explains what it filters out. Tell it “Hide NordVPN notifications,” and it remembers that as a rule. When something needs a response, you can ask it to act directly.

Tasks can keep running in the background while you do something else.

**What we want this to become**

We believe a phone should adapt to its user: remember preferences, handle recurring tasks, and build software for needs that existing apps don't cover.

Just as the iPhone brought the internet and social networks into people's pockets, we want to bring the full power of AI to everyone. Instead of opening apps, people will just have to ask.

name: Ageospatial
long_description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.

name: Superserve
long_description:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.
one_liner: Virtual machines for long-running agents
