Before that, he was Founding Engineer and Director of Engineering at Long-Term Stock Exchange (YC S17), building capital markets software used by 50,000 startups.

launches.title: Superserve: Virtual machines for long-running agents
launches.tagline: Cloud VMs for running complex environments across many agent sessions
launches.body:
Hi YC! I am Pavitra, founder of Superserve.\
\
We give every agent session its own computer in the cloud, with the whole application environment it needs to build, run, and test software.

**We already run over 100K machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.**\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h8uXUiT-aFU>

### **The problem**

Say your agent is fixing a bug in a web app. It needs the code, dependencies, database, and browser to check its work. If you come back tomorrow with feedback, that work should still be there.

Giving every session that environment means managing startup delays, preserving state, controlling access, and paying for machines while they wait. Across many sessions, that becomes substantial infrastructure work.

### **Our solution**

**Superserve handles that infrastructure for you.** Every session gets an isolated VM with your application already set up. It starts quickly, keeps the agent’s files, memory, and processes between turns, and can pause with no compute charges.

### **How we compare**

* **Fastest cold-start** and **snapshot start** on[ AI Sandbox Bench](https://aisandboxbench.com/): **0.52s** and **0.55s** median, respectively.
* **#1 sandbox provider and #2 overall** on[ DevTool Arena](https://devtoolarena.com/codex/api?utm_source=chatgpt.com), which measures how well Codex discovers and uses developer tools.
* Beats **E2B, Daytona, Modal, Vercel, Cloudflare, and Google Cloud Run** on time to first successful command in[ ComputeSDK’s 100-machine burst benchmark](https://www.computesdk.com/benchmarks/sandboxes/burst-tti?utm_source=chatgpt.com), with a **0.37s** median.
* One of our customers benchmarked their workload as **77% cheaper on Superserve than their previously custom built EC2-based sandbox.**

### **How Superserve works**

**Run your whole application.** Put your repo, dependencies, Docker services, databases, and browser into a template. Every session starts with the environment the agent needs to build, run, and test software, faster than any other VM.

**Keep the work between turns.** Pause a machine with its files, memory, and processes intact, then resume that state when the agent has more work. Machines can stay paused indefinitely. Compute charges stop while paused; stored state is billed only for what you use, not what’s allocated on the disk.\
\
**Fork a machine to explore in parallel.** Create independent copies of a paused machine, including its files, memory, and processes. Agents can try different fixes or run evals and RL rollouts from the same starting point, without rebuilding the environment. Each copy keeps its work separate.

**Control what the agent can access.** Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You control the VMs network ingress and egress, which services the agent exposes, and we enforce the rules outside the VM (and the agent’s boundary). Managed API credentials are brokered on outgoing requests and kept outside the agent’s environment.

### **Our background**

I was a founding staff SWE at Dosu, building code-reasoning agents used by 200K engineers, including teams at HashiCorp, Datadog, and LlamaIndex. Giving every agent session a secure environment with the codebase, bash, and tools it needed took substantial infrastructure work. I started Superserve to make that part easy.

Before Dosu, I was a founding engineer and Director of Engineering at Long-Term Stock Exchange (YC S17), building capital markets software used by 50,000+ startups.

I’m building Superserve with Alejandro and Amit. Alejandro led the Kubernetes platform at Oracle. Amit built the copy-on-write storage engine in our Firecracker fork, so machines can share a template while keeping each agent’s work separate.

### **Our ask**

**If you’re building coding agents, AI teammates, or eval and RL environments, talk to us.**

[**Book a 25-minute call**](https://calendly.com/superserve-ai/25-min) or email [**founders@superserve.ai**](mailto:founders@superserve.ai). We’ll review your current setup, benchmark your workload, and work on the Superserve integration with you.

Prefer to get started yourself? [docs.superserve.ai](https://docs.superserve.ai)

launches.title: Canos: Cancer detection for dogs with a tube (not a drop) of blood
launches.tagline: Liquid biopsy that finds cancer earlier and tracks it through treatment
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126939&key=user_uploads/3670537/9bad1ffd-c8bf-44f7-a78b-e4f1253781f5)

**TL;DR:** Canos detects and tracks cancer in dogs from a single blood draw by reading the whole cell-free DNA genome. In a benchmark of 896 samples from 341 dogs, our model reached 91% sensitivity and 95% specificity, and it gets better with every new sample. At New York Vet last week, 160+ veterinary professionals from 130 clinics/hospitals came to our booth to learn more in just two days, and we’re now onboarding 10 founding clinics/mobile vets in New York City and the Bay Area.

<https://youtu.be/SA6jE_RFaFA>

**The problem**\
1 in 4 dogs will develop cancer in their lifetime, and most cases are caught late, because dogs can’t tell us when something feels wrong. Routine bloodwork rarely gives an answer, and advanced imaging like CT is costly and requires sedation. Vets need tools that not only detect cancer, but also show where it is and what type it is, so they know exactly what to do next.

**The solution**\
We’re bringing the standard of human liquid biopsy to veterinary medicine. Instead of measuring a single biomarker or a fixed panel of mutations, we read the whole-genome cfDNA signal and analyze 500+ multimodal features, including methylation, one of the most robust signals for cancer detection and the key to telling where a cancer comes from. Vets draw blood at a routine visit, and the same test tracks how a dog responds to treatment over time.

**The bigger picture**\
Every test builds something rare: records of the same dogs from health, to cancer, to treatment. Dogs age roughly 7 times faster than humans and develop cancer naturally in our homes, so what takes decades to observe in people unfolds in a few years. This data can unlock breakthroughs in cancer and ageing research for dogs and humans alike, and opens the door to more personalised treatments, such as vaccines.

**The team**\
I’m an Oxford zoologist (PhD), and Bin is an Oxford machine learning scientist (PhD). We’re lifelong animal lovers who have built in pet cancer before: at our previous company, ZYTCA, we built an AI pathology platform for pet cancer in 6 months, and ZYTCA went on to raise $3.3M and launch across Europe, Asia and Latin America. We took Canos from idea to working prototype in 3 months, validating the workflow on our own blood, and have already shared our first scientific [paper](https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11113122/v1).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126939&key=user_uploads/3670537/66d0ef6f-4f4a-433c-a9e1-1fd813ec0b22)

name: Hundred
long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.
one_liner: 100% automated inspection for precision hardware parts

launches.title: Hundred: Automated inspection for precision hardware parts
launches.tagline: Catch sub-100μm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re[ Erica](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erica-diaz1/),[ Iris](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iris-liao-03b041152/), and[ Imani](https://www.linkedin.com/in/imani-gosserand/), co-founders of[ Hundred](https://hundred.systems/) 

Hundred replaces the typical human visual inspection done on precision hardware parts with an automated system that can scan a whole shipping tray of parts at once.

<https://youtu.be/xC9_YnK2PJc>

**The Problem**

Small part designs change too fast for traditional machine vision to keep up, so factories still inspect parts by hand: literally people with microscopes sorting out bad parts. As manufacturers move away from China to the US or India, operators familiar with common defects don’t move with them. While trained operators miss \~15% of defects, untrained operators miss even more. 

One bad part can turn a finished product into scrap material and more than 3 bad parts in an hour can stop the assembly line. Defects cost U.S. manufacturers $45B a year, and line downtime costs another $245B.

**What we’re building**

Hundred eliminates human subjectivity by imaging parts at mass production volumes, right in their shipping trays. A full tray can be placed in the Hundred rig, which detects defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials and finishes. Where human inspectors might require a month of training, Hundred can stop defects on Day 1.

**Our goal is to make sure engineers can set their specs once and know that part quality will hold up when they leave the factory.**

**The Team**

**Erica** designed and ramped consumer hardware at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap for 5 years where she root-caused device failures to bad parts and drove vendors to fix them.

**Iris** was a Quantitative Researcher at Citadel. She then spent a year at Imperial College London researching ML on 3D meshes and other structured data.

**Imani** worked for 5 years at Twitch as a software engineer at the intersection of notifications, short-form content, and ML for hundreds of millions of streamers and viewers.

**Our Ask**

We’d love to connect with precision hardware companies and contract manufacturers who are struggling with part inspection or looking to scale their inspection capacity.

**Learn more at [hundred.systems](http://hundred.systems)**

launches.body:
Hi, I’m [Melanie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/-melaniechen-/?isSelfProfile=true) and I’m the founder of[ Kiwi](https://withkiwi.ai/). 

<https://withkiwi.ai/> | [linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kiwi-ai-inc/) | [x/twitter](https://x.com/with_kiwi_ai)

### Tl;dr

Kiwi makes GTM agents self-improving and accurate, without having to hire data engineers. Every agent run can cite the SQL query it ran over the GTM data lake as evidence, and every decision or approval in the agent workflow powers evals that improve the agent. 

If you or another GTM team that you know is struggling to use agents in their day-to-day workflows and keeps falling back to repetitive, manual tasks, [trykiwi.now](http://trykiwi.now). 

<https://youtu.be/xozh9X5Hkd8>

### The problem

6 months ago, I was leading the post-sales team at a startup, and I hit a breaking point. I had spent 20 hours that week reviewing and fixing the work that my GTM teams’ agents had done. Despite spending hours each week on enablement, I always felt behind. Every week, the industry was moving forward with some new technique to best use agents efficiently and effectively, but onboarding the entire GTM organization onto a new workflow each week was impossible. On top of that, even when everyone had migrated to the new workflow, their agents were still generating slop because the underlying data wasn’t correct, and there was no way to ask the agents to show their work on each run. I started talking to other GTM teams, and now after learning from over 100 different companies, I’ve learned that there are two main obstacles keeping most GTM teams from becoming successfully agentic: 

1. Continuous enablement: Teams can easily adopt one skill, but as soon as operators fork the skills or context, it gets impossible to audit who’s using what agents where and for what and how successfully, or to push new changes to everyone’s agents. 
2. The data: when the underlying data infrastructure doesn’t exist, there is no way that agents can know how and where to fetch the data they need for a workflow.

### Kiwi handles the continuous enablement and maintenance of agents, as well as the data engineering, for you.

At Kiwi, we believe that an agent is only as good as the data that you give it. So, we sync all of the data from the tools in your GTM tool stack into a data lake. When you build an agent on Kiwi, we break it down into agent steps and human checkpoints, and every agent step that requires external data will show the SQL query that the agent runs under the hood, as well as a snapshot of the data pulled. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124027&key=user_uploads/1678005/27c31990-4696-41f4-b615-1ce6f5042a82)

Every checkpoint approval, feedback, or decline is also stored in the data lake, in addition to agent run parameters, so that Kiwi can detect shifts in your agent usage and suggest improvements. In addition, you can test agent changes against the data from historical runs. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124027&key=user_uploads/1678005/dea0699c-9987-4995-aa2d-7ec7da0f0d06)

With Kiwi, your GTM team can become fully AI-native without having to hire even more cooks in the kitchen or build out more surface area for your team to maintain. 

### Why us

The Kiwi team has spent years building data infrastructure that has powered billions of ACH and debit transactions at companies like Plaid, Jane Street, and Chalk, and experienced the pains of enablement firsthand. We’re building the platform that we wish we had, and could not find on the market. 

### Our Ask

If you or someone you know is struggling with how to make their GTM teams AI-native, we’d love an introduction! Reach out at [trykiwi.now](http://trykiwi.now), or email me at [melanie@withkiwi.ai](mailto:melanie@withkiwi.ai) !

launches.tagline: Find, verify, prioritize and fix the most complex vulnerabilities automatically
launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wypshdV_04o&vq=4k>

**What is OpenHack?**

OpenHack is an always-on AI security engineer. It learns your codebase, infrastructure and business logic like a real security engineer; scans your code for the hardest logic based vulnerabilities, and alerts you about vulnerabilities it has verified as real and exploitable.

OpenHack is trusted by Pocket, HydraDB, Docura Health, OpenSEO, Hue, Melty and more.

Book a demo: <https://openhack.com/demo>

**Launch offer:** Free **Claude Mythos** Scanning until November 11, 2026!

**Catastrophic vulnerabilities that OpenHack found for our customers:**

* **Full account takeover.** Retrieved all sensitive user data and logged in as any user on the platform.
* **GitHub org takeover.** Chained multiple vulnerabilities to get admin access to a company's GitHub organization, including the ability to delete it.
* **Payment and billing bypass.** Exploited business logic flaws to use paid features forever, for free.
* **Cloud storage exposure.** Found unauthorized access to S3 buckets at Papermark, a platform used by Fortune 500 companies. Their team fixed it quickly and the advisory is public:[ https://openhack.com/advisories/OH-2026-001](https://openhack.com/advisories/OH-2026-001)

None of these were caught by code review or traditional scanners.

**How OpenHack works under the hood**

OpenHack built a custom harness refined over months. It’s easy to make a harness that satisfies the basics, but building one that can do recon, hunting, validation, verification, triaging, fixing properly is extremely hard. We constantly refined our harness and outperformed Github CodeQL, Semgrep and Snyk on the OWASP benchmark.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125918&key=user_uploads/318539/393c6475-8ad4-4ae8-84ef-47fe77006a14)

We’re also actively working on PentestBench, a more relevant benchmark for pentesting that works on extremely complicated logic bugs requiring a full exploitation chain.

**Why we built this**

Hey! I’m Ananay Arora. I've been finding security vulnerabilities for over 12 years, with bounties from Meta, Apple, Perplexity, DHS, Y Combinator and more.

Every time, the bug was simple once you understood what the system was _supposed_ to do. Scanners don't understand that. They pattern-match, flood you with false positives, and miss the logic bugs that actually get you breached. And now attackers are using AI too.

So we built OpenHack to hunt for bugs the way a real security engineer would, with full context about your business.

**What OpenHack offers**

* **AI code scanning** that understands your business logic, system design and what your developers meant to build
* **AI pentesting** of your live app, chaining findings together the way a real attacker would
* **OpenHack Blueprint**: A tool to map out your entire infrastructure + codebase deployment, like you would on a whiteboard
* **OpenHack Assistant:** Ask and take action on anything and everything regarding your security posture
* **Supply chain and secrets scanning** across your dependencies
* **Automatic verification**, so you only see real, prioritized vulnerabilities, not a pile of false positives
* **Linear and Slack integrations**, so findings land where your team already works
* **Agent MCP Integration**: all of OpenHack can be accessed with any of your favorite agents and be used to fix vulnerabilities lightning fast  
* **Compliance reports and a Vanta integration**, so you can get through enterprise security reviews faster (we personally help with these too!)
* **AI and/or human pentests**, with founder-led support over Slack, phone and email ([**Sample Pentest Report**](https://openhack.com/sample-pentest-report.pdf)**)**

**Want OpenHack on your codebase?**

* Book a demo: <https://openhack.com/demo>
* Email me directly: [ananay@openhack.com](mailto:ananay@openhack.com)
* Signup on <https://openhack.com>

We are [Vivek](https://www.linkedin.com/in/viveksoneja/) and [Rajesh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rajeshkumar05/), co-founders of Aucert.

Testing mobile apps has always been slow, manual and error prone. Aucert solves this by deploying a team of expert AI agents that operate autonomously to ensure your app meets your expectations.

**TL;DR:** Aucert is an autonomous mobile app verification platform with a team of expert AI agents. Pick a build, start a scan, and the agents test it like a real user, then report what broke with the evidence: functional bugs, accessibility issues, design issues, and Google Play and App Store policy violations etc. What takes top apps weeks and multiple teams, Aucert does in hours.

<https://youtu.be/pd_mqx7HXNo>

**Why is mobile validation so hard?**

On the web, you roll back a bad release in minutes. On mobile, the bug sits on people's phones until they update, while the fix waits on a hotfix and another round of store review. Meanwhile, coding agents write code faster than any team can check it.

**How does Aucert work?**

Aucert’s mobile verification platform uses purpose built AI agents that evaluate your app from multiple lenses. Pax knows Google Play and App Store policy. Iris checks accessibility.  Genie uses the app like a real user, screen by screen. There are no test scripts to write: the agents learn the app on their own and hold every build to your team's standards.

Every finding comes with evidence, and your team decides what ships. What takes top apps weeks and multiple teams, Aucert does in hours.

Vivek Soneja and Rajesh Kumar have lived this problem from the inside. Vivek was the founding mobile architect at PhonePe (500M+ users) and worked on WhatsApp at Meta. Rajesh spent 11 years at PayPal and patented automated payments testing.

It's actually hard to do it well, and the market opportunity is very deep (and fun). $800Bn is spent on digital advertising every year, an extra $400Bn goes to people who manage this spend - with incumbents like WPP at $18 billion in revenue. That's who we’re going after.

### **Who we are**

We’re best friends and repeat founders, including one company in marketing automation that we built and sold earlier this year. 

[Robin](https://robinchoy.com/) started his first company in 2016 (HireSweet, AI for recruiting - $4M annual revenue), did YC for the first time in the Winter 2020. Then left HireSweet in 2024, started an angel fund that invested in 130+ amazing companies total, including Starcloud, Mastra, Conductor, Blaxel, Casco, Sygaldry, and so many more + launched Botdog with Gui.

[Gui](https://www.guillaumemiara.com/) has been a software engineer in tech for 13 years (Globality, Staff at Oscar Health, Defacto) and holds master's degrees from CentraleSupélec and Berkeley. He most recently built Botdog together with Rob. You might find him on a surf board at Ocean Beach when the conditions are right.

launches.title: RATLOG: Reusable heavy-lift rockets powered by an engine with 90% fewer parts
launches.tagline: First engine hot-fired in 4 months for under $30K. $400M in launch reservations signed.
launches.body:
𝗧𝗟;𝗗𝗥: Launch capacity is becoming a bottleneck, so we at RATLOG are 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲𝗫 with reusable heavy-lift rockets powered by an engine designed to use 𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀 than conventional designs. We built and successfully hot-fired our first engine in 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 and have signed reservation agreements worth $𝟰𝟬𝟬𝗠. Now we are printing an engine with 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝘅 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 for a hot fire in November. If you’re a satellite operator, [reach out to us asap](https://calendar.app.google/xPzyR7iHmEJ3Gt116)**.**

<https://youtu.be/i-RuldD2YHU>	

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺

Satellite operators need to put more mass into orbit than ever, but an available launch slot can be 𝟯–𝟰 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 and cost up to $𝟭𝟱,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺. Every delay pushes back the start of operations and revenue.

As satellite constellations grow and new projects like space stations and orbital data centers take shape, customers need more launch capacity and more options.

As one European launch broker put it: “𝗜𝘁’𝘀 𝗴𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝗳 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝘀𝗹𝗼𝘁.”

𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

We’re building 𝗿𝗲𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝘃𝘆-𝗹𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗿𝘆 𝗽𝗮𝘆𝗹𝗼𝗮𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘂𝗽 𝘁𝗼 𝟮𝟬 𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝘀, powered by an engine architecture that aims to use 𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀 than conventional designs.

We’ve 𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗯𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗺𝗽 by using a different method to pressurize the propellants and developed a **new rocket engine cycle** around it.

This simpler architecture reduces manufacturing complexity and cost, while reusability spreads the cost of the hardware across multiple flights.

Think of it as a 𝗯𝘂𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲: customers book capacity on a shared flight and pay by the kilogram.

**Team**

Charlie and Paul met through mutual interest in rotating detonation engines for cruise missiles and started a club, then met Felix and Matty.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122077&key=user_uploads/3173499/08b61f2e-5027-4a5d-912e-96e7381e9cd3)

From left to right

* 𝗙𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘅 𝗞𝗲𝗹𝗺, Chief Avionics Officer: Developed PCB designs since the age of 16.
* 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲 𝗪𝗲𝗶𝘀𝗲, Chief Executive Officer: Previously worked on ESA's Argonaut Moon Lander and space telescope.
* 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝘆 𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀𝗻𝗮𝗰𝗸, Chief Operating Officer: Founding team at Lio (YC S23, a16z), working closely with CEO and COO.
* 𝗣𝗮𝘂𝗹 𝗞𝘂𝗻𝗵𝗮𝗿𝘁, Chief Technology Officer: Designed rocket engine nozzles for ESA's Argonaut lunar lander.

**Traction**

* Signed reservation agreements worth $𝟰𝟬𝟬𝗠.
* Built and successfully hot-fired our first rocket engine in 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀.
* Spoken with 𝟳𝟬+ 𝗽𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗵 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀.

**Ask**

* If you’re building satellites, space stations, or orbital data centers, we’d love to discuss your launch plans. Book a meeting [here](https://calendar.app.google/xPzyR7iHmEJ3Gt116) or reach us at [charlie.weise@ratlog.space](mailto:charlie.weise@ratlog.space).

launches.title: Maritime: Fully managed cloud for running AI agents at scale
launches.tagline: Run millions of agents, each on its own isolated, persistent VM.
launches.body:
Hi everyone, we’re Maria and Ary, founders of [Maritime](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/38061) (YC F26).

**TL;DR:** Maritime is a fully managed cloud platform for running millions of AI agents, each on its own isolated, persistent VM.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TnGXH9H0cTw>

**Why we built Maritime** 

We believe we’re heading toward a world with billions of AI agents. Everyone will have agents working for them, and businesses will run entire teams of AI employees. A new generation of startups will build and sell these agents, giving every customer one of their own.

We started working on Maritime when OpenClaw was released. Now, with dots, Instinct, Grok Bot, and Muse, that future is taking shape. We saw the infrastructure challenge firsthand while hosting hundreds of agents during our research at MIT. Even at that scale, our time went into getting environments running, maintaining them, and debugging individual agents.

Running billions of agents will require infrastructure that lets developers give each one a persistent computer and manage entire fleets with ease. We’re building Maritime to make that possible, so any startup can launch an agent product, give every customer their own agent, and scale it to millions in no time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=120824&key=user_uploads/3118952/6772cfd5-737c-4278-8a02-ec3793cb070b)

**What Maritime does**

Maritime gives every agent a persistent computer and manages the infrastructure around it:

* **An isolated VM for each agent.** Run code, install software, and use a browser.
* **Pricing built for scale.** Hosting starts at $1 per agent per month, making it practical to give every customer their own persistent computer and grow your fleet as your product grows.
* **Persistence between tasks.** Keep files, memory, installed software, and logins so agents can pick up where they left off.
* **Tools to manage individual agents.** Inspect, debug, and fix each customer’s agent directly.
* **Different environments for different workflows.** Choose Linux computers, Windows desktops, or virtual Android phones based on the software and apps your agents need.

You can run your agent code inside a Maritime VM, or keep your agent on your existing backend and use MCP to let it control a Maritime computer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=120824&key=user_uploads/3118952/db071ab8-94f8-4245-9de8-f574cc2aba1d)

**Who it’s for**

Teams building and selling AI employees, personal assistants, and other products where every customer has an agent of their own.

We want founders to focus on building and growing their products, with Maritime managing the infrastructure to run them.

**Our ask**

* **Try Maritime:** Host three agents for free at [maritime.sh](http://maritime.sh). Hosting starts at $1 per agent per month.
* **Introduce us:** If you know teams building and selling agents, especially those deploying a separate agent or computer for every customer, please comment or connect us.

<https://youtu.be/ScivsFG1qxw>

Mobilizing energy is a national priority, with electronic warfare and field computing requiring increasing power. Designed, manufactured, and put into low-volume production in 1/4 of the time of most incumbent battery manufacturers— SPM is filling the gap that both startups and major primes are experiencing. America needs more reliable battery pack suppliers that produce high quality, safe and reliable packs, with non-FEOC components. That’s how we’ve always done it.

We started directly selling our battery pack and power system capability to customers in August 2026 and went from pre-orders, to over $400,000 in contracted revenue in one month, with a large qualified pipeline for the remainder of the year. We are slated to become a prime contractor in 2027, but we have a much more rapid strategy right now - sell to prime contractors who needs packs - and this strategy works. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125487&key=user_uploads/1979736/ebec0c80-adc8-4781-b52f-0941a64aaefe)

Our team is scaling automated production capacity in Pittsburgh Pennsylvania - we’re booked into February 2027. Because our entire battery packs are vertically integrated except the cell, we can develop cell-agnostic custom battery packs with a patented design methodology that doesn’t require specialized manufacturing equipment. After design and low-volume production starts, any shop with a spot welder can acquire parts and finish the assembly. In the end, this strengthens domestic battery pack supply chain integrity with rapidly scalable battery packs that use a common module form factor. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125487&key=user_uploads/1979736/848da5cf-c7c4-4dec-9ac3-1715b295b704)

Super Powers Mobility started out developing 470V 10-20 kWh high-voltage powertrain systems for light off-road vehicles and late this summer we shifted to power systems for energy mobilization and military mobility products like UGVs, UAS, and USVs. Since switching focus, SPM has joined 4 federal contracts to supply batteries and power electronics systems.

You can also check our YC Jobs page.

I founded SPM after a 4-year career as a Sr. Mechanical Integration engineer at Tesla on the Cybertruck, 2 years at Honda R&D Americas as a powersports vehicle engineer, and 4 years as a professionally sponsored off-road racer. launches.title: DeepMark - Reinventing Trust in Voice
launches.tagline: A live watermark inside AI voice that survives phone calls
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/76SqazbxK4w>

Hey, we are Slavko and Kosta 👋

We have been working together for six years, first as two researchers at the University of Montenegro, now as founders. Somewhere along the way, we became best friends. Kosta is our CSO, and I am the CEO.

**The problem**

Voice is uniquely vulnerable to impersonation. A few seconds of audio is enough to clone anyone, and the same voice agents that answer a bank's phone can be turned around and pointed at the bank's customers. People have started to hesitate before picking up. Good technology scales good outcomes, and it scales bad ones just as well. Our job is simple. Restore trust in voice.

**What we built**

DeepMark is real-time audio watermarking for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we put a certificate inside the sound itself, on the voice company's side, as the voice is being generated. Not metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The certificate becomes part of the voice.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/b3239118-82c1-4fb4-82c2-f4363685a0be)

Then the voice goes out into the real world, and the real world is rough on audio. Compression, codecs, a bad connection, a cheap speaker, a worse microphone. Think about how flat a human voice sounds over the phone. Our certificate survives the trip. On the other end, a phone, a call center, or an API reads it and shows who is speaking, who issued the certificate, and whether this agent is allowed to be on the line. Detectors ask whether audio is fake. We answer who is authorized to speak.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/171abdf5-efb9-442b-a153-dbbb1ba981d4)

**Why this is hard**

Four things have to hold at the same time. It has to be real time, or a phone call makes no sense, and voice companies already fight for every millisecond. It has to leave the audio quality alone, nobody trades a worse voice for a safer one. It has to survive the phone line. And the ID has to be long enough, because the longer the ID, the more certificates we can issue. A watermark that works beautifully in the lab falls apart the moment audio meets a phone line. And a live call has no file to sign. Nothing survives the trip except the sound itself, so the identity has to live inside the sound. We spent years hitting that wall. Then we built a tool that measures all four at once and published it, so anyone can check our work, and everyone else's.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/a9930538-1deb-4609-8938-4bdbcf8c88ce)

**How we got here**

Our mentor, who did his PhD in digital watermarking, told us not to bother. The field was saturated, nothing left to contribute. We were too stubborn to listen, and our learning-based approach turned out to be one of the first of its kind.

Kosta wrote his PhD on watermarking along the way. I am still writing mine! We published some of the earliest work in deep audio watermarking, cited by teams at Meta, Microsoft, Sony, and Adobe. This year our robustness benchmark landed in IEEE Access, and our AWARE paper was accepted at EUSIPCO. Before YC, we signed our first platform license with a leading voice AI provider, and it is now in production.

**Our ask**

We want to meet voice AI companies. If you build voice models, book 20 minutes with us and we will run DeepMark on your own audio, so you can see the mark survive your calls. The EU AI Act's marking rules already apply and the 2 December deadline for systems on the market is close, so this is a good month to talk. If you know someone at a voice AI platform, an intro means a lot to us.

[slavko@deepmark.me](mailto:slavko@deepmark.me), or book a demo at [deepmark.me](http://deepmark.me). Thanks for reading. 🇲🇪 → 🌉

name: Wondersearch
long_description:
Our mission is to give every AI agent the right context, from any amount of data.

WonderSearch is search built for AI agents. We let developers make all of their data searchable by meaning, without embeddings, servers or ingestion, so agents can pull the right context and cite where it came from. Unlike vector databases and RAG stacks, there's no pipeline to build or maintain: connect your files and data, and they're searchable right away. It runs on our own search model, and you pay only per query, whatever the size of your data.

Teams use WonderSearch across their own documents and knowledge, and build it into their products, help centres and AI features, connecting through MCP, our API, the CLI or the Python SDK.

(Evokoa, Inc. is the company behind WonderSearch.)
one_liner: Instant semantic search over your data without embeddings.

launches.title: Cesara: AI agents that make sure every healthcare transaction is paid per contract
launches.tagline: Every healthcare transaction checked against the contract, with underpayments recovered automatically
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Every healthcare transaction should be paid according to the contract. Today, billions aren't. Cesara reads a health system's payer contracts and checks every claim against them when it's submitted. When a payment comes back short, Cesara automatically files the appeal with the contract clause attached and recovers the money. \
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IDbQo3WsSGY>

### The problem: contracts change, but team capacity doesn't

Payer contracts keep changing. Amendments, fee schedule updates and annual rate increases all change what a hospital should be paid partway through the year. Every change has to be loaded and checked by hand. Revenue cycle and managed care teams can't keep up, so underpayments only show up months later in spreadsheets, after the payment has posted. **Health systems lose $40B+ a year from contractual underpayments.**

### How Cesara works

* **Every contract in one place.** Cesara pulls rates, carve-outs, stop-loss terms and rate increases from the contracts themselves. It keeps them in sync with Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email and your chargemaster.
* **Every claim checked when it's submitted.** Cesara calculates the expected payment up front. Say a payer pays $42,000 on a claim where the contract's stop-loss clause means $78,000 is owed. Your team sees the gap right away, with the clause attached.
* **Automatic recovery.** Cesara files each appeal with the contract excerpt and the payer's remittance (835) attached. It tracks the appeal until the money is recovered and the claim is closed.
* **Better contract negotiations.** Your team can ask its contracts anything in plain language and model proposed rates before signing. They walk into payer meetings with payment trends and evidence ready.

### Enterprise grade from day one

Cesara is built for health systems, not retrofitted for them. It connects to Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email, Waystar and Availity, and it posts work to Teams and Slack.

* **Rolled out in phases.** Cesara first runs alongside your current process to prove its accuracy on your own claims. Next it recommends actions for your team to approve. Then it recovers underpayments automatically within limits you set.
* **Every action traceable.** Each underpayment, appeal and recovery links to the contract clause behind it, and every action is logged.
* **Your team reviews exceptions, not every claim.** Anything above your approval threshold goes to your team before Cesara acts on it.

Want a free audit of your claims? [**team@cesara.com**](mailto:team@cesara.com)

launches.title: Aikido Technologies: GW-scale datacenters at sea
launches.tagline: Aikido deploys clean marine datacenters in weeks, not years
launches.body:
Hi Y’all,

We’re Sam, Bingbin and James and [we’re building AI datacenters out on the ocean](https://youtu.be/k0kcc934lW4?si=068bCBwyDkkNGkM4), powered by the wind and cooled by the sea. Our first unit, A1DC, will hit the water by December and we already have customers lined up to rent the GPUs.

**TLDR:** 

* We’re building datacenters out in the ocean because there is free energy (wind) and free cooling (cold seawater), and no required permits (once you are far enough away from shore);
* Building datacenters out in the ocean is tricky because things break;
* We’ve built [energy infra in the ocean](https://youtu.be/DhHRR_apxmQ?si=UoLwnEfRPLz-nmr5) designed for 25+ years and have developed [our own offshore platform](https://youtu.be/fr8Bh8sTIxM?si=_6eN8AGIvccI2F2I) that is well suited for the integration of AI infrastructure and can be deployed quickly and at scale.

 

**Ask**: 

Can you introduce us to neoclouds, AI labs, inference providers or other compute aggregators who would be interested buying compute on our first 10MW unit? Point them to: [aikidotechnologies.com/reserve](http://aikidotechnologies.com/reserve) 

**Problem:** 

* There are 5+ year wait times for grid connections.
* Conventional energy supply chains are maxed out. Prices for gas turbines have tripled.
* 70% of Americans oppose datacenters in their community. Many states have enacted moratoriums and pauses on datacenter construction and energization, from Texas to New York. 
* New datacenter builds are focused on minimizing friction, not maximizing efficiency nor clean energy. Building GW-scale gas-fired compute close to our cities results can result in a 1deg C localized increase in temps.

**Solution:**

Moving the units out into the ocean solves multiple challenges simultaneously:

* **No Permitting**: Our units don’t impose on the grid nor can be seen by landlubbers;
* **Cheap**: They can be largely powered by the wind (which is stronger and more consistent offshore), and cooled indirectly by the cold seawater.
* **Infinite scale:** No matter where you build in the world, the units are designed and built the same – only the anchoring system differs.
* **Easy Maintenance**: They can be serviced using robotics and existing fleet of offshore vessels and technicians;

**Product:**

Aikido’s product is AO60DC, which we build in farms of 10s-100s. Each platform is the size of a football field and supports:

* 5,000-6,000 GPUs (our first unit will have 78 x GB300 NVL72 racks);
* 15-18MW wind turbine, Hours of battery storage, backup power generation;
* Ultra-low PUE (<1.08);
* Fast and ultra-high bandwidth back to shore via existing subsea fiber;
* Onsite robotic inspection and maintenance (from our friends at Nines);
* On demand human access via vessel or helicopter in 1-4h;

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125245&key=user_uploads/523370/b1102cd6-d63c-4dd1-a473-9616921aa0be)

**Timeline:**

We started designing our first unit, _A1DC_, back in February; kicked off retrofit of the offshore platform in the US in June, received final permits for the platform in September and will be doing a test fit-up in November. 

We’ve already completed the first stage of the full-scale AO60DC design and will be kicking off the final design, with third-party certification, later this year. We will begin construction next Spring and the unit will hit the water late next year as we look for first customers to rent out the capacity.

**The Team’s Backstory:** 

Bingbin and Sam met back in 2014 at a company that helped build some of the world’s first floating offshore wind, with now 100MW+ in operation. They decided to leave to make offshore wind platforms that were better/cheaper/faster than conventional ones, which were just borrowed from O&G. So they left and joined Otherlab, where they met James, who brings a background in aerospace, designing and building helicopters. They founded Aikido in 2022 with the support of Breakthrough Energy Fellows program (happy to refer folks!) and pivoted from the energy space to the datacenter space in early 2025. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125245&key=user_uploads/523370/ee567cdc-4001-4320-8c62-b5122c3189c2)

The three of us with our first 1:250 scale prototype at a friend’s pool in 2022.

launches.title: Spacesheep 🐑: Documents of the future
launches.tagline: A new surface where people understand and work with AI.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, I'm Michael, the founder of [Spacesheep](https://spacesheep.dev) (F26).

## TL;DR

**Spacesheep: documents of the future.** Spaces are the place your teams and agents can be productive. Your AI makes the space; your team reads it, comments on it and builds on it.

Ask the AI you already use: "Use spacesheep.dev and give a visual explanation of how GPUs work." You get a document, a mockup, a dashboard, an app or art. Share it with specific people, your team, or publicly.

Our launch video:

<https://youtu.be/cFVCDSs-GZs>

Agents make our work more productive. Their output keeps growing, but our ability to read stays the same. We're building a new surface where people understand and work with AI.

Spacesheep in 90 seconds:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKQtOTrRBBA>

## Why we're building it

Agent use pushes productivity, but we get constantly burned out by relentless walls of AI-generated text. We don't believe a chat interface is the final evolution of human-computer interaction. Agents know how to shape information for humans, and that shape is not a wall of text. The full story: [spacesheep.dev/why](https://spacesheep.dev/why)

## What we built

If you can imagine it, you can sheep it. Information can take many more shapes than a page. With one prompt, create and share designs, styled documents, dashboards and vibe-coded apps your team and customers work in together.

### Dashboards and live data

Cited, charted, and kept current. Machines and services stream numbers straight into the space, like [a thermal camera on an AI chip's board](https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/thermal-master-p3-live-camera-stream) at 25 frames a second while GPU experiments run, or [an AI Foundry lab dashboard](https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/aifoundry-lab-dashboard).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/70f6f951-c043-4261-af2a-4379d7cfed7c)


### Investigations

Turn agent output into dashboards and stories people actually understand. For example, [YC by the numbers](https://spacesheep.dev/@misha/yc-by-the-numbers): we pointed an agent at YC's public directory, 6,305 startups over 21 years, and it came back as one story in six eras, from consumer web to agents and robots.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/74805160-58ea-40a9-b983-15b2d92b1491)


### Interactive designs

[An interactive map of the ET-SoC-1 chip](https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/et-soc1-chip-diagram) you can click through and comment on, from the whole chip down to a single vector unit. Each space is designed from scratch for what's in it. No templates.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/c7047d56-9b60-4933-a50c-97fe3927c356)


### Apps, CRMs and forms

Teams build their own internal apps, CRMs and forms, even games: for productivity, for fun, or for working with suppliers and customers. Everyone edits the same records, and there are no servers to run.

### Collaborate

Jump on a space with your team and your AI. Comment on the exact line. Write @spacesheep and the AI fixes the space while everyone watches. Every version is kept.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124256&key=user_uploads/836233/e1e00c9c-53c7-4a5b-873e-a8e58e31dba4)


This is how James Briggs uses it to stay in the loop while Claude Code writes his code: plans, code explainers and reviews he can actually read.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJVcc4O-7ck>

### Never lose a link

Ask in your own words and the space is there. State-of-the-art search, built by former Pinecone engineers.

### Use your AI. Or ours.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, Grok and open-source harnesses like opencode all publish to the same space. Or use Spacesheep's own AI on the dashboard, in Slack and more.

### Own your data

Your spaces are yours. Every space and every version syncs to your own Google Drive or GitHub, so you can read them anywhere, take them with you, and never depend on us to keep them.

## About me

Founder/CEO of Spacesheep (YC F26). Previously MTS at Anthropic, where I built the internal app deployment framework and the first version of CC Artifacts. Before that, staff engineer at Pinecone and Twitter.

## Our ask

* **Try it.** Ask your agent to "share this to spacesheep.dev" and send the link to your team.
* **Design partners.** Know an organization that wants to use Spacesheep? Introduce us.
* **Feedback:** [feedback@spacesheep.dev](mailto:feedback@spacesheep.dev) or [@micmakarov](https://x.com/micmakarov) on X
* **YC founders:** a year of the Team plan for up to 15 members. Redeem it on Bookface.

name: ChampionEffect Inc.
long_description:
ChampionEffect is an AI Coach that teaches AI to every employee at a company, in Slack and Teams.

The Coach helps with a new AI concept, a new workflow, or any tool. It jumps on a call and walks you through the work, just like a coworker would. It points to the top use cases in your industry and tailors everything to your company’s needs and tools. Every time someone does a walkthrough with the Coach, it learns how real work gets done at the company and uses that knowledge with other coworkers.

Before this, we ran a YC company (Cambly) that taught English to millions of professionals and generated $100M+ in revenue. Now we’re using what we learned to teach millions about AI.
